items.title: The Matron roams the whole tower, deck to deck
items.detail: She already hunts her deck (154 m), the stack decks under it (143, 132), the 176 ring, and the rings above it that she reaches by lines and the ladder in her Turn. The build order's next big step is still 'her reach up the tower band by band (XL)', and the owner's new rule is that there is no 'just her deck'.
items.source: 03_EXECUTION/ACTIVE_GOAL_PROGRESS.md, 'Handoff for the next session (2026-10-19, evening)' + night directives; 00_START_HERE.md 2026-10-19 night rows

items.title: A fun way to keep her at bay that does not kill her
items.detail: The owner's new rule is that the player is never helpless. Today the only counterplay is the rotten catwalk, which kills her, plus sneaking, lures and running. No deterrent that holds her off without killing her exists yet.

items.title: Her face: realistic, uncanny, adult-scary
items.detail: Her figure is built from primitives in matron_view.gd, and exposure only changes its colors (tunic, blisters, grey, bloodshot eyes, thinning hair). The owner wants a face that is as realistic as possible and deeply wrong: uncanny and adult-scary, not Halloween.
items.source: 03_EXECUTION/ACTIVE_GOAL_PROGRESS.md, Handoff night directives; 'Her look follows the exposure'

items.title: Her breathing and footfalls change by stage
items.detail: The music box already changes by stage. Her breathing and footfalls by stage are marked 'Not done' in goal item 2.

items.title: She wrecks your work: placed stock shoved off edges, machines reset or jammed
items.detail: The owner asked for this on 2026-10-19: she shoves the stock you placed off edges and resets or jams machines you set, more often the higher her stage. Today she only takes, throws and hoards stock and unhooks the cage rope.

items.title: Tune her rage numbers once she follows you up the tower
items.detail: Her rage gain, cooling and stage thresholds are CHOSEN placeholders, to be tuned once she follows up the tower (build order 2).
items.source: 03_EXECUTION/ACTIVE_GOAL_PROGRESS.md, 'The Matron's rage and her three stages'; Handoff item 3

items.title: Her shove while you hang from a ledge or hold a ladder
items.detail: A shove on a player who is hanging or on a ladder sets the body's speed against the hold, and this is untested. The note says a shove that breaks the grip is next.

items.title: Cage B with her, and cage C beyond it
items.detail: The rules for her unhooking and riding cage B at the 176 ring are written but cannot be reached in today's world. Cage B sits on the island of cages 1.09 m off the ring, and she only gets there by riding cage A up with the player.

items.title: She calls and rides lifts on her own
items.detail: Decision 9B says she can send a lift away or board the lift you called. Her hearing note says a lift she calls waits for one near her levels, because today's lifts are rigged and tripped by the player or are far below.

items.title: She rides a zipline trolley while frail; the riser from 143
items.detail: The kit already lets her ride a line's trolley while frail, but there is no case for it yet, because the trolley on her deck's line leaves with the player. The riser from 143 is judged the player's way, not hers.
items.source: 03_EXECUTION/ACTIVE_GOAL_PROGRESS.md, 'The Matron after a lead more than a level away'

items.title: The Matron hearing the forklift or the crane
items.detail: The hearing code exists, but it is not proven. The machines work at or below 58 m and she keeps to 154 m and up. This matters once she roams lower or the machines reach her levels.
items.source: 03_EXECUTION/ACTIVE_GOAL_PROGRESS.md, 'The machines heard from their parts, and the Matron's ears'

items.title: The Matron kept across a quit and reload
items.detail: Kept simple so far: a reload finds her asleep in the locker. That conflicts with her exposure only getting worse over the day, and with her being loose in the tower.
items.source: 03_EXECUTION/ACTIVE_GOAL_PROGRESS.md, 'The Matron: a released thing that hunts you' (Kept simple); rage entry

items.detail: The lines are captions until a person records them. The names (Navarro, Walt Brenner) are proposals kept in one table, waiting on the owner.

items.detail: The spine's arc for Walt Brenner after Act 1 is not written or built.

items.title: Locker wake, strain and burst
items.detail: She sleeps in a steel locker on the 154 m deck. A loud noise carried within 30 m wakes her, then comes 16 s of strain (gauge, lamp, knocks, dents, four bolts popping) before the door tears off into the shaft and she unfolds over 2.2 s.

items.title: A real 220 kg Jolt body that never teleports
items.detail: An upright 2.1 m capsule moved only by bounded foot acceleration. She hunts at 6.8 m/s (faster than the player's walk, slower than the sprint), brakes and cuts hard, and never steps off an edge (she plants her feet 0.25 m short of one).
items.source: src/sim/matron.hpp header and speeds; src/sim/matron.cpp walk_toward

items.title: Hearing through the whole tower
items.detail: Player noise (hard landing, sprint, walk, rungs, crouch creep, forklift) and world crashes (impacts, the yard crane) reach her by the shorter of two paths: straight through decks (10x the distance per deck) or around through the open shaft (1.4x per bend). A lead is placed on the level the sound came from.
items.source: src/sim/matron.cpp carry_m, decks_between, pick; src/sim/physics_world.cpp (hear feed); src/sim/physics_world_movement.cpp matron_loudness

items.title: Sight: 9 m close, 50 m across the shaft, own level only
items.detail: Two eye rays a head's width apart, so thin posts hide nobody. Sight works on her level, or up a ladder from it; long sight across the shaft only decides whether she commits to the catwalk.

items.title: 25 levels known, each a walking-line graph
items.detail: She knows the 154 m deck (catwalk, ladder foot, post at the first cage's mouth), the 176 ring (two cages, the leap gap, a post by the second cage), ten upper rings from 198 to 396 m, and thirteen stack decks from 11 to 143 m. Routes are Dijkstra over each level's lines, with a straight-line clearance check.

items.title: Up one ladder, 154 to 176, only in the Turn
items.detail: Seen or heard on the ladder, she guesses the player is at its head and goes to its foot. Frail, she only stares up it. In the Turn she climbs in jerks (0.6 m/s, 2.2 m/s bursts) and mantles onto the 176 ring.

items.title: Down a line on her forearms, only in the Turn
items.detail: Lines cross the shaft from each stack deck to the one below and from each upper ring to the one below. In the Turn she jumps from the stand for the bare cable, slides on her forearms (sparks, screech) and lets go over the far band. She only takes a line that has already been ridden.

items.title: Rides a cage she happened to step into
items.detail: If her floor moves faster than 0.3 m/s she clings to it, with no grab, step or Turn, until 1 s after it stops. She then hunts the level it stopped at. She never boards or calls a cage on purpose.

items.title: Vaults and gap leaps in the Turn
items.detail: In the Turn she vaults anything below her chest when there is floor beyond it, and leaps gaps up to 3 m (for example the open half of the first cage's mouth on the 176 ring). Frail, she crosses no gap wider than 0.45 m.

items.title: Her mind: guards, peers, learns, unrigs
items.detail: When she loses you she stands silent in the way up. A noise that fooled her makes her check the next one from a vantage. Fooled twice, far noises only turn her head. She takes your rope off a rigged cage's eye, and guesses where a ridden line or climbed ladder ends. Everything she learns is forgotten on a restore.
items.source: src/sim/matron.cpp pre_step (Guarding, Peering, Unrigging), stand_down; matron.hpp her mind

items.title: The Turn
items.detail: A 0.9 s wind-up (spine cracking, head turning the wrong way) is followed by a 3.2 s lunge in 9 m/s bursts with pauses. It is triggered by a clear line within 13 m or a hard landing heard within 20 m, and how soon it can come again depends on her stage (45 s as a pest, 18 s dangerous, 4 s fully changed).

items.title: Rage and three stages, moved by sound only
items.detail: Pest, Dangerous and Changed. Rage is fed only by sound level at her ear, plus spikes; it decays in quiet, has no floor over time, and uses separate up and down thresholds so it never flickers. No UI shows it; the player reads her.

items.title: Her hands by stage; running into her is never a death
items.detail: A pest shoves you away. Dangerous, she aims the shove at the shaft's rim when you are within 3 m of it. Fully changed, her catch kills. A full-speed collision with her body is not a death (native test 'matron collision', commit 0ccfbfc).
items.source: src/sim/matron.cpp shove_direction; src/sim/physics_world.cpp caught/shove block; git 0ccfbfc

items.title: Pest mischief: takes, throws or carries off your stock
items.detail: Light stock you have handled counts as yours to her. As a pest she picks it up within 5 m, throws it at you at 7.5 m/s from 2.5 to 6 m, or carries it to her post and drops it there. Only 3 throwable pieces exist, all on her deck's north band.
items.source: src/sim/matron.cpp fetch_stock, throw_stock, take_stock; src/sim/loose_stock.hpp kMatronThrowables

items.title: The rotten catwalk: the one thing that kills her
items.detail: Eleven bolted plates cross the shaft. Bolts shear above 2.1 kN averaged over 0.25 s, so they hold a climber but not her. She only steps onto it with her prey in plain sight ahead. Any fall of more than 12 m below her level also kills her.

items.title: Checkpoint freeze, and death puts her back in her locker
items.detail: While she is out and you are on her level, the checkpoint stops renewing so it cannot become a death loop. A death restores you, and her at her locker on the 154 m deck, with rage, stage and exposure kept and everything she learned forgotten.

items.title: Look changes with exposure
items.detail: Over 600 s out: pale skin and a white tunic, then blistered skin, a stained tunic and bloodshot eyes, then grey skin, filth and thinning hair. The change only goes one way.

items.title: Figure built from code primitives, with many poses
items.detail: Lofted tubes, blobs and ribbons with noise-triplanar cloth and skin: a stooped first-aid attendant with arms to her knees, hooked four-finger hands, rags, and a music box at her hip. Poses include the shuffle, an all-fours scuttle with dropped frames, searching with a hand at her ear, standing guard, peering, unrigging, clinging, climbing, hanging from a cable, carrying and throwing. In the Turn her spine twists, her neck goes backward, elbows and a knee reverse, and her limbs stretch.

items.title: Her face as it stands
items.detail: A 26x32 sphere pushed into shape by 15 Gaussian blobs (brow, sockets, hollow cheeks, hooked nose, pointed chin), with a split jaw that opens on a dark mouth, 18 uneven teeth, ball eyes with amber glowing irises plus an omni light, eye bags, ears, a headscarf blob and ribbon hair. The head turns to track the player. There are no eyelids, blinks, eye movement, lips, wrinkles or skin shading.

items.title: Her sounds, all synthesized in code
items.detail: Locker knocks, bolt pops, the burst, a music box (heard far off, slowing as she nears, fast when dangerous, warped in the Turn or fully changed, silent at her post), breath, steps, shrieks (on sight, Turn, throw, leap, climb, fall), bone cracks, rung clangs, cable screech, shackle rattle and plank crack.

items.title: Proof: native and touch tests
items.detail: Native tests: matron, matron-collision and matron-mischief. touch_matron plays her from the deck's start, touch_matron_act plays her first act from 154 m to 220 m by touch with a capture at each stage, and look_matron_gallery renders her looks.

items.title: She cannot go up past the 176 ring
items.detail: Her only active way up is the single ladder from 154 to 176, taken only in the Turn. The 176-198-220 climbing route (boards, standpipe, catwalk, scaffold) is explicitly 'where she cannot follow' in the act test. On the rings from 198 to 396 m and on the stack decks she has no way up at all. Owner directive 2026-10-19 night: no 'just her deck', she moves up and down.
items.source: src/sim/matron.cpp constructor (climbs_ has one entry; upper levels way=-1); ui_test_act.gd header; 00_START_HERE.md directives

items.title: No deliberate use of machines (cages, lifts, swing, mast)
items.detail: She only rides a cage she was standing in as it left. She never boards, calls or works one, and never rides the float lift, swing, cascade mast or the other lifts the player uses, so riding a machine always shakes her off.

items.title: Going down is narrow, and any long drop kills her
items.detail: Down is only by a line, only in the Turn, and only a line already ridden. The riser ladder from 143 is not taken from the top. Any fall more than 12 m below her level kills her, so she cannot drop through the shaft or off a ring.

items.title: Tied to her home deck: locker, post, catwalk, restore
items.detail: A restore always returns her to her locker on the 154 m deck (level 0). Her posts, unrigging, catwalk, stock and the checkpoint-freeze logic all assume her deck. Once she roams, someone has to decide where she reappears after a death without creating a death loop, and whether she gets a post on each level.
items.source: src/sim/matron.cpp restore (level_=0, spawn at locker); matron.hpp freezes_checkpoint

items.title: No sight up or down the open shaft
items.detail: She sees only on her own level. She cannot see you a deck above or below across the open well, so a strong moment is unused: her staring up at you through the shaft from three decks down and then starting toward the way up.

items.title: Upper rings and stack decks are bare loops; nothing above 396 m
items.detail: The upper rings are a plain square loop each, and the stack decks copy her deck's band loop. They have no posts, ways up, props or stock for her. The tower above 396 m (TP-340, 484, 640, 750, 800 m) is not among her levels at all.

items.title: A fun, non-lethal way to keep her at bay
items.detail: Not built. Today the player can creep quietly, make decoy crashes by shoving crates, out-sprint her (which is loud), ride away, re-rig a cage, or drop her through the catwalk (which kills her). The owner's 2026-10-16 idea of boxes, beams and containers to use against her was deferred. Because she hunts by sound, something that floods or stuns her hearing, or physically pushes her 220 kg body back, would fit.

items.title: Realistic, uncanny, adult-scary face
items.detail: The blob-sculpted sphere is far from realistic, and the amber glowing irises read as Halloween. It needs a high-detail head mesh, skin with subsurface shading on the phone renderer, pore, wrinkle and radiation-burn detail that follows exposure, wet eyes with lids that blink wrong and track you, and small facial movements beyond opening the jaw.

items.title: A body realistic enough to match a realistic face
items.detail: The body is lofted primitives on rigid pivots, with noise textures, no skinning, no cloth simulation and four-finger hands. A realistic face on this body would itself look wrong in a cheap way, so the figure needs to come up to the same level.

items.title: Her voice is synthesized, not a recorded person
items.detail: Her shriek and breath are made from tones and noise in code. The owner's rule is 'machines make sounds; only people have voices', so her voice needs real recordings (breath, whimpers, humming the music-box tune, the first-aider's soothing words gone wrong). The source and licensing need a decision.

items.title: Breathing and footfalls by stage
items.detail: The music box already tells her stage. Her breathing and footfalls do not change with stage yet; this is the handoff's goal item 2, still open.

items.title: Higher-stage mischief: shoving placed stock off edges, jamming machines
items.detail: Asked for by the owner on 2026-10-19: she shoves stock you placed off edges, and resets or jams machines you set, more of it the higher her stage. Today mischief happens only as a pest.

items.title: Stock for her across the tower
items.detail: Only 3 throwable pieces exist, all by her deck's north rail, plus seven pieces of loose stock on her deck. A roaming Matron needs things to take, throw and knock about on every level she reaches. The owner said to add stock freely.

items.title: Rage numbers are placeholders, untuned
items.detail: The gain, spike and decay rates and the stage thresholds were picked as a starting point and are to be tuned once she follows the player up the tower.

items.title: No felt presence beyond sound: haptics, camera, light
items.detail: Nothing in haptics or the camera reacts to her (only the general hit feedback on a shove), and lights don't fail or flicker as she nears. Her presence is carried by sound and sight alone, which falls short of the owner's 'engulfed and immersed'.
items.source: grep of godot/presentation (main_feel.gd only calls matron_view.update_view)

items.title: She is not saved across quit and reload
items.detail: Reloading starts her asleep in her locker again. This was a deliberate simplification ('kept simple'), and it matters more once she roams and changes over a long run.

result.notes: The main finding: she knows 25 levels (11 to 396 m) and can hear through all of them, but in practice she is held to the 154 m deck and the 176 ring. Her one way up is a single ladder, taken only in the Turn, plus a cage she happens to be standing in. Her one way down is a line someone has already ridden, again only in the Turn. A fall of more than 12 m kills her, and a restore always puts her back in her locker. So 'move up and down the tower' is mostly new work, not tuning: deliberate cage and lift use, climbing the parkour routes, surviving drops, levels above 396 m, sight across the shaft, and a restore rule that works away from her home deck. Her face and voice are fully procedural (a blob-sculpted sphere with amber glowing eyes; a shriek and breath made in code), which is far from the realistic, adult-scary face asked for and conflicts with the 'only people have voices' rule. No non-lethal way to keep her at bay exists yet. HEAD moved from ee8fa5c to 0ccfbfc during this survey (the 'collision is never a death' test); its CI run is in progress, and the mischief commit 8b5b95e's CI failed.

What is done: the story's Act 1 core from 154 to 220 m. That covers her rage and stages, her look by exposure, the music box by stage, her hands by stage, a pest's mischief, the radio's first four lines, and the touch playthrough of her first act.

What is not started: everything above the 220 ring. That includes her reach beyond her deck area, the crew, the harpoon, the X-ray room, the scaffold, the cloud break, the last beam and topping out, night lighting above the Stack, and the badge-in opening.

The owner's new directives from tonight are added as items because they belong in the plan, although the doc predates them: she roams deck to deck, a non-lethal way to keep her at bay, and a realistic, uncanny face.

The doc's morning snapshot lists three workflow scripts that were drafted and never run (Feel It, Break the Route, The Hunt Goes Up). It says the story supersedes them.

Status calls rest on code greps. No code mentions badge-in, a gate log, hard hat props, the harpoon, a helmet lamp, an X-ray room, a last beam or credits. Ten machines still start on a hanging handle: E and F (src/sim/band_wet_isolation.cpp), G, H and I (band_plate_shop.cpp), J, K and L (band_facade_crane.cpp), and M and O (band_midstack_service.cpp). Her levels and climbs are set up in src/sim/matron.cpp, roughly lines 60 to 112.

items.title: Wow-factor first: every new piece should be extraordinary and stunning
items.detail: From now on the work should aim for true wow-factor experiences, since the game is deep enough for the stunning stuff. This is written down as the top directive, but nothing stunning has been built under it yet.

items.title: Make the player physically feel the climb, immersed and engulfed
items.detail: This is a one-of-a-kind physics experience, and the person playing should feel the weight, impacts and danger in their body and be pulled into it. That means camera, body response, sound and touch feedback working together. No dedicated work has been done on this yet.

items.title: The Matron moves from deck to deck, up and down the whole tower
items.detail: There should be no 'just her deck'. She has to be able to follow and roam up and down. Today she cannot follow past her ladder to the 220 m ring. The handoff lists 'her reach up the tower band by band' as the next big build.
items.source: Owner, 2026-10-19 night; 00_START_HERE.md row 2 ('to build'); ACTIVE_GOAL_PROGRESS.md handoff entry

items.title: A fun, non-lethal way for the player to keep her at bay
items.detail: The player must never be helpless against her. They need something fun that holds her off or drives her back without killing her. It is not designed or built yet. The latest commit (bumping into her is never a death) does not cover this.

items.title: Her face: as realistic as possible, uncanny, adult-scary
items.detail: Her face should look as close to a real human face as possible, with all the scary cosmetics, so it lands in a deeply unsettling uncanny-valley place. It should be adult horror, not childish Halloween scary. Right now her figure in godot/presentation/life/matron_view.gd is built from simple shapes.

items.detail: Claude may add loose stock, props and dressing wherever they make the world richer and more physical. Nothing new has been added since this permission was given.

items.title: Help develop the game: propose and build, not just carry out orders
items.detail: The owner wants Claude acting as a co-developer, bringing ideas and content, not only doing what is listed.

items.title: Iterate and prototype quickly with every tool available
items.detail: Use anything clever to try ideas fast: the Godot tool, captures, throwaway scenarios, parallel agents. Applies to all coming work.

items.detail: A standing rule. Speed must not cost quality. Use everything at hand to reach the strongest version. It is written down as in force.

result.name: She Knows the Steel: the Matron anywhere in the tower
result.pitch: After her first act, you never again know which floor she is on. You only know how she is coming, and you always hear it first. Every ladder you climbed, every lift you rode and every line you slid is hers too. So are the four service risers in the corners of the shaft, which you cannot grip and she can. Once she is fully changed, the columns and braces on the outside of the tower are hers as well. The simulation finds all of these ways in the steel itself, so she arrives somewhere real, at a speed you could time, after a sound that told you first. You feel her in the phone when she is on the steel you are standing on. You can stand at the top and let a drum fall on her, and she goes screeching down to the next flange. She comes back angrier, and by a different way.
mechanics: HER MAP, BAKED FROM THE STEEL. The native test binary gets a bake mode (SCRAPERX_ONLY=matron-map-bake). It builds the whole world at rest and writes the generated file src/sim/matron_map.inc. This follows the same pattern as world_solids.inc, which solid_export.gd generates and CI checks for drift. Steps: (1) Floors. Over a 0.5 m grid covering the tower's footprint and every band's extents, cast one all-hits ray down from 810 m. Every upward-facing hit on a static body, or on a kit body at rest, is a candidate floor. It is kept only where her capsule fits with 2.1 m of headroom and the floor is at least 0.48 m across, the rule walk_toward already applies (kFootSpanM). (2) Levels. Cells are grouped by height (within 0.3 m) and by touching, so each patch is one level: a deck band, a ring, a cage floor, a machine deck. (3) Walk lines. Each patch is thinned to its middle line, with nodes at corners and junctions. On a 9 m Stack band that gives the x = 21.5 line she walks today. (4) Links, by type (next item). (5) Proof. A headless Matron is sent across every candidate link inside the bake, and any that fail are dropped and listed. The output is roughly 40 levels, 700 nodes and 200 links: a few tens of KB of constants. Hand-written overlays stay as they are: her posts, the cages' eyes, the rotten catwalk.

THE WAYS SHE KNOWS (link types, all found in the geometry). LADDERS: stacks of rungs that pass box_is_hold (no thicker than kGripMaxSection, 0.18 m), spaced no more than 0.45 m apart, with a foot within reach of a floor and a head within 1.2 m of one. This finds the 154 to 176 ladder, C2's wall ladder through deck 7's equipment hatch, the davit ladders, and C3's wall ladder and riser ladder from 143 to 154. CORNER RISERS: the four service risers in world_solids.inc (x +-15.8, z -134.2 / -165.8; a 0.7 m pipe from grade to 154 m, with a 1.1 m flange 1.4 m under each deck). In general, any vertical member 0.3 to 1.8 m across that passes within reach of two floors' edges. The bake's capsule sweep puts her line wedged into the corner between the pipe and the shaft's corner, about 0.65 m from the pipe's axis and 0.19 m clear of both edge beams. That is right under the spot where each band's two shaft rails meet. The player cannot grip a 0.7 m pipe, so the risers are hers alone. OUTSIDE STEEL: the Stack's perimeter columns (1.6 m square at x +-26 and 0, z -124 / -150 / -176), the ring corner columns above 154, and the rings' 0.4 m chevron braces at about 23 degrees, which she crawls. Every deck or ring edge she passes is a stop. LINES: the lines across the well from every deck and ring to the one below (Zipline::lines(), already built for every level), taken on her forearms as today. RIDES: every kit guide's cage, and every vertical::Machine with walkable Ports, linking the levels at each end of its travel. DROPS AND PULL-UPS: a floor's edge with another floor below within her drop, or above within her reach. For a hang-drop she hangs by her hands with 2.6 m of her below them. Every link records its STOPS: the floor edges, flanges and ladder feet along it that would catch her. The bake refuses any link with more than 11.5 m between stops. That is under kFallenBelowM (12 m), which is what guarantees a knock-down never kills her.

HER STAGE DECIDES HOW SHE MOVES, NOT WHETHER. The owner said she must move up and down, so a bake test proves every level can be reached from every other at every stage. The stage changes how she does it and which links she uses. PEST: ladders and corner risers feet first, slowly (0.4 m/s on a riser, CHOSEN), resting at each flange with a breath. She rides lifts. She never uses the outside steel or the cable, and never drops more than 1.2 m: a slow old woman in the pipes. DANGEROUS: steady on links (0.8 m/s), she slides the cable after you, and hang-drops up to 3 m. FULLY CHANGED: the outside of the tower is hers. She goes head first down risers and columns, hang-drops up to 6.5 m, and climbs in kClimbBurstMps jerks with stalls between; the Turn can come on any link. Today a frail Matron stands at a ladder's foot and gives up (follow_climb); that ends. Fun turns to horror in space: as she gets worse, more of the building becomes hers.

HOW SHE KNOWS YOU ARE ON ANOTHER LEVEL. HEARING stays as built (carry_m: ten times the distance for each deck between, 1.4 times for each bend round the shaft) and now works across all of the map's levels. SIGHT ACROSS LEVELS: today she only sees you on her own level or up her one ladder (pre_step's `perceivable`). Now the same two-ray sees() reaches through the open shaft and past the outer edge, up to 45 m (CHOSEN). Within 9 m it is checked every tick; farther out, every 9th tick on a fixed phase (10 Hz). THE SHAFT LOOK: while searching, she walks to the nearest shaft rail and looks up for 2.5 s, then down for 2.5 s. That is where she spots you, and where you look over the rail and see her face. THE STEEL CARRIES BOTH WAYS: if the player's hands are on her link (within 0.6 m of its line), she knows exactly where they are, just as the player feels her. RIDES AND LINES GIVE YOU AWAY: a lift you ride or a line you slide becomes a lead at its far end. This generalizes today's guess_line_ and guess_climb_.

HOW SHE CHOOSES A WAY. When her lead changes level, she plans over the whole map: a shortest-path search over link ends (no more than about 500 nodes). The cost is walking metres over her stage's speed, plus each link's time, plus penalties. She keeps the plan at least 3 s unless the lead's level changes. INTERCEPT: with the player on a link, she heads for its far end; if she gets there first, she waits at its head, still and silent (her Guarding, with the head as the post). You climb toward a face looking down at you. WATCHED LINK: a link whose head the player stands within 3 m of costs 25 s more (CHOSEN). She stops at the ladder's foot, looks up at you, and walks off toward the corner riser. You watch her decide. SPOILED LINK: a link she was knocked off is left out of her plans for 30 s. VARIETY WITHOUT RANDOMNESS: costs within 10% of each other are broken by a hash of (link index, lead level, tick / 900). She is not always at the same corner, but a replay is identical. LOST: she searches the lead's level, does a shaft look, then drifts one level toward the last loud sound. She never moves toward you without a path.

THE TELL, THEN THE ARRIVAL (second by second). The contract with the player: before she stands on your level, there are always at least 4 s of her link's sound (CHOSEN, and tested). Each link has its own signature, all of them structure or machine sounds placed in 3D at her hands. LADDER: a bright clang per rung (built). CORNER RISER: a hollow knock per handhold, a deeper bong as she passes each flange, and the pipe ringing on after. OUTSIDE COLUMN: palm slaps, a long creak, wind round her. CABLE: her forearms screeching (built). RIDE: the machine's own sounds, and her breath close by. DROP: a landing that booms through the deck, fed into the impact ledger so it is one system with every other hit. MANTLE: fingers scraping the edge beam, then one palm slapped flat on the deck, then her head. The rhythm shows her stage: as a pest, a knock every 1.2 s and a rest with a breath at each flange; fully changed, three quick knocks and then silence. YOU HEAR HER AS SHE HEARS YOU: pre_step already computes player_carry (how far your noise carries to her ear) every tick. The native exports it with the number of decks between, and the view muffles and quiets her music box, breath and knocks by exactly that, so 'two decks below you' sounds like it. Nothing appears on the HUD.

YOU FEEL HER IN THE STEEL. A new haptic kind, &"her", goes through main_feel.gd's _haptic. When she is on the same link the player is on or holding (the same ladder, the same riser corner, the column at your corner), each of her handholds is a pulse in the phone. It gets stronger as she nears, and fades to nothing beyond 12 m along the link. Her landing on your floor within 15 m is one heavy pulse. It is counted in haptic_counts like every other kind, so CI can check it.

SEEN DOING IT: the poses that make the gasps, added to matron_view.gd's _pose. Her hand comes first over every edge: 0.6 s of fingers curling over the edge beam before her head appears. The shaft look: her head tipped back past straight up, jaw slack, her face lit by the deck's work lamp. As a pest she goes feet first and rests at the flanges; fully changed she goes head first, spidering. On the corner riser she is wedged in with her knees up. Her figure is drawn on any level, up to DRAW_RANGE_M (140 m).

KEEPING HER AT BAY: KNOCK HER DOWN A STOREY. It cannot kill her, by construction. While she is on a link (climbing, hanging or mantling), a hit that changes her speed by more than 1.4 m/s in one tick tears her hands off. That is about 300 N s on her 220 kg: a 55 kg drum or the 50 kg iron pig let go from a storey above does it; a thrown 18 kg toolbox does not. She slides down her link with her drag on it to the next stop (the flange below, the ladder's foot, the deck edge under her on a column), catches with a crash and a shriek, hangs stunned for 2.5 s, and that link is spoiled for her for 30 s. Every knock adds 0.08 to her rage (CHOSEN), so each one buys you time and makes her worse. The corner riser's line, right under the corner where the rails meet, is exactly where something let go over the rail falls on her. Stops no more than 11.5 m apart mean she never falls past kFallenBelowM. DENYING A WAY (new stock): hinged steel hatch lids on deck 7's equipment hatch and on the new ring ladders' landings. A hatch or ladder head with 150 kg or more on it (CHOSEN, what she can lift from below) is closed to her for as long as the weight stays. She pounds on it, and then goes another way. Her pest mischief already shoves stock off edges from above, so the same weight works both ways.

HER WEIGHT IS REAL. She is a 220 kg Jolt body, and every lift was balanced for one rider. On Stage A, the 800 kg skip still lifts the 350 kg cage with a rider and her, but with 150 kg of margin left instead of 370. A test table rides every lift with her aboard and records what it does, under the rule that nothing strands: a machine she rides must come back as found. Rule 11 says machines are started by the body, so a body can start them: her weight on S1's scale plate, her feet shoving S2's shoot bolt (her 9 m/s/s on 220 kg is about 2 kN against its 900 N shoes). She starts one only once she has seen or heard the player start it this run (Decision 9's C), and a restore makes her forget. The lift you sent away comes back with her in it.

CHECKPOINT: HER LAST FOOTING. Today a restore puts her back at her locker on the 154 m deck (Matron::restore sets level_ to 0 and respawns her). Instead, the checkpoint keeps her last footing on a floor of her map: level, x, z and yaw, plus her state, stage, rage and exposure. It is only renewed while her planned time to reach the player is over 20 s (CHOSEN), which replaces freezes_checkpoint's 'player on her deck' rule. A death puts you back where you last stood and her back where she last stood, far enough away by construction, and she keeps hunting the level she was on. Simulation::save_game carries the same. save_format_key changes, so older saves are refused cleanly. A restore still makes her forget what she learned this run, as it does now.

CHEAP AND DETERMINISTIC ON A PHONE. The map is compiled-in constants: nothing is generated at startup. Each tick she costs her existing walk rays, at most 2 sight rays, plus 2 more at 10 Hz for distant sight. She plans only when her lead changes. Her level comes from the baked floor heights, not from rays. route_toward copies her level's nodes and edges into new vectors on every call, an allocation every tick today; it moves to a fixed scratch buffer. Only simulation state decides anything, and ties break by index. Budget: her pre_step averages at most 0.15 ms on the host, measured in the reach test, then checked on the phone with the Godot profiler.

Fairness. If every way is hers, deaths can feel cheap. Three guards are tested: the 4 s tell before every arrival, 'no lead, no plan', and the 20 s rule for checkpoints, which prevents deaths on arrival.

Breaking the built first act. A pest now climbs, where today she gives up at the ladder's foot. touch_matron_act's beat ('quietly to her ladder and up it; in her Turn she comes up after') and several native sections must be revised on purpose, not patched to pass.
Her 220 kg on lifts balanced for one rider may stall one, or break a proven contract. The ride table in milestone 5 may force counterweight retunes, each proven again.

result.wow: On deck 12 you lean over the shaft rail to see whether she followed you up. Three decks down, a pale face is already tipped back past where a neck should go, looking straight at you. She walks into the corner and wraps herself round the north-east riser. The pipe starts to knock under her hands, one hollow bong a second, rising, and the phone in your palm pulses with each one, because she is on the steel you are standing beside. You have about half a minute, and the drum by your feet is the only thing heavy enough.

result.name: Her Tower: the Matron as the tower's other climber
result.pitch: The Matron is no longer the monster of the 154 m deck. She becomes the tower's other climber: a 220 kg body that uses the steel you use (ladders, lines, lifts) and steel you can't (the four riser pipes in the shaft corners, the diagonal braces on the outside of the faces). You hear her two decks down through the open shaft. You lean over the rail and see her shinning up a pipe toward you, or hear the long shriek of skin on steel as she slides a storey in four seconds and slams onto the flange under your deck. You climb a ladder to get away and she is waiting at the top, because she took the outside steel and it was faster. Every move she makes is physics: her hands carry her real weight on real holds with a finite grip. That means a drum you shove over the rail tears her off the pipe and drops her a storey, alive and stunned, and then she looks up and starts climbing again. Her map is read from the tower's own collision, so wherever the tower goes, she can follow.
mechanics: THE TOWER READ (her map, generated, not written by hand). A native bake runs over the fully built world (static bodies plus the kit's static route bodies) and writes a generated table, src/sim/matron_nav.inc. It is kept honest the way world_solids.inc is: a test rebakes and CI fails on drift. The bake region is the tower footprint (x -34..34, z -185..-112) plus each machine frame's bounds grown by 3 m, so tree trunks, lamp masts and the yard stay out. It produces three things. (1) SHEETS: downward all-hit rays on a 0.25 m lattice find up-facing static tops with 2.15 m of headroom. Neighbors within a 0.36 m rise flood-fill into sheets: the 14 stack decks, the 11 rings, TP-340, the 418, 640, 662 to 750 decks, C3's walkway, the 155.18 bridge (which merges into deck 14 by its 0.33 m steps), and catwalks. Each sheet is stored as 0.5 m cells. A cell is standable only where floor lies under her middle and 0.3 m to each side (so the 0.3 m scaffold boards are no floor to her, as today). Each cell also records which of its eight neighbors she can walk to, blocked by a hip or chest ray against a rail, post or column. Storage is run-length rows, about 60 KB for the tower. (2) MEMBERS: static leaf boxes sorted by the player's own box_is_hold test and by shape. Rung columns are horizontal holds no thicker than 0.18 m and no longer than 2.2 m, stacked at a pitch of 0.45 m or less: every ladder and the scaffold panel. Poles are vertical, 0.08 to 0.8 m thick: the four risers, the 0.1 m standpipe. Braces are tilted 15 to 75 degrees and 0.2 to 0.6 m thick: 112 StackBraces at 59 degrees and 96 UpperBraces at 24 degrees. Joints are where two member axes pass within 0.6 m of each other. Each member's usable span is swept with her capsule at hugging offset, and the span is cut wherever it hits something. (3) LINKS: typed edges between two sheet cells, or between a sheet cell and a member station. Each has a cost in her seconds per stage and a stage mask. Drops and haul-ups come from edge cells whose outside neighbor has standable floor on another sheet below or above within reach. Gaps come from edge-cell pairs up to 3.0 m apart within 0.8 m of the same height. At runtime the world adds the links that move: lines (Zipline::lines(), one-way down), rides (Kit guides with a vertical axis and 3 m or more of travel, plus vertical::Route decks, open only while the deck stands at her end), and the catwalk (its plates are dynamic, so it keeps its current sight-commit rule).

HER LINKS AND HER PHYSICS ON EACH (all numbers CHOSEN, to tune). Walk and step: up to 0.36 m. Haul-up onto a ledge: 1.0 m as a pest, 1.9 m dangerous, 2.5 m fully changed (the height her hands reach). Drop: 1.2, 3.0 or 6.0 m by stage. She lands on her feet and is stunned 0.15 s for each m/s over 5. Gap leap: up to 3.0 m, in the Turn or fully changed (today's kLeapReachM). Ladder: up and down at 0.3 m/s as a pest (new: frail, rung by rung, resting), 0.6 dangerous (today's kClimbMps), 0.8 changed, with 2.2 m/s jerks in the Turn (kClimbBurstMps). Riser or pole down: a governed slide at 3.0 m/s at every stage, with her rests at the flanges 1.4 m under each deck. Up: shinning at 0.45 m/s dangerous and 0.7 changed, 2.0 in Turn bursts. Getting on and off a riser means going over the 1.05 m shaft rail: a haul from the flange, 2.3 m to the rail's top, so dangerous or worse. The outside steel (braces): fully changed only, 0.7 m/s up along the member, 1.2 m/s down, 2.0 in Turn bursts. A StackBrace passes each deck's edge at its middle, so from any stack deck there is a brace on each face one storey up or down. Line: today's rules (in the Turn, on the bare cable, never down a parked line). Ride: today's clinging (kRideMps, kLetGoSeconds). Hatch: a hinged kit plate (the level-7 east band hatch today, more later). Her push on it is bounded at 2,500 N, so a shut hatch the player has weighted down holds her under it. Getting from walking onto a link, and back off it, is a transfer: her body is driven to the attach pose at no more than 12 m/s² with collisions on. A transfer that has not finished in 2 s is abandoned and she replans. Nothing sets her position except a checkpoint restore, the one exception Law 21 allows (the same as for the player).

THE HOLD (one physical primitive for ladders, poles, braces and ledges). This replaces climb()'s SetGravityFactor(0) and SetLinearVelocity. A Jolt SliderConstraint joins her body to the hold: Body::sFixedToWorld for static steel, or the kit body itself when the hold is dynamic and weighs at least kGripMinBodyMassKg 400. The slider axis is the member's axis. Gravity stays on. A velocity motor drives her along the member at her stage speed, and its force limit is her pull: 3,400 N up, 1.6 times her 2,158 N weight. Down, the limit is her squeeze: 3,000 N. A 120 kg drum riding on her stalls her climb. A dynamic hold carries her real weight, so the structure feels her. Her capsule's translation-only axes give the slider's rotation part zero inertia on both sides, so Jolt's RotationEulerConstraintPart Deactivate()s that part (SetInversed3x3 fails): checked in Jolt's source. Her grip is read every tick from GetTotalLambdaPosition()/dt. Over kHerGripN 5,500 N for 2 ticks, or kHerGripTearNs 450 per blow, her hands open. That is 1.2 times the player's kLedgeGripMaxForceN 4,500 and kLedgeGripTearImpulseNs 350 (CHOSEN). In the Turn her grip is 1.5 times stronger. A flange or a ladder's head is a hard limit on the slider, never counted against her grip.

KNOCKED OFF, NEVER KILLED BY IT (the physics behind keeping her at bay). A 15 kg toolbox thrown at 7.5 m/s (about 150 Ns) leaves her on. A 25 kg bar dropped a storey is borderline. A 200 kg oil drum shoved over the rail from 4 m above (about 1,800 Ns) tears her off. On a pole her legs stay wrapped when her hands open: she slips down on 1,200 N of leg squeeze, which is under her weight (4.4 m/s² down), until the next flange stops the wrap. That is about 9.8 m/s after a storey: a slam, a stun of 0.25 s for each m/s over 5, and she is alive. On a ladder or a brace she falls free. Her regrip reflex catches any rung row, deck edge or flange she passes within reach while she is falling slower than kRegripMps 10 m/s. Otherwise she lands on the floor below, which a ladder's foot always is, and she is stunned. The bake marks member spans with only open shaft under them (nothing to catch). Only a fall there, or today's catwalk, is her death (kFallenBelowM stays the last word).

HER WEIGHT IN THE WORLD. She is a real 220 kg body everywhere. In a counter-mass lift she is part of the balance: S1's bucket fills until it outweighs the cage with both riders in it, and Stage A's skip lift may not rise with her aboard. A 'ride with her' row is added to each lift's test matrix, and no lift may be left with no way to fix it or go on (rule 5). Bolts and plates she stands on shear by their real load (today's catwalk). Her hold force is published, so the steel groans in proportion to what she actually puts on it.

CHOOSING THE WAY (deterministic, cheap). An abstract graph: nodes are the link endpoints (about 1,400 for about 100 sheets and 700 links). Edges are her walk time between endpoints on one sheet (baked all-pairs), plus each link's cost in seconds at her current stage's speeds, with links her stage cannot take left out. A route is Dijkstra on that graph from her cell to the lead's cell (one BFS distance field on each of the two sheets), then A* with octile costs over her own sheet's grid (6,200 cells at most) to the next endpoint, smoothed by the baked passability. Ties always go to the lower node index. She replans every 45 ticks (0.5 s, a fixed phase of the tick count), when her lead changes sheet, when a ride's deck leaves her end, or when a link fails. Once she is on a hold she finishes it, unless turning back costs under 60% of going on. How far she will go depends on her stage. A pest gives up on a route costing more than 90 s and searches her own sheet (and does her mischief). Dangerous, she pursues up to three sheets away. Fully changed, she pursues anywhere and takes the outside steel. This keeps the owner's rule that a silent climber leaves her a pest.

HER SENSES ACROSS LEVELS. Hearing stays carry_m(). decks_between() counts static up-facing hits against baked sheet heights instead of levels_, so every level muffles at kDeckMuffle 10, and the way round through the open shaft (kBendMuffle 1.4) still carries. New, for heavy hits only (ImpactLedger hits on static or heavy bodies, never footsteps): a third path through the frame, the horizontal distance plus the vertical distance times kFrameMuffle 2.0 (CHOSEN). A beam dropped on the deck under hers is felt in the columns. One dropped three decks down is not. Sight across levels uses today's two-ray sees(), now with no same-level gate, so the real geometry decides: decks block and the open shaft does not. Beyond kSightM 9 m the far test runs every third tick, out to kCommitSightM 50 m (the shaft's diagonal plus two decks). Leads go to the sheet under the sound: the highest standable cell at (x, z) no more than 0.3 m above the sound and within 3 m below it. A sound in the air on a link (a ladder, a line, a riser) makes that link the lead, and her guess is its far end, generalizing guess_line_ and guess_climb_.

TRAIL, CUT-OFF, GUARD. The world remembers where you went, and she reads it the way a person would, by seeing it. A line with no trolley at its top (Line::parked false), a cage at the other end of its travel, or a rope rigged on an eye, seen within kSightM as she passes its foot, becomes a lead to its far end. A quiet climber is followed slowly, never forgotten. Cut-off, dangerous and up: when she perceives the player on a link heading for sheet S, she compares her route cost to its head with the player's time left on the link (the length left over their speed on it). If hers is no more than 3 s longer, she goes to the head and waits there silently, facing down it. Guarding generalizes today's posts: the baked heads and feet of the player's route links (kit route entities and machine cages) are posts. On her sheet she guards the one whose far end is nearest the player's last lead. Undoing the rigging on the well's A and B cages is kept as it is.

CHEAP ON A PHONE. Baked lookups replace walk_toward()'s edge_at()/floor_at() rays on static floors. Today those are 3 rays times 4 samples per check, and several checks a tick: up to about 70 rays. Rays stay only on dynamic floors (a cage) and for the one floor ray in feel_floor(). Sight costs at most 2 rays a tick, gated as above. carry_m() checks only the 4 sounds nearest in a straight line out of kMaxSounds 16. A hold costs one constraint read. A replan (Dijkstra on 1,400 nodes plus grid A* on one sheet) runs at most every 0.5 s. Budget: a mean of 60 µs or less per tick on the CI host, and 0.2 ms or less on the phone, measured by a perf test.

DETERMINISM. The bake is a pure function of the built world, frozen into constexpr tables. At runtime everything is integer-indexed with fixed evaluation order and index tie-breaks. The replan cadence is set by the tick count. No clock, no randomness: the Turn stays state-driven. The native determinism test runs a tower chase twice and requires identical bits.

CHECKPOINT AND SAVE WITH HER ANYWHERE. Matron::Saved gains her last firm footing (x, y, z and sheet), her state, her lead (sheet, x, z, seen or heard), and the stage, rage, exposure and handled stock it already has. freezes_checkpoint() changes from player_on_deck_ to: she sees the player, or her route cost to the player's footing is under kFreezeSeconds 20 s. Every commit therefore has her at least 20 s of route away, and a death never restores her within reach. restore() puts her at her saved footing, never on a hold (a commit made mid-ladder saves the foot she climbed from). What she learned is forgotten, as today. On disk, write_save()/read_save() append an optional trailing block after the grips (the same pattern the grips used). A save without it loads her sealed, as built, as every load does today.

WHAT THE PRESENTATION GETS (so she is readable). MatronSnapshot gains link_kind (walk, ladder, pole, brace, line, ride, drop, haul, leap, transfer), link_progress, hold_load (0..1 of her grip), slide_mps, slam_mps, stun_s and sheet_y. From these, matron_view.gd poses the pipe wrap and slide, the brace crawl, the haul over the rail, the drop and crouch, the knock-loose flail and the wrong-limbed stand-up. Audio plays machine and surface sounds only: rung clank per hand, steel groan by hold_load, pipe shriek by slide_mps, flange slam by slam_mps, a landing thud. Her breathing stays a recorded human voice.

src/sim/matron.cpp route_toward(): Dijkstra over about a dozen nodes per level, with way_clear() casting 3 static-only rays at her hips. onto_floor_lines() and floor_of() (a level within 8 m) and settle_level() (|feet_y - floor_y| < 0.6) all go through levels_.

src/sim/matron.cpp walk_toward(): edge_at() and floor_at() cast 3 rays (her middle and kFootSpanM 0.24 to each side) at 4 samples to kStepOverM 0.45, for several checks a tick, plus the leap (kLeapReachM 3.0) and vault probes. kEdgeDropM 1.2, kEdgeMarginM 0.25.

src/sim/matron.cpp follow_climb() and climb(): her gravity is turned off (SetGravityFactor 0) and SetLinearVelocity is used with kClimbAccel 70, so her weight never reaches the rungs. Frail, she only stands at the foot. In the Turn she climbs at kClimbMps 0.6 with kClimbBurstMps 2.2 jerks and a mantle of kMantleOutM 1.0.

It runs with SCRAPERX_BAKE_NAV=<path> ./build/host/scraperx_sim_tests and is restricted to the tower footprint and machine frames. (2) Sheets found: 14 stack decks at 11.00..154.00, 11 rings at 176.25..396.25, and the upper decks (340.45, 418.25, 640.25, 662.1, 684.1 ... 750), with the 155.18 bridge merged into deck 14. milestones.title: The Hold: her hands carry her weight, with a grip the world can beat
milestones.what: New src/sim/matron_hold.cpp: a breakable, motor-driven SliderConstraint along the member, with gravity on, pull 3,400 N, squeeze 3,000 N, grip 5,500 N / 450 Ns, and hard limits at flanges and heads. Pole hands and legs, the regrip reflex, slam and stun. climb() moves onto it, and the riser's slide and shin are added. Her rotation part is confirmed deactivated, with no NaNs.
milestones.proof: Native `matron-hold`. Ladder: up the 154 to 176 ladder, the hold measuring 2,158 N +-3% while she rests on it, onto the 176 ring. Riser down 154 to 143: peak 3.2 m/s or less, stops at the flange, hauls over 143's rail. Riser up 143 to 154 in 30 s or less when dangerous. A 15 kg toolbox at 7.5 m/s leaves her on. A 200 kg drum shoved over 154's rail onto her tears her hands off: she slips to the next flange (slam 11 m/s or less), alive, stunned at least 2 s, then climbs again. Ledger: she never gains height beyond the work her motor did. A dynamic kit hold shows her weight as its load. All existing `matron` sections pass.

milestones.title: Seen, heard, played by touch
milestones.what: MatronSnapshot gains link_kind, link_progress, hold_load, slide_mps, slam_mps, stun_s and sheet_y. matron_view.gd gets poses (pipe wrap and slide, brace crawl, rail haul, drop and crouch, knock-loose flail, wrong-limbed rise). The player climbs C3's ladders while she shins up behind, shoves the drum over the rail onto her (she drops a storey, alive), and reaches the 176 ring. It fails unless every beat's native event (link log, knock-off, slam) happened. A phone-budget perf check (her tick 0.2 ms or less mean in the preview build) passes.

risks: The Hold's SliderConstraint on a rotation-locked capsule: Jolt deactivates the rotation part, but the position part with a moving motor target on a 220 kg body against static steel must be checked for jitter at 90 Hz. Fallback: a PointConstraint to a small kinematic 'hand' body driven along the member, with her axial pull capped by her own controller and the grip still read from the constraint's lambda.

Bake churn and size: every world edit regenerates matron_nav.inc, as with world_solids.inc, and CI's drift step adds a few seconds. Run-length storage keeps it near 60 KB. If it grows, the cells go to 0.75 m on the large stack bands only.

Silly generated links (a lamp mast, a moving machine part, a member that clips a deck edge at hugging offset). Mitigations: the bake region is restricted, members are static only, dynamic holds must weigh 400 kg or more, each member's usable span is swept with her capsule, an explicit entity deny list, and the connectivity report is reviewed before it is committed.

A Matron who can go anywhere can make the climb oppressive and will break the tuned first act (touch_matron_act relies on her frail stage not being able to climb). Stage gates, the pest's 90 s give-up, the 20 s route-time checkpoint freeze, and the owner's rule that a silent climber keeps her a pest are the levers. The first act needs retuning, and this should be named to the owner.

Machines with her aboard: counter-mass lifts may stall or run in reverse with 220 kg more in the cage, and a governed car may pin her. These are emergent and wanted, but each lift needs a 'ride with her' test, and none may be left with no way to fix it or go on.

'Never killed by being knocked off' depends on the regrip reflex finding something. Spans over the open shaft are marked, and a hit there can still kill her. The owner wants her kept at bay, not killed, so those spans may need to be closed to her or given a net or flange.

Phone cost when she is on dynamic floors or in transfers (rays come back there). The per-tick ray budget and the perf test guard it, but ARM ray cost is not yet measured. Jolt float determinism between ARM and x86 is still not established (already an open item).

Presentation: a 2.1 m figure on a 0.45 m brace in the face plane, or wrapped round a 0.7 m pipe 0.6 m from a rail, may clip. The bake's swept spans keep her body clear, but her limbs need their own IK pass in matron_view.gd.
result.wow: You are on the 143 m deck by the shaft's corner when the tower starts to shriek: skin and cloth on steel. You look over the rail and up through the open shaft, and she is coming down the riser pipe 1.2 m out over the drop, wrapped round it like something that isn't a person, a whole storey in four seconds. She slams onto the flange just under your feet and her hands come over the rail. You shove the oil drum off the deck above onto her as she starts up again. It tears her off, she slides screaming down the pipe to the next flange, and lies there. Then she turns her face up toward you and starts to climb.

result.name: Off Her Feet: the Matron's balance, and everything in the tower that can take it
result.pitch: You can't fight a 220 kg thing with your fists, but the tower is full of mass, and she has to stand on two legs or four like anyone. She comes scuttling along the band on all fours. You sprint at the ingot dolly and shove it rolling down the band, and it takes her legs. She goes down full length on the steel and slides, and the floor shakes. As a frail pest you can slide under her reaching hands and sweep her feet; when the Turn's wind-up brings her upright and shaking, you heave the toolbox in your hands and she goes over backward. She stays down for seconds, never for good: she gets up faster and more wrongly at each stage, every fall makes her angrier, and if you knock her over an edge her hands always catch it. So the game becomes reading her stance, choosing what to hit her with, and going quiet before she stands up again.
mechanics: Her balance, modeled in the simulation as a declared reduced-order body (plan section 2.6 rule 3), the same way the player's landing recovery is: an inverted pendulum. The Matron gets a lean state: her center of mass offset from her feet, x, and its speed v, both 2D in the floor plane. Each tick, x'' = (g/h)x minus her recovery, and her recovery is capped by stage. A blow adds its velocity change to v. She falls when v > w(b + r), with w = sqrt(g/h); h is her center-of-mass height, b her base half-width and r how far she can step. Below w*b she absorbs the blow, between the two she staggers, above it she goes down. It costs a few floating-point operations a tick, all from simulation state, with no randomness.

Her stance follows what she is doing, matching the pose matron_view.gd already draws. Upright (shuffling, searching, peering, guarding, unrigging, and the Turn's wind-up, where she stands folded at the waist and shaking): h 1.05 m, b 0.12 m, w 3.06 per second. On all fours (hunting above 1 m/s, the Turn's lunges): h 0.55 m, b 0.45 m, w 4.22 per second. Her step reach r by stage (CHOSEN): pest 0.20 m, dangerous 0.55 m, fully changed 0.85 m. The speeds that knock her down: upright, 0.98 / 2.05 / 2.97 m/s; on all fours, 2.74 / 4.22 / 5.49 m/s. Special cases: in the Turn's wind-up r is 0, so any blow over 0.37 m/s puts her down; during a lunge's bursts r is doubled, so mid-burst she is all but impossible to knock down; with stock in her hands (a pest's mischief) r is halved, because her hands cannot catch her.

What counts as a blow, measured the deterministic way the impact ledger already works. walk_toward and climb store the velocity they set. In post_step, the external change is the velocity after the step, minus that stored velocity, minus gravity times dt. It counts only when a body was moving toward her at 1 m/s or more before the step: the player, stock, a machine, a cage. The check is a CollideShape query after the step, of her capsule grown by 3 cm against the moving and player layers, with results sorted by BodyID. The striker's speed before the step comes from a pre_velocity added to the ledger's ImpactSnapshot (the ledger already has it as last_velocity). This is the player's own 'struck' rule: running into a wall, a rail or a crate at rest never knocks her down. The contact's height sets which way she falls: below her knees (0.5 m) a sweep takes her base, so she falls toward the striker; above that a shove sends her away from it.

Stagger: the Staggering state, 0.4 to 1.2 seconds depending on how far the blow went past w*b. Her feet stop chasing. walk_toward drives her toward her own capture point at her stage's recovery acceleration (pest 4, dangerous 9, changed 16 m/s^2), so she stumbles a few steps the way she was knocked, and those steps can carry her over an edge. Her hands are out to catch herself: caught() returns false the whole time.

Down, a real body on the floor. BodyInterface::SetShape swaps her standing capsule (radius 0.30, half-height 0.75) for the same capsule lying along the fall's direction. SetPositionAndRotation sets it down; this is allowed because her rotation is locked by mAllowedDOFs, not by the solver. It is laid where a shape cast finds room; where there is none she crumples into a 0.9 m kneeling capsule. Her friction goes from 0 to 0.6 while she is down, cloth on steel, so she slides and stops. Down time: pest 6.0 s, dangerous 3.5 s, changed 1.5 s. While down she has no hands (no catch), no eyes (sees() is false, her face is on the plates) and no Turn (turn_ is reset). She is a 0.6 m obstacle the player can vault with the existing vault move; fully changed, a hand comes up as you pass over her (caught() applies to a body within 0.6 m above her lying axis).

Getting up, and crawling out. She stands only when the standing capsule clears a shape cast at her lying center. If a beam is low over her, or a crate or trolley lies on her legs, she crawls out first at 0.8 m/s (a Crawling state: the lying capsule driven along the floor by her feet code at 4 m/s^2) to the nearest clear spot, which can be straight at you. How she rises differs by stage: a pest's slow push-up, a dangerous Matron's quick one, and fully changed, a rise all at once with every joint wrong (the view decides the pose; the simulation only sets the time). For 1.5 s after she stands she is set (r doubled), so she cannot be kept down by blow after blow.

Over an edge, her hands always catch it. This is how 'not kill her' holds for every edge. When a stagger or a fall takes her feet off the floor (no floor within kEdgeDropM under her middle, falling faster than 2 m/s), she catches the last floor point she stood on, which is recorded every tick she is on the floor. That builds a temporary Climb record there (foot_y the rim less 2.1 m, head_y the rim, pointing back over the floor) and a PointConstraint holding her hands to the world at the lip. The existing climb() then mantles her up, gravity factor 0 as on a ladder: 7 s for a pest, 3.5 s dangerous, 1.5 s changed. Nothing the player does makes her let go. The catwalk is unchanged: a plate whose bolt shears under her takes her down with it, and that stays the one thing that kills her.

Pain feeds her rage. Hearing does not, because her own impact falls inside kOwnSoundM. A knockdown adds 0.10 to her rage as a pest, 0.08 dangerous and 0.05 changed; a stagger adds 0.02. Her body is tracked in the ImpactLedger, so her 220 kg landing on steel is a real hit: the presentation plays it and anything else that listens hears it. Because she is blind on the floor, since_heard_s_ keeps running from the blow. A player who knocks her down and then goes quiet and out of sight sees her stand up into Searching, then Guarding: they have lost her. Each knockdown costs about 30 s of quiet (rage decays at 0.003 a second), so knocking her down is a choice with a price, not a spam button.

The Turn: the wind-up is also the opening. The 0.9 s she stands still and upright before a lunge is the one warning and now the one window: any blow fells her. A knockdown cancels the Turn and restarts its cooldown at her stage's value (turn_cooldown_seconds). The more changed she is, the more often she rears (the cooldown drops from 45 s to 4 s), so the more often there is a window, but she stays down only 1.5 s.

THROW, the one new player verb, on touch with no new button. Grounded with a load in the hands (kit CarryKind::Load), the up-swipe's move ahead becomes UpMove::Throw (a new value 15 appended to the enum in simulation.hpp). The hint 'THROW' is drawn where the thumb swipes, through touch_controls.gd's up_hint, with no label on any object. update_carry lets go of the load and adds the arm's impulse along the view (facing plus look pitch): min(270 N*s, m * 10 m/s), the grip force (900 N) over a 0.3 s heave. That is a toolbox at 10 m/s, a 22 kg pallet at 10, a 50 kg pig at 5.4 and a 55 kg drum at 4.9, all on top of the body's own speed. The reaction is paid as balance debt on the ground (like shove_player's stumble) and as velocity in the air. A thrown toolbox fells an upright pest (1.3 * 18 * 10 / 238 = 0.98 m/s) and staggers anything else. A thrown drum lands on its side and rolls.

The slide tackle, an existing parkour move (a swipe down at a sprint). Feet first into her body counts as a landing for the legs, using the crouched landing speeds (kLandingPreparedFreeSpeed 8, kAnkleBreakPreparedSpeed 14), not as a hit to the head. When she is upright and the player's slide puts his center below her knees, the slide goes under her hands: caught() is false for that body, and the sweep (about 3.4 m/s against a Matron walking upright) fells her at every stage. On all fours her hands are low, and her hands reach 0.85 m while her body is 0.65 m away, so a slide runs into her hands. A pest shoves him, a dangerous Matron shoves him at the shaft, and fully changed it is a death. The slide counters her early and kills you late.

Mass from the world. Anything moving that meets her counts, because the blow is measured, not scripted: the ingot dolly on her deck (420 kg, friction 0.06, at 19.4, -147.4 by the catwalk's east end), drums and gas bottles knocked over to roll, a swinging cage, a forklift. Shoved into her charge, mass is judo: a 260 kg cart at 4 m/s meeting her at 6.8 gives 1.3 * 260 * 10.8 / 480 = 7.6 m/s, which fells her at every stage outside a burst. Stock is added freely: a block trolley (LooseStock::Kind::BlockTrolley, 260 kg of concrete block on a flat steel trolley with a yellow push handle, friction 0.06) on every stack deck and upper ring, laid by a new lay_trolleys() after lay_matron_throwables() so saves made before it still line up. With her roaming the whole tower, every level then has something light to throw (dress_tower's toolboxes, pallets, drums) and something heavy to roll.

Her own counterplay, learned within a run like fooled_ and forgotten on a restore, and scaling with her stage. A pest is too frail to answer anything. Dangerous: a thrown piece of 25 kg or less that she sees coming, within 1 m of her hands, she catches with the existing take_stock and PointConstraint and throws back at once through throw_stock (0.2 s wind-up). A piece thrown from behind, or while she peers at a lure noise, still lands. Once a rolling or sliding body has knocked her down, she watches tracked bodies: one she can see closing on her at 2 m/s or more with under 0.6 s to contact, she sidesteps at kCutAccel (dangerous and changed, never mid-burst). Fully changed, she swats thrown pieces aside instead of catching them, and only mass or the wind-up works.

The music box comes off. On a knockdown 1.5 times or more past her fall threshold, the cord at her hip parts (a declared simplification: the simulation adds the box body, a 0.6 kg carryable, entity Matron::kEntity + 2, at her hip, with her hip's velocity and the fall's whip). It skitters across the deck, still playing, its 90 s spring running down. After she stands, a pest or a dangerous Matron goes to the box before going after the player, ties it back on (4 s pest, 2 s dangerous) and stays still while she does it. Within 6 m of it, still playing, her rage falls 4 times as fast. The player can PICK UP the box, and then she hunts the music: the box is a sound she hears each tick at loudness 0.5, through decks, by carry_m. Thrown onto the deck below, it leaves her standing at the rail over it, on her own lines, listening down, until it runs down. Thrown somewhere she cannot hear it, it is gone for the run, and with it the last thing that calms her: her rage then never falls below 0.30. Fully changed, the box no longer draws her at all.
grounding: src/sim/matron.hpp: class Matron, State enum Dormant..Unrigging (= 9), to which Staggering = 10, Down = 11, Crawling = 12 and Rim = 13 would be added; Stage {Pest, Dangerous, Changed}; Turn {None, Windup, Lunge} with kTurnWindupSeconds 0.9, kTurnBurstMps 9.0, kTurnPauseMps 3.5, kTurnCooldownPestSeconds 45 and kTurnCooldownChangedSeconds 4; body constants kMassKg 220, kRadius 0.30, kHalfHeight 0.75, kStandCentre 1.05; kCatchM 0.85; kFallenBelowM 12; kOwnSoundM 1.5; rage constants kRageDecayPerSecond 0.003, kRageDangerousDown 0.30, kRageChangedUp 0.85; the Saved and View structs; Throwable and set_throwables (at most 32, the handled_ bitmask); the Climb struct {x, z, foot_y, head_y, out_x, out_z}

src/sim/matron.cpp constructor (lines 115-127): her body is a dynamic capsule on the moving layer, mAllowedDOFs translation only, mFriction 0, mAllowSleeping false, mass overridden to 220 kg. So SetShape/SetRotation can lay her down without the solver tipping her, and her friction must rise while she is down.
