milestones.title: Her balance and the blow, in the native
milestones.what: The lean state and inverted-pendulum step in Matron::post_step. The blow measured as velocity change after the step, minus what her feet set, counted only from a body that was approaching her (CollideShape after the step, sorted by BodyID; ledger pre_velocity). Stance taken from her state, the stage step-reach table, the Staggering state with stumbling steps toward her capture point, Down as a timer (still upright at this stage), caught() off while staggering or down, pain added to rage, and the Turn cancelled by a knockdown. New View fields: knockdowns, staggers, balance.
milestones.proof: A new group SCRAPERX_ONLY=matron-balance (run_matron_balance in tests/sim_tests_matron.cpp). (a) push_toward the ingot dolly into a pest coming up the east band: knockdowns == 1, shoves == 0, down at least 5.5 s, rage up by at least 0.10. (b) After debug_set_matron_stage(2), the same push at a walk into her hunting on all fours: staggers >= 1, knockdowns == 0. (c) Her full-speed hunt into the east band's skid crates (pieces 3 and 4) and the shaft rail: knockdowns == 0 and staggers == 0. (d) A knockdown in her Turn's wind-up ends the Turn (turn == 0, cooldown restarted). Then SCRAPERX_ONLY=determinism with a knockdown in its run, still identical bit for bit, and matron, matron-collision and matron-mischief all still pass.

milestones.title: THROW on touch
milestones.what: UpMove::Throw (value 15, appended), offered by update_up_move when grounded with a CarryKind::Load in the hands, resolved in resolve_up, and carried out in update_carry: let go plus the arm impulse min(270 N*s, m * 10 m/s) along the view, the reaction paid as balance debt. In main.gd and touch_controls.gd the up-swipe hint reads THROW where the thumb swipes. A thrown piece counts as handled_ for her mischief.
milestones.proof: SCRAPERX_ONLY=handling, extended: a toolbox leaves the hands at 10 +- 0.3 m/s faster than the body along the view, a 55 kg drum at 4.9, a 50 kg pig at 5.4. The thrower stumbles (stumble_count +1) and does not fly. A thrown toolbox landing shows up in the ledger as a hit. Every existing touch scenario that swipes up with a load in the hands (touch_stack's pig into the third lift's cage, touch_wet's spool) still passes, or is updated on purpose.

milestones.title: A body on the floor
milestones.what: SetShape to the lying capsule, laid where a shape cast clears (else the kneeling crumple), friction 0.6 while down, the rise checked against the standing capsule, Crawling out from under, the 1.5 s set after rising, and restore() putting her upright and back at her locker. The player can vault her lying body. Fully changed, her hand comes up at a body passing over her.
milestones.proof: matron-balance: after a knockdown her shape's bounding box is under 0.7 m tall and the player's vault is offered across her. A skid crate shoved onto her legs gives crawls == 1 before she stands. A checkpoint restore mid-Down gives state Emerging and the standing shape. A second blow within 1.5 s of standing does not put her down again. look_matron_gallery gains _pose("down_pest"), _pose("crawl") and _pose("rise_changed") PNGs (Xvfb plus --capture, per the handoff).

milestones.title: Her hands always catch the edge
milestones.what: The last floor point she stood on is recorded every tick. Off the floor during a stagger or a fall, she builds a temporary Climb at that point, takes a PointConstraint at the lip, and climb() mantles her back: 7 / 3.5 / 1.5 s by stage. The catwalk's bolt rule stays the one death.
milestones.proof: A new group SCRAPERX_ONLY=matron-rim. The ingot dolly is shoved into her at the catwalk's east mouth (x 17.6, z -147 to -153, where the shaft's rail is open for the plates). Result: rim_hangs == 1, alive, feet back on the band within 7.5 s as a pest and 2 s fully changed, and the player's death_count unchanged. The existing catwalk test (her weight shears a plate, she falls, state Dead) still passes in matron.

milestones.title: What she learns, stage by stage, and the slide
milestones.what: Dangerous, she catches a thrown piece she can see and throws it back. Once knocked down by a rolling body, she dodges bodies she can see coming. Fully changed, she swats thrown pieces aside. A slide under the hands of an upright Matron fells her; a slide into her on all fours is caught. The feet-first slide counts as a landing for the legs. The block trolley is added (lay_trolleys, after lay_matron_throwables).
milestones.proof: matron-balance stage cases, set with debug_set_matron_stage. (a) A pest searching upright, met by a crouch at a sprint: knockdowns +1, shoves +0, deaths +0. (b) Fully changed and hunting on all fours, the same slide: death_count +1. (c) Dangerous and facing, a toolbox thrown at her: catches_thrown +1 and throws +1 within 1 s; the same throw from behind while she peers at a crate dropped as a lure: staggers or knockdowns +1. (d) A second trolley at a dangerous Matron felled by the first: dodges +1. Then SCRAPERX_ONLY=save and stock pass with the trolleys appended, and an older save still loads with its stock where it was.

milestones.title: The music box comes off
milestones.what: The box body is added on a knockdown 1.5 times past her fall threshold. A 90 s spring. She goes to it (pest or dangerous) and ties it back on, her rage falling 4 times as fast near it while it plays. Carried by the player, she hunts the music; thrown to the level below, she stands over it listening; thrown out of her hearing, it is lost and her rage floor is 0.30. The presentation plays matron_music at the box's body.
milestones.proof: A new group SCRAPERX_ONLY=matron-box. A dolly knockdown gives box_loose == true and a box body on the deck. After she stands, her target is the box before the player, and her rage falls at 4 times 0.003 a second while she is near it. Player PICK UP gives her a lead on the box each tick. The box thrown over 143's gate onto the 143 m band leaves her still on her deck, over that place, for the rest of the spring. Fully changed (debug stage 2), a loose box draws her nowhere.

milestones.title: Played by touch through all three stages, seen and heard
milestones.what: A new touch playthrough, touch_matron_bay (ui_test_bay.gd extending ui_test_chase.gd, added to ui_test_driver.gd's table), from the 154 m deck. Wake her. As a pest, slide under her hands; heave the north band's toolbox during a Turn's wind-up. Dangerous, roll the ingot dolly into her at the catwalk's east mouth: she goes over the rim and hauls herself up. Use her box as a lure. Fully changed, only mass and the wind-up work. Then on to Stage A's cage and up. In matron_view.gd, the poses (stumble, sprawled full length, crawl, three rises, hanging by the hands from the lip) and the sound of 220 kg landing on steel plate. No synthesized voice: her cry is a recorded human performance or nothing.
milestones.proof: tools/godot/godot --headless --fixed-fps 60 --path godot -- --uitest=touch_matron_bay passes, failing if any beat does not happen in the simulation (knockdowns, rim_hangs and box_loose read from the native, deaths only where the scenario means one). With Xvfb and --capture, a screenshot of each knockdown, the rim haul-up and the loose box. touch_matron_act still passes unchanged.

risks: Swapping her shape next to other bodies can leave her overlapping them, and Jolt then pushes them apart violently (a launch). She must be laid only where a shape cast clears, else crumpled into the kneeling capsule. Standing up has to pass the same check.

Catch before contact: her hands reach 0.85 m and her body 0.65 m, so a fast striker is caught a tick before the blow lands. The 'slide under the hands' rule and 'hands busy while staggering or down' must live in caught(), and matron_->post_step must stay ahead of the caught check in PhysicsWorld::step (lines 713 and 767), or the slide tackle kills the player.

Determinism: the blow must never be read from contact callbacks, which run in job order. Only queries after the step, with results sorted by BodyID, and the ledger's velocities in its tracked order. Determinism across machines (Android ARM against x86 CI) is still not established for any of this.

Balance tuning: too easy and she stops being scary; too hard and the defense is useless. The step reaches, recovery rates, down times and pain-to-rage numbers are CHOSEN and need tuning in the touch playthrough. Pain feeding rage limits overuse by itself, but it can also push a clumsy player to fully changed early.

Stunlock: a 420 kg dolly or trolley pinned against her could knock her again every tick. The 1.5 s set after rising, and a down timer that a blow never restarts, must hold. A test should cover a dolly left resting against her.

The rim catch has to work on moving floors and odd geometry: a cage, a plate, the 1.09 m gap at the 176 ring's cages. A lip on a moving body needs the constraint on that body, not on the world. A lip on a plate whose bolt then shears is a death by design, and that has to read as fair.

Turning the up-swipe with a load from Jump into THROW changes existing play. Any touch scenario or player habit that jumps with a carried load (the third lift's pig, the float lift's spool) has to be checked.

Save layout: the new trolleys and her box body add bodies, and Matron::Saved may grow. The trolleys must be appended after lay_matron_throwables, and the box kept out of the kit's body order, or older saves lose their stock positions. The save and stock groups should be run.
The drawing must match the collision shape: the lying figure has to fill the lying capsule, or the player vaults air or trips on nothing.

Voices: the owner's rule is recorded human voices only. Her cry on going down needs a real recorded performance; until then the knockdown is heard as body and steel only, and the existing synthesized cues on her should be checked against this rule.
Cost on a phone: a CollideShape and shape casts each tick are cheap but not free. Run them only on ticks with a blow or while she is down, staggering or rising.
result.wow: The Turn: her spine cracks, she rears upright and shaking, and the music box warps. You have the toolbox in your hands and swipe up. It hits her square in the wind-up, and she goes over backward full length onto the deck plates; you feel the boom of 220 kg landing on steel. The cord at her hip snaps, and the music box skitters away across the plates, still playing, slowing as its spring runs down. Her head turns the wrong way round on the floor, toward the box and not toward you, and she drags herself after it on her elbows. You have about six seconds, and you didn't kill her.

result.name: The Riser Road: her whole tower, deck to deck
result.pitch: You are on deck 99, quiet, and somewhere far above a clang rings down the shaft. Then another, closer. One clang for every deck. You lean over the rail and look up: 22 m above you, in the corner of the shaft, a white tunic is wrapped round the rusty pipe that runs the whole height of the Stack. She is sliding down it, stopping on each flange with a bang and turning her face down to look for you. As a pest she comes after you the way a person would: slowly down a ladder backward, or hanging from a zipline's trolley. Once you make her dangerous, the building's pipes belong to her. Fully changed, she crawls up the diagonal steel on the outside of the tower and drops through hatches onto you. The tower stops being a level with a monster on it. It is her house, and every way between decks is a way she might be coming.
mechanics: THE TOWER GRAPH (new src/sim/matron_nav.hpp/.cpp, class TowerNav). It is built once when the world is built, right after the ziplines (physics_world.cpp, next to matron_->set_zipline), from the static collision itself. NarrowPhaseQuery::CollectTransformedShapes is run over the tower's box (about x -60..60, y 5..800, z -210..-90), limited to static bodies, and gives every box leaf: the native stack slabs, world_solids.inc and the kit's static parts. Cylinder and hull leaves are skipped. FLOORS: a leaf with a level top that is at least 0.9 m wide both ways and has 2.2 m of headroom. Floors whose tops are within 0.35 m of each other and that overlap or touch within kStepOverM (0.45 m) join into one LEVEL, using union-find in a fixed order. A level's WALKING LINES are each floor box's center line along its long axis (two crossing lines on a large plate), plus a connector node where two boxes overlap. This rebuilds the band loop the Matron uses today, and it breaks the loop correctly at deck 7's east hatch (z -148.70..-145.00). Each line is checked at build time with today's way_clear sweep (static only, at hip height, across her width) and the floor_at samples from walk_toward. If a line is blocked it moves sideways inside its box by up to 3 m, and if it is still blocked it is dropped and listed. A floor that rises 0.15 to 0.6 m above its neighbor is a STEP edge (the new clamber move). From 0.6 to 1.4 m it is a VAULT edge (her existing Turn vault). LEVELS AUTHORED BY HAND WIN: the 154 m deck (catwalk, post, eye, ladder) and the 176 ring (cages, gap, posts) keep their hand-written Level. A generated level at the same height only adds short spurs from those lines to the feet of new links. Each spur is checked with way_clear.

LINKS BETWEEN LEVELS, all generated, each a record of kind, from_level, to_level, foot (the stand point on the walking lines and the mount point), her climb line (a vertical line, x and z, with a bottom y and a top y), head landing, out direction, and over_m (how high she must rise to get over a rail at each end). MEMBERS: a static leaf at most 35 degrees off vertical and at least 3 m long. A run of four or more horizontal holds (box_is_hold) stacked at 0.45 m or less is a LADDER. A vertical member with a 0.3 to 0.9 m section is a PIPE: the four corner risers at x +-15.8, z -134.2 and -165.8, 0.7 m square, from 0 to 154 m, with a 1.1 m flange at every deck minus 1.4 m. These are too thick for the player's hands (kGripMaxSection 0.18), so they belong to her alone. A 0.9 to 1.8 m member is a COLUMN. A member tilted 15 to 35 degrees is a BRACE (the Stack's StackBrace diagrid, UpperColumn and UpperBrace above 154 m). A member becomes a link between two levels it passes when there is a standable point within 1.3 m of it on both levels. Her climb line is the nearest vertical line within 1.2 m of the member that her capsule (radius 0.3, half-height 0.75) can sweep from foot to head without touching anything static. That rule makes her clear the riser flanges on her own, and the presentation leans her figure in to hug the pipe. A riser therefore gives 13 storey links per pipe, 52 in all, each usable up and down. LINES come straight from Zipline::lines() (stand, ramp_foot, top_floor, bottom_floor), down only. RIDES come from kit guides with a vertical axis whose body has a floor part of 1 m^2 or more, with one stop at each end of travel, each matched to a level. This needs a small new Kit API: guide_count, guide_body, guide_axis, guide_limits. DROPS: perimeter probes every 1 m along each floor box edge that no other floor touches find floor 2.5 to 11.5 m below with a clear fall column, for example deck 7's hatch, landings, and cage roofs. GAPS: floor again within 3 m at a height difference of 0.8 m or less. REACHES: a ladder or pipe whose foot she cannot stand at but which is within 2.5 m of a floor edge, for example the upper route's ladders, which stand off 0.3 m boards. A hold on a floor narrower than her is never a foot. This keeps the act's rule that she cannot follow up the standpipe to 198 m.

WHO MAY USE WHAT, tied to the three stages so the player can read it. PEST: what a person uses. That means walking, the clamber, ladders (up at 0.4 m/s, down backward at 0.5 m/s), a zipline whose trolley is parked (Zipline::clip_other with on_cable=false: frail, she rides lines like anyone), and rides on a car that is already at her stop when it is moving her way or the player is aboard. She never sends a car away (decision 9 B). DANGEROUS: also the building's pipes: up a riser at 0.7 m/s, down it in a slide held to 3 m/s by her forearms and knees, stopping 0.6 s on each flange she passes (each stop is a clang), plus the bare cable of a ridden line (today's Turn move), ladders up at 0.9 m/s and head-first down at 1.6 m/s. FULLY CHANGED: also the outside steel (columns and braces, up at 0.8 m/s and down at 1.2 m/s), drops of up to 11.5 m (she lands, crumples for 1.2 s, and gets up), gaps, and reaches. THE TURN keeps its present meaning: for its 3.2 s it adds the jerky bursts (kClimbBurstMps 2.2 on any climb) and the gap leap and bare cable at any stage, as today. The present 'frail cannot take hold of a ladder' rule becomes 'a pest climbs it slowly'.

HER MOVES ON A LINK are one generalized form of today's climb(): gravity factor 0, and velocity driven toward her climb line with the kClimbAccel limit. Each link has phases. APPROACH: walk to the foot along the level's lines. MOUNT: up over_m and out to the climb line, which is today's mantle in reverse and gets her over a shaft rail. TRAVERSE: up or down at the link's speed. Going down a pipe, she stops at each flange height. DISMOUNT: today's mantle, rising over_m at the head to clear the rail before stepping in (kMantleOutM). Each phase has a time budget. When a phase runs over (a crate on the ladder's head, a car that has left), she backs off, refuses that link for 20 s (like fetch_refused_), and re-plans. Rides reuse today's clinging (feel_floor and riding_). She steps off once the car has stopped plus kLetGoSeconds. Lines reuse follow_line and ride_line. A drop is a short fall that is exempt from the kFallenBelowM death check until she lands on the target level. On any link the climb, line, or riding exemptions from the fall check apply, as now.

HOW SHE PERCEIVES A PLAYER ON ANOTHER LEVEL. (1) HEARING is unchanged. carry_m and decks_between already carry sound through the decks (kDeckMuffle 10) or round through the shaft (kBendMuffle 1.4). decks_between counts only levels marked as decks (more than 50 m^2), so a cage roof or a stand does not muffle. (2) SIGHT THROUGH THE SHAFT is new. When the player is on another level within 40 m, today's two-ray sees() from her eyes to them is run once a tick. A clear line gives a seen lead on the player's level. This is what lets her look up at you from three decks down. (3) GUESSES generalize guess_line_ and guess_climb_ into guess_link_. A player seen or heard on any link (ladder rungs, a line, a car, the riser ladder) is guessed to be going to its far end. (4) LOOKING: a lead she will not chase sends her to the rail over or under it (onto_floor_lines, as today), where she stands in the Peering state with her head pitched up or down the shaft. The player can see her face at the rail above them.

HOW SHE CHOOSES TO PURSUE (replacing the one-level-at-a-time follow_line and follow_climb with follow_plan). The nodes are link feet and heads on each level. Walking edges cost path length divided by her speed. Link edges cost their time at her stage plus 1.5 s each to mount and dismount, and links her stage cannot use are left out. Dijkstra runs from where she stands to the point on the lead's level nearest the lead, with ties broken by index. It runs when the lead changes level, every 0.5 s while she pursues, and when she arrives at a link's head. She carries out only the first link, then plans again. WHAT A LEAD IS WORTH: a seen lead, always. A heard lead, only if the plan costs no more than 40 s for a pest, 150 s when dangerous, and anything when fully changed. Otherwise she goes to look (above). AMBUSH (decision 9 B, waiting quiet at a choke point): when the player is on a link and she can reach its far end before they can, she plans to the far end and waits there still and silent, which is today's Guarding pose. GIVING UP: kLoseTrackSeconds and Searching as today, then stand_down. On a generated level there is no post, so she patrols the level's loop.

KEEPING HER AT BAY WITHOUT KILLING HER (the owner's newest ask, in a causal world). On any climb her grip has a limit, like the player's ledge grip. Something that hits her hard enough knocks her off: an impulse on her body over kHerGripNs (CHOSEN, about one 25 kg toolbox let go from a deck above onto her on the pipe). She then slides down the member with her grip gone for 0.5 s, catches it again, and gets off at the level below, alive. A storey lost and her rage spikes. Dropping stock down the shaft onto her uses the touch controls the player already has (PICK UP, then LET GO over the rail). The catwalk is still the one thing that kills her.

CHECKPOINT. freezes_checkpoint() changes from 'the player is on her deck' to 'her planned time to the player is under kSafeLeadSeconds (CHOSEN 25 s)'. The plan cost is cached every 0.5 s and worked out again at once after a restore. Her release edge still commits once, as now. A restore no longer always puts her back at her locker. Saved gains her level's floor height, position, and yaw, as they were at the commit. If she was out, a restore puts her body back there in the Searching state with no lead, her rage and stage as committed. Her place at a commit is a floor she stood on, because a commit is not taken while she is on a link. DISK SAVE: her Saved record is appended after the grips in write_save (the existing rule that a later record goes last, so older saves still load). A save without it loads with her asleep, as all saves do today.

DETERMINISTIC AND CHEAP ON A PHONE. The build goes through the leaves in a sorted order (by y, then x, then z, then size), rounds every generated coordinate to 1 cm, and uses no clock and no randomness. Its hash is printed and checked. Cost: one pass over a few thousand box leaves, a few hundred capsule sweeps for climb lines and walking lines, and about 8,000 one-ray drop probes, all once, at load. That is a few tens of milliseconds on a desktop. Per tick, she adds one cross-level sight check at most, and only while the player is within 40 m on another level. Dijkstra over 300 to 600 nodes runs at most twice a second. A level's walking-line search stays today's route_toward over a few dozen nodes. Memory is well under 100 KB. If phone startup or cross-platform hashes are a problem, the same generator writes a baked src/sim/tower_nav.inc, in the way world_solids.inc is generated and checked for drift in CI.

RAGE AND STAGES are unchanged, but they now decide her reach. A quiet player keeps her a pest, and a pest goes only as far as a ladder or a parked trolley will take her within 40 s. Noise opens the pipes. Fully changed, she can reach the whole tower. The player learns this by watching her, never from a meter.

PRESENTATION AND SOUND (matron_view.gd _pose gets new branches beside climbing, on_line and clinging). The snapshot carries link_kind, link_phase and link_dir. New poses: shinning up a pipe (arms hugging, legs hitching, the figure leaned in to the pipe); sliding down it (head up, knees locked round it); backing down a ladder as a pest, or coming down it head first when dangerous; crawling up a diagonal brace spread out like a spider; crumpling after a drop and rising with joints cracking; hanging from a trolley's bar. Sound comes from the steel. Her hands and feet strike the pipe and the rungs, a flange rings when she stops on it, and a long screech marks a slide. milestones.title: M1: The Stack is hers, deck to deck from 11 to 176 m, by the corner risers, the ladders and the lines
milestones.what: TowerNav builds the stack decks from 11 to 143 m (with deck 7's hatch breaking its east band) and keeps the hand-written 154 deck and 176 ring, joined by checked spurs. It also builds the clamber and step edges and these links: the 52 corner-riser storey links up and down, every ladder she can stand at both ends of (her ladder to 176, the C3 riser ladder from 143 to 154, and any others the rules accept), and all the stack lines. Also in this milestone: follow_plan (Dijkstra, a lead's worth by stage, the ambush at a link's far end, refusal after a stall), sight across levels through the shaft, guess_link_, the stage gates (a pest climbs ladders slowly and rides parked trolleys; dangerous opens the risers and bare cables), the reach-time checkpoint rule with restore where she stood (in memory), and poses for the pipe climb, the pipe slide and going down a ladder. The act is re-staged on purpose: on 143, made dangerous, she now comes down the pipe while the climber goes up the riser ladder past her.
milestones.proof: Native `matron-nav` (new): 14 stack levels found, with deck 7's east band split at z -148.7..-145.0. 52 riser links. Every stack deck has a way up and a way down for a dangerous Matron, and a way down for a pest. No link foot is on a floor narrower than her: the standpipe to 198 and the route ladders above 220 are not links. The graph's hash is the same on two builds, and the build time is printed. Native `matron`: 'two below' now goes down the risers when she is dangerous and by parked trolleys as a pest; 'climb' now has a pest climbing at 0.4 m/s. New sections: 'riser down' (dangerous, from 154 to a sprint on 99, with five flange stops, alive, hunting on 99 within 30 s, never more than 1.2 m off the pipe's climb line); 'riser up' (a player seen on 154 from 110); 'checkpoint reach' (it commits with her 25 s or more away and not inside that, and a death puts her back where she stood at the commit). Also `determinism` (now comparing her level and link) and `save`. Touch: `touch_matron_riser` (new, with --capture showing her on the pipe from below), `touch_matron_act` (re-staged, still meeting all three stages), `touch_matron`, `touch_matron_line`, `touch_matron_climb`, `touch_matron_ride`, `perf_grade`.

milestones.title: M4: She learns the lifts, and the whole tower played by touch
milestones.what: Decision 9 C: once she has seen the player work a vertical machine's CALL or RAISE this run, she can work it too. Route::pre_step gets a second actor, her support entity. A restore forgets this. The player hears the cascade mast coming back down for her. Then comes a long touch playthrough across the tower with her following by risers, lines, ladders, rides and the mast she called.
milestones.proof: `matron` 'called': after seeing the player ride the cascade mast up, she calls it down at the 264 band and rides it to 291, and before seeing it she never calls it. `determinism`, `save`. Touch `touch_matron_tower` (new): from 154 down the Stack to 66 by lines, back up by S3 and C3, then on to 291 by the swing, C6 and the cascade mast. Each stage is met, deaths are counted and kept under a stated number, and screenshots are taken at the flange clangs and the outside crawl.

risks: Generated walking lines meet clutter that the static sweep cannot see: forklifts parked on the deck 11 and 44 west bands at x -21.5, loose stock, and machines' dynamic bodies. Mitigation: a progress monitor (no closer in 1.5 s means sidestep inside the floor box, then refuse that edge for 20 s and plan again), the Turn's vault, and `matron-nav-soak` patrolling every level in CI.

Behavior changes ripple through the tests already built. The act's 143 beat breaks once a dangerous Matron can come down the risers. The 'climb' and 'two below' sections assumed a frail Matron cannot hold a ladder and moves one level at a time. M1 budgets a deliberate re-staging of `touch_matron_act` and these sections, rather than adding special cases to keep the old behavior.

Cross-machine determinism is not established (the owner's law, ARM phone against x86 CI). Small float differences in the build could produce a different graph on the phone. Mitigation: round to 1 cm with margins on every threshold, print and check the graph's hash, and fall back to a baked tower_nav.inc that is checked for drift in CI, like world_solids.inc.
Phone startup time for the build, and how the Jolt broadphase handles the transformed-shape gather. Measure it in `perf_grade`; bake it if it costs more than about 50 ms on the device.

Fairness: a Matron who can reach anywhere can make chases you cannot win or deaths you cannot escape. Guarded by the speeds she has on links (slower than the player's lines and machines), the pipes opening only when she is dangerous, the worth limits on heard leads, the 25 s reach-time checkpoint, and restoring her where she stood, not on top of the player. All of these numbers are CHOSEN and need tuning in play.

Two bodies on one member: the player and her on the same ladder, or the player at the pipe's head as she dismounts. Today's caught() needs her within 1.4 m vertically, and a shove while the player holds a ladder is noted as untested in the log. Rule: no hands while she is traversing, hands during the dismount, and a fully changed Matron's catch of the player's feet on the same ladder is a death. These need their own tests.
Hearing could be muffled wrongly by generated small floors (stands, cage roofs, the bridge platform) if decks_between counts them. Only levels marked as decks (more than 50 m^2) count.

Her climb line clears the flanges with a capsule that stands up to 1.1 m off a pipe's axis, so the figure must be leaned in to hug the pipe or she will read as floating beside it. That is presentation work, checked with --capture.
Riding a parked trolley as a pest uses up that line's trolley until a death or a load. That is a real consequence the player has to route around. The parachute is still the way back.
The hand-written 154 deck and 176 ring stay special (catwalk, posts, eye, unrigging). Generated levels get no posts in this design, so she patrols there instead of guarding a way up.
result.wow: On deck 99 you hear a clang far up the shaft, then another, closer, one for every deck she passes. You look over the rail and see her in the corner of the shaft, wrapped round the riser pipe 22 m above you, sliding down it and stopping on each flange with a bang, her white tunic lit by each deck's lamp, her face turned down at you. She is counting down the decks to yours.

result.name: Feet First: kick her down, never dead
result.pitch: She comes down the band at you with the music box rattling too fast on her hip, and the hint under your right thumb changes from JUMP to KICK. You flick up. Your boot rises into the bottom of the screen, time slows to a crawl as your sole lands on her tunic, and then 220 kg of the site's first-aid attendant folds over and skids across the steel while you fly back the other way and roll. A pest stays down, whimpering, and the toolbox she stole skitters loose. A dangerous Matron braces against a kick she can see coming, so you hit her from behind, drop on her from a ledge, or slide a drum into her shins. Fully changed, she shrugs off a boot to the chest, and only the world can take her legs; she gets up from every fall straight into the Turn. Each knockdown buys you seconds and costs you rage, so every fight is a choice: be safe and loud now, or face a worse Matron later. You can stop her, trip her, knock her over an edge or stomp her off a ladder, and she always gets back up.
mechanics: KICK is the up verb (swipe up, or Jump in the button scheme), offered by the native when her body is ahead of you. No new button: UpMove::Kick and its hint text KICK already exist (main_context.gd UP_HINTS) for the wall kick-off. On the ground it is offered when she is 1.1 to 2.6 m ahead, within 35 degrees of your facing, within 1 m of your height, with a clear line to her. Taking it makes a lunge kick: a low, flat hop, feet first, at your current speed plus 2.5 m/s forward and 2.0 m/s up. In the air it is offered when her chest is within 1.3 m ahead; taking it makes a kick-off from her, the wall kick-off with her body as the wall. When she is in the band, KICK beats vault and springboard.

The kick lands when your feet reach her within 0.35 s of taking it. The native pushes the two bodies apart, the way the wall kick sets velocity directly. The push along the line from you to her is mu*v_close + 85 kg*kKickPushMps (3.0 m/s, the same as kWallKickMps), where mu = 85*220/305 = 61 kg. It goes onto her as +J/220 and onto you as -J/85. You also get kWallFriction*push upward, and the stick steers you along her side up to kWallKickAlongMps, so you can tic-tac off her chest. The legs can only pass so much (kKickMaxNs, CHOSEN, about 850 N*s). Past that the knees give: you are thrown back at most 6 m/s, and she keeps the rest of her charge.

Her hands are knocked aside. For 0.4 s after a kick lands, caught() returns false, and it stays false while she staggers or lies down. A kick that misses (she moved, or you misjudged the range) is just a hop. If you land inside kCatchM of her, her hands decide by stage, as today: a shove, or a death when fully changed. Kicked from closer than 1.1 m, you are inside her arms and the kick is never offered.

Her balance (new in matron.cpp) sorts each blow into one of three kinds. FRONT: your kick, or stock hitting her above the knees. It is judged by the change in her horizontal speed, and bracing raises the bar. ABOVE: a body of 40 kg or more coming down onto her at 4 m/s or faster (a drop-kick from about 0.8 m up, or a crate off a deck above). LOW: a body whose center is under 0.6 m above her soles (a rolled drum, a reel, your slide) pushing into her with 150 N*s or more. She can brace against FRONT blows only. ABOVE and LOW blows put her down at any stage, because nobody can brace against her legs being taken or a weight from above.

STAGGERED (new state): her feet stop driving her and only brake, at 4 m/s^2 instead of kCutAccel's 30, for 0.4 to 0.9 s. A kick that carries 2 m/s drives her back about a meter in stumbling steps. DOWN (new state): her capsule is swapped for a lying one, a RotatedTranslatedShape laid along the direction she was knocked, with its underside on the floor (her body has no rotation degrees of freedom, so the shape sets the angle). While she is down, cloth-on-steel friction slows her at 4 m/s^2 (her body's own friction is 0.0). She stands back up only where shape_pose_is_clear finds room for her standing capsule. If a crate lies on her, she is PINNED and heaves it off with a bounded upward force (her strength is CHOSEN).

The stages, from STAGE (her rage), as a table of thresholds. PEST: never braces. Floored by a 1.5 m/s change. Down for 3.5 s, then she gets up slowly. DANGEROUS: braces against a FRONT blow when sees_player_ is true and you are within 50 degrees of her facing. Braced, a blow of 1.5 m/s or more staggers her and only 3.5 m/s or more floors her, which you only reach by meeting her charge. Unseen, the pest's thresholds apply. Down for 2.0 s. FULLY CHANGED: braces against every FRONT blow while facing you, and a frontal kick only staggers her (the bar is above the legs' limit). ABOVE and LOW blows floor her for 0.9 s. In every stage, an ABOVE or LOW blow floors her.

She gets up into the Turn. When she rises while dangerous or fully changed and turn_cooldown_s_ has run out, the rise is her Turn's wind-up: her spine cracks as she straightens, and the lunge follows. Fully changed, the cooldown is 4 s (kTurnCooldownChangedSeconds), so she nearly always gets up lunging.

Knockdowns cost rage. Each DOWN adds kRagePerDown directly to her rage: 0.04 as a pest, 0.06 dangerous, 0.08 fully changed. Her own body's thuds never reach her ears anyway (kOwnSoundM). Roughly nine knockdowns take a pest to dangerous, and a quiet minute (decay 0.003/s) undoes about four. Hitting her keeps her off you and makes her worse. Walt notices it on the radio before you do.

Physical consequences beyond her body: when she staggers or goes down, she lets go of any held stock (drop_stock). The toolbox flies on with her momentum, and you can take it back. Stock you send into her obeys the same rules: a slide (kSlideMinimumSpeed 5 m/s) into a 55 kg drum sends it rolling into her shins (LOW), and a 160 kg skid crate shoved off a deck edge lands on her (ABOVE, and PINNED if it comes to rest on her).

Over an edge, she catches it. If a stagger or a fall carries her center past floor support, she catches the lip she crossed (her hands, kHandsAboveCentre) and hangs. Then she climbs back over through her existing climb() and mantle (kMantleMps, kMantleOutM), using a Climb made where she went over. A pest hangs 5 s crying, then climbs slowly. Dangerous, she is up in 3 s. Fully changed, 1.2 s in jerks (kClimbBurstMps). Her grip on a lip is not yours to break, so a kick is never a kill. The one existing death stays as it is: knocked onto the catwalk, her weight shears the bolts.

STOMP is the down verb at a ladder's head when she is climbing it and her hands are within 1.6 m under the floor's edge (the 154 to 176 ladder at x 5.0, z -129.05). Your boot knocks her off the rungs. She falls to the floor at the ladder's foot, which is her own level, so she is never below kFallenBelowM and never dies of it. She lands DOWN for 2 s plus 0.15 s per meter fallen. In the Turn she climbs in jerks (kClimbBurstMps 2.2), so the stomp has to land in the pause when her hand reaches the top rung.

She learns within a run (decision 9 C, like fooled_). After two knockdowns by the same kind of blow, she guards against that kind for the rest of the run, whatever her stage. FRONT: she braces as if dangerous. ABOVE: she will not stand within 2 m under an edge you are standing on; she stops short and waits, or throws something. LOW: as a pest she stops to let rolling things pass, and in the Turn she vaults them. A restore forgets all of it, like everything else she learns.

What you see and feel, moment to moment. Taking the kick: the eye dips 8 cm, the kicking leg comes up into view from below (first_person_body.gd), and the arms swing back for balance. At contact: slow time at 0.35x for 0.25 s, easing back over 0.3 s (the launch shot's method of fewer native ticks per frame, audio slowed with it). A heavy haptic pulse scaled by the push, a dull body thud, her breath knocked out (a recorded human voice; a caption until recorded), and three wrong notes jangled from the music box on her hip cord. The camera is pushed back with the kick-off. Her reaction: staggered, she backpedals with her arms windmilling. Down, she folds, her back slaps the deck, and she slides with her arms flung wide while the box clacks along the steel (the scrape cue). Getting up as a pest: she rolls onto her side and pushes up on thin arms. Fully changed: her head turns to you first while her body is still flat, then she snaps upright with a bone crack. Over an edge: her fingers on the lip, her face under it looking up, the box ticking below her in the void. REDUCED MOTION turns off the slow time and the camera push.

The foreman's radio, captions until a person records them, each set off once by native state, never by a timer. Her first knockdown: "Did you just kick her? She's sick, Navarro. Don't hurt her, just keep her off you." Her stage rising within 20 s of a knockdown: "Whatever you're doing to her, stop. She's getting worse." Her first hang from an edge: "Don't let her fall. Please." That last line also hints at his cover-up.
grounding: src/sim/matron.hpp: Matron is a Jolt capsule: kMassKg 220, kRadius 0.30, kHalfHeight 0.75 (2.1 m), kCatchM 0.85. Its State enum (Dormant through Unrigging, 0 to 9) gains Staggered, Down and Hanging. View gains kicks/downs/trips/stomps counters, the way shoves, throws and vaults are counted today. The stage thresholds (kRageDangerousUp 0.45 and Down 0.30, kRageChangedUp 0.85 and Down 0.65), the Turn cooldowns (kTurnCooldownPestSeconds 45, kTurnCooldownSeconds 18, kTurnCooldownChangedSeconds 4) and kFallenBelowM 12 decide the scaling. Saved stays as it is: a restore puts her at her locker and forgets what she learned.

src/sim/matron.cpp constructor (lines 115-127): her body has mAllowedDOFs translation only, mFriction 0.0 and mLinearDamping 0.0. So a lying shape has to come from a RotatedTranslatedShape (the body cannot rotate), and a downed body needs its own friction.

src/sim/matron.cpp walk_toward (818-975): her feet brake knockback at kCutAccel 30 m/s^2 and plant at every edge (edge_at). A hit is erased in about 0.1 s today, which is why Staggered and Down must turn the feet off. The vault and leap paths there are where the learned LOW guard (vaulting rolling stock in the Turn) goes.

src/sim/matron.cpp step_turn (979-1000) and step_rage (1007-1040): rising into the Turn hooks onto turn_cooldown_s_, and kRagePerDown is added beside the spike term. caught() (1579-) and shove_direction() (1591) get the kick guard. drop_stock()/release_stock() let go of held stock when she is floored. climb() (773) and its mantle are reused for climbing back over a lip. post_step's kFallenBelowM check is why a ladder stomp onto her own level is never a death.

src/sim/physics_world.cpp lines 764-778: the existing caught() -> kills() / shove_ready() -> shove_player() branch is where the kick guard and the Down state take her hands away. shove_player() (1218-1228) is the model for the player's side of a kick: a stumble, landing_response_, hit_toward_. The impacts_->tick() -> matron_->hear() loop (648-656) shows why her own thuds never feed her rage (kOwnSoundM).

src/sim/physics_world_support.hpp PlayerContactListener: observe_hit skips Matron::kEntity (her body is not a blow). A new observe_matron records the hardest blow on her body each tick (the other body's momentum, the height of its center over her soles, its downward speed), picked in a total order as supports_better does, because Jolt calls contact callbacks from worker threads in no fixed order.

milestones.title: Her balance: Staggered, Down and Pinned in the native
milestones.what: Add observe_matron to PlayerContactListener (the hardest blow on her body each tick, in a total order). Add the FRONT/ABOVE/LOW classification and the Staggered and Down states with the lying RotatedTranslatedShape and cloth-on-steel friction. She stands up only where her standing capsule fits, and is pinned while stock lies on her. She lets go of held stock when hit. Stage thresholds are CHOSEN constants in matron.hpp. No player verb yet: stock is the hammer.
milestones.proof: New native group `matron-balance`: a 55 kg drum rolled at 3 m/s into a pest's shins puts her Down (LOW). The same drum at her chest while she is dangerous and braced only staggers her. A 160 kg skid crate shoved off the top of the deck's crate stack lands on her and she stays PINNED until she heaves it off. A pest knocked at 2 m/s lies 3.5 s and rises; fully changed she lies 0.9 s. A held toolbox flies free. Down never leaves her below kFallenBelowM. `matron`, `matron-mischief`, `save` and `determinism` (identical chases, comparing her state and shape) all pass.

milestones.title: KICK: the up verb against her body
milestones.what: update_up_move offers UpMove::Kick for her (a lunge kick on the ground, a kick-off in the air). The push between the two bodies, with the legs' limit, the steered tic-tac and the 0.4 s guard on caught(). Bracing by stage and sight, rising into the Turn, kRagePerDown, and the snapshot and bridge counters (kicks, downs, staggers).
milestones.proof: Native `matron-kick`: a standing pest kicked from 2 m goes Down with no shove and no death, and her held toolbox is let go. Dangerous, facing and seeing the kick: staggered at least 0.8 m, not down. The same kick from behind: Down. Fully changed, frontal: staggered only, the player thrown back at least 3 m at no more than 6 m/s, no death, no arm broken on open deck. A kick met with her Turn burst floors her while dangerous. Started from 3 m (out of range), KICK is not offered. A miss that lands inside kCatchM gets her hands. Her rage rose by exactly kRagePerDown per Down. `determinism` passes. Touch: `touch_matron_kick` (new) shows KICK as the up hint with her 2 m ahead, swipes it, and the native reports downs >= 1 and deaths == 0.

milestones.title: Edges, the ladder stomp, and what she learns
milestones.what: Catching a lip after being knocked over an edge, and climbing back through climb() and its mantle, with hang times by stage. STOMP as the down verb at the ladder's head. Learning by blow kind (two of a kind sets her guard for the run; a restore forgets).
milestones.proof: Native sections: 'edge': kicked through 143's open north rail, she catches the lip, hangs (5 s pest / 3 s dangerous / 1.2 s fully changed) and climbs back, never below kFallenBelowM. 'stomp': with her climbing the 154-176 ladder in the Turn, a stomp at the 176 ring's ladder head drops her to the 154 deck alive, Down for at least 2 s plus her fall time. 'learned': after two frontal Downs a pest braces against a third kick (staggered, not floored); after a death's restore she is floored again. 'catwalk': kicked onto the catwalk plates, the bolts shear as before (her one death stays intact). `matron`, `save`, `determinism` pass.

milestones.title: The feel: leg, slow time, haptic, sound, her body, the radio
milestones.what: The first-person kick leg and arms. Slow time at contact through launch_shot-style ticks, off under REDUCED MOTION. A haptic pulse scaled by the push. The thud, the music box's three wrong notes, and her knocked-out breath as a recorded-voice caption. Stagger, Down, slide, rise (fully changed: head first) and edge-hang poses in matron_view.gd. Walt's three lines in foreman_radio.gd.
milestones.proof: `look_matron_gallery` gains poses captured with --capture (staggered, down, rising-changed, hanging at a lip) and is checked by eye. `touch_matron_kick` asserts slow time fired (fewer native ticks per frame in the contact window, back to normal by 0.6 s), a haptic pulse at contact (it fails without one, like touch_roll), the radio's first-knockdown line shown on the plate once, and with REDUCED MOTION set, no slow time. Screenshots of the contact frame and the head-first rise.

milestones.title: Into her first act
milestones.what: Rework the act's middle so the player is never helpless against her. On her deck, the stolen toolbox is won back by kicking her down. At the ladder, when she follows in the Turn, a stomp sends her back down before the climb to 220. Tuning pass on the CHOSEN numbers from the playthrough.
milestones.proof: `touch_matron_act` (ui_test_act.gd) is extended and still fails if any beat is missing from the simulation: at least one KICK Down as a pest with the toolbox back in hand, one LOW Down from a slid drum while she is dangerous, one ladder stomp, then the climb to the 220 ring. Deaths stay within the act's budget. Stage screenshots via --capture. CI plays it.

risks: Swapping her shape mid-contact (lying capsule against a rail, stock or the cage) can push into geometry or pop her. Every swap and every stand-up needs a clear-pose test with a fallback: if lying does not fit, she stays standing and staggered.

Determinism: Jolt reports contacts from worker threads in no fixed order. The blow pick must use a total order, as the support sample does, or chases will diverge (the `determinism` check will catch it).

Her body was built to be driven only by her feet (friction 0.0, edge planting in walk_toward). A downed or staggered body slides, so the lip catch has to be robust everywhere she can stand: her deck, the 176 ring, the upper rings, the stack decks. Otherwise a kick becomes an unintended kill.
The emergent catwalk kill (knocked onto the plates, the bolts shear) is consistent with her one death, but the owner may want kicks to be strictly non-lethal. That is a choice for the owner.

Your rebound against her charge is large in real physics. Without the legs' limit (kKickMaxNs, 6 m/s rebound) a kick near the rail breaks an arm (kArmBreakHitSpeed 8.5) or throws you off the deck. Too low a limit and the kick feels limp. This needs tuning by feel on the phone.

Balance: a pest may become trivial (acceptable, she is a pest), while fully changed may feel hopeless if frontal kicks only stagger her. The ABOVE and LOW blows and the stomp must be easy to read and to find near where she hunts, which may mean laying more drums and reels on her levels.
Rage per Down may read as punishment. Walt's lines and the music box's tempo have to make the cause readable without a meter, which the owner forbids.
Verb priority: with her standing in front of a crate, KICK must beat vault and springboard predictably, or a swipe does the wrong thing at the worst moment.
Using her as a tic-tac wall could let players skip parts of the route in her act (onto cage roofs, up the ladder's head). Either accept it as intended fun or check the act's sequence.
Recorded voices: her gasps and cries and Walt's lines need real people. They stay captions until then, as with the radio today.
Slow time on a phone also slows the audio mix and may sicken some players. It must be short, and REDUCED MOTION must turn it off.
result.wow: Her Turn lunge comes at you. You jump into her burst feet first and time drops to a third: your boot sole is on her chest under her ruined face, and the music box swings up off her hip on its cord. Then she folds and skids across the deck while you're thrown back rolling the other way. You're still on the ground when her head turns to look at you, before her body moves.

result.name: Heave, Topple, Run: throw what you carry, knock her down, pay for it in rage
result.pitch: Anything you can carry, you can now heave. Hold Action and your arms draw the toolbox back to your chest. Let go and it flies along your line of sight at about 6 m/s. Hit her with it while she's a pest and she goes down in a heap across the band. The music box on her hip skips and stops, and you jump over her body and run. Every blow feeds her rage, though. Knock her down too often and she gets up dangerous, then fully changed, and at that stage she snatches your toolbox out of the air and throws it back at your head. Fully changed, only heavy things put her down: the 420 kg ingot dolly shoved down the band, or a drum dropped down the ladder shaft onto her as she climbs after you.
mechanics: THE HEAVE (the player's throw). While carrying, a tap on Action still means LET GO, so the S3 pan, the float lift's spool and every current playthrough work as before. Holding Action for 0.2 s or more turns the button to THROW and draws the load back. Releasing throws it along the view (facing plus look pitch, raised 8 degrees). The arms put in up to kHeaveWorkJ = 300 J at a full 0.6 s wind-up (CHOSEN), with a minimum draw of 0.25. Speed = min(7 m/s, sqrt(2*E*draw/m)), which gives: toolbox 18 kg 5.8 m/s, pallet 22 kg 5.2, iron pig 50 kg 3.5, drum 55 kg 3.3, gas bottle 60 kg 3.2. The feet absorb up to 150 N*s of the kick back; anything over that pushes the thrower back. Swipe down and Drop still mean PUT DOWN.

Decoys come with the heave. A thrown piece's landing is an impact-ledger hit she already hears (Matron::hear, picked by loudness at her ear): a toolbox landing at 7 m/s is about 440 J, loudness 0.65, heard about 36 m away. A throw that lands past her pulls her to the crash. Her existing wary/fooled logic wears decoys out: after two false leads she checks from a vantage point, and far noises stop pulling her off her post.

HER BALANCE (the blow). This uses the same method as the impact ledger: work out the hit from her own motion. After the physics step, her velocity is compared with what her feet set it to in pre_step. Her friction is 0, so the floor adds no sideways push. Mass times the sideways change is the blow, in N*s. On a climb, where gravity is off and climb() sets her velocity every tick, the full 3D change counts. A blow only counts on a tick when the ledger reports a hit by a tracked body (stock, forklift, crane hook) within reach of her. Her own held or thrown piece never counts, and neither does the player's body, which the ledger doesn't track. So walking into her stays as it is: her hands decide.

WHAT A BLOW DOES, BY STAGE (CHOSEN, tuned later). PEST (frail): 60 N*s or more puts her DOWN for 3.0 s, so any full heave works. DANGEROUS: 60-160 N*s makes her REEL for 0.7 s (feet off, stumbling back with the blow); 160 or more puts her DOWN for 2.0 s, so a drum or pig does it but a toolbox doesn't. FULLY CHANGED: thrown light stock she sees coming, she catches; 350 or more makes her reel for 0.5 s; 700 or more puts her down for 1.2 s. Only rams and drops are that heavy. ON A LADDER: half the threshold tears her hands off the rungs and she falls to its foot.

DOWN. Her feet stop driving. A capped floor drag of 6 m/s^2 (cloth on steel) stops the slide within about 0.75 m. Her body swaps to a low sprawled box (about 1.7 x 0.5 x 0.6 m) laid along her heading: a RotatedTranslatedShape on the same body with the same mass, so nothing teleports. Her body is a real 0.5 m obstacle you can jump or vault. caught() is false while she's down: no shove, no kill. She drops whatever she's holding. Her Turn ends and its cooldown starts over at her stage's value (45/18/4 s), so a pest knocked off the ladder can't climb again for 45 s. She stands up only where her standing capsule fits.

THE COST. Each blow adds min(0.3, 0.0015 x N*s) to her rage, on top of anything she hears. A toolbox hit adds about 0.14 and a drum about 0.27, so two drum hits take a pest to dangerous. A knockdown is borrowed against her rage. The only way to pay it back is quiet: decay is 0.003/s, so a drum's worth takes about 90 s of silence.

SHE ANSWERS (her stage and her mind). (1) Her pest mischief closes the loop. A piece you threw counts as handled, so she goes and gets it (fetch_stock) and throws it back at you (throw_stock): a pest plays catch with your toolbox. (2) Her learned sidestep. After two blows in a run (forgotten on restore, like fooled_), below fully changed, a throw she saw leave your hands that would pass within 0.8 m of her in the next 0.5 s makes her cut sideways at kCutAccel (30 m/s^2), away from the shaft's rim. A throw from out of her sight still lands. (3) Fully changed, she catches it. A piece of 70 kg or less she sees coming within 0.9 m of her hands is taken by her existing hand constraint (take_stock) and thrown straight back at kThrowMps (7.5 m/s) after a 0.2 s wind-up.

THE HIGH GROUND. She only climbs the 154-to-176 ladder in the Turn. A toolbox let go over the ladder's head falls about 11 m and hits her head at about 15 m/s (about 265 N*s); a drum hits with about 800 N*s. Either tears her off and she falls to the foot. She survives that fall, which is horror in itself, and is down, with her Turn cooldown (her only way back onto the ladder) starting over. A plain LET GO at the edge is enough: no throw needed.

RAMS FOR WHEN SHE'S FULLY CHANGED. Heavy things the player shoves by walking into them (existing) count as blows: the ingot dolly on her deck (420 kg, friction 0.06, rolls) at 1.5 m/s is about 630 N*s, skid crates are 160 kg, and the forklifts and crane hook are already tracked. Two free-rolling cable reels (180 kg, on their rims) are added: one on her deck's south band, one on the 176 ring.

READING HER WITHOUT A METER. The music box skips on every blow and goes silent while she's down. When it starts again, slow and winding up, she's getting up. How she gets up shows her stage: a pest pushes up slowly; dangerous, she rises from knees bent backward; fully changed, she comes up stiff as a plank, hinged at the heels. Reeling: her torso thrown back along the blow, arms flailing. The sounds are a body thud on steel and a bone crack. No synthesized voice: a groan, if added, will be a recorded human line.
grounding: src/sim/matron.cpp:117-127, the Matron() constructor: she is a Dynamic 220 kg CapsuleShape(kHalfHeight 0.75, kRadius 0.30) with mAllowedDOFs translation only and mFriction 0. milestones.title: M1: The heave
milestones.what: Throwing what you carry. Simulation::request_throw(draw) adds StepCommands throw_requested/throw_draw. update_carry releases the load and launches it on the 300 J energy model with the capped kick back. ImpactLedger resyncs the launched body so the throw isn't a fake hit at the hands. Touch: tap Action = LET GO as before, hold = THROW (button label changes, first-person arms draw the load back, a haptic pulse on release). Playable right away against her: thrown landings are decoys she hears, and as a pest she goes and gets what you threw and throws it back.
milestones.proof: Native SCRAPERX_ONLY=heave: a full-draw toolbox leaves the hands at 5.5-6.1 m/s and lands 4 m or more away; a drum at 3.0-3.6 m/s; no ledger hit on the launch tick and one on landing; a tap still sets the load down where it is held; a toolbox thrown toward her locker from 20 m wakes her. Native matron-mischief (unchanged), stack (S3 pan still LET GO), determinism. Touch: new touch_heave (154 m deck: PICK UP the toolbox, hold ACTION reads THROW, release facing east, carrying 0, box 4 m or more away, then a tap LET GO drops at the feet); touch_stock, touch_stack, touch_wet green (Action tap regressions).

milestones.title: M2: Down and reeling, by stage, at a price
milestones.what: Her balance: the blow read after the step in Matron::post_step, counted only with a ledger hit near her. The stage table (pest down at 60 N*s for 3.0 s; dangerous reels at 60, down at 160 for 2.0 s). State::Downed: feet off, floor drag, the sprawled box shape with a clearance check (falls back to a standing reel where it doesn't fit), no hands, Turn ended and its cooldown restarted, getting up only where the standing capsule fits. The rage cost per blow. Presentation: downed/reeling poses, the get-up by stage, the music box skip and silence, the body thud. Snapshot and bridge fields.
milestones.proof: Native SCRAPERX_ONLY=matron-bay: (a) a pest hit by a full-draw toolbox is Downed within 3 ticks with a blow of 80-110 N*s; the player standing 0.5 m away for 2 s gets no shove or catch; she is up again after 2.8-3.2 s, rage up by 0.12 or more, no deaths. (b) Downed across the north band, a sprint at her goes over her body (player feet above 154.5 m at her x), no death. (c) debug_set_matron_stage(1): a toolbox only reels her, a drum puts her down for about 2 s. (d) Four drum hits make a pest dangerous. (e) Her walking into a rail and riding Stage A's cage give no false blow. (f) A restore while she is down brings her back upright at her locker. matron, matron-collision, matron-mischief, save and determinism still pass. Touch: new touch_matron_bay (godot/presentation/ui/ui_test_bay.gd, extends ui_test_act.gd): woken, she comes along the north band, hold and release ACTION at her, native Downed, walk past within 1 m unshoved, she gets up, takes the toolbox and throws it back; a --capture pose 'downed'.

milestones.title: M3: The high ground (the ladder)
milestones.what: Blows on a climb at half the threshold tear her off: climb_ ends, gravity comes back on, she falls to the foot and is Downed on landing, her Turn cooldown started over. Ammunition added at the 176 ring's ladder head (a toolbox and a drum), laid last so saves line up. This milestone is the wow moment.
milestones.proof: Native matron-bay ladder leg: she is climbing in the Turn about 5 m up; the toolbox let go over the ladder's head from the ring hits her at 150 N*s or more; climbing becomes false; she lands at the foot alive (floor_y 154) and Downed, and as a pest she doesn't take hold again for 40 s or more. The drum tears her off when debug-set fully changed. Native stock and save: the new pieces come after the Matron's throwables and older saves still load. Touch: touch_matron_bay's second leg, taken from touch_matron_climb's route: at the head, PICK UP the toolbox, face down the ladder, LET GO, and she falls off the rungs; a --capture pose 'torn_off'.

milestones.title: M4: Her answers, and rams for when she's fully changed
milestones.what: Fully changed, she catches thrown pieces of 70 kg or less that she sees (the existing take_stock hand constraint on the 'piece in flight' slot) and throws them back at 7.5 m/s after 0.2 s. Her learned sidestep after two blows in a run (below fully changed, only for throws she saw, away from the shaft's rim; forgotten on restore). Fully changed thresholds: 350 N*s to reel, 700 to go down. Two free-rolling cable reels added (her deck's south band, the 176 ring). Gallery poses for each stage's get-up. Progress log entry; 00_START_HERE's 'never helpless' directive row marked built.
milestones.proof: Native matron-bay: debug_set_matron_stage(2): a toolbox thrown at her in sight is in her hands within 0.4 s (caught_from_air 1) and comes back (throws +1, the player's hit_count goes up). Dangerous after two blows: a third throw seen leaving the hands misses (dodges 1, her nearest approach to the piece over 0.6 m), while one thrown from behind her lands (blows +1). Fully changed: the ingot dolly shoved along the east band into her puts her down (blow of 600 N*s or more); the rolling reel makes her reel. determinism passes with a heave in its inputs. Renders: look_matron_gallery captures down, reeling and get-up for pest, dangerous and fully changed. CI's touch list gains touch_heave and touch_matron_bay.

risks: False blows: her feet pressing into a rail, a cage floor moving under her, or her own held piece could read as hits. Mitigation: count only on ticks with a ledger hit near her; skip while riding, on a line, or holding; a native leg with her walking into the rail and riding a cage must show no blow.
The ledger's last_velocity carries through the carry, so without a resync at launch every throw is a fake 300 J crash at the player's hands that she hears. That needs ImpactLedger to resync one body.

Swapping in the sprawled shape inside a rail, crate or the player can make Jolt push bodies apart hard. Mitigation: CollideShape check before the swap, falling back to a standing reel; the get-up also checks its capsule. If something stays on her (a pallet, the player standing on her) she waits, then shoves out after 2 s.

Too easy: stock is everywhere, and a pest goes down to any full heave. The counters are the rage cost, her throwing your stock back, the learned sidestep and the fully changed catch, but every number is CHOSEN and there is no device access to tune feel on the phone.

Hold-to-throw moves the Action LET GO from press to release (a delay under 0.2 s). Existing playthroughs that tap Action to let go (the S3 pan in touch_stack, the float lift's spool in touch_wet, touch_stock) have to be run again. INTO THE PAN stays let-go only.

Vaulting over her: the vault and mantle probes understand box leaves (leaf_box), which is why the sprawled shape is a box, but a 220 kg dynamic body may still be refused by some probe. A plain jump clears 0.5 m anyway, and the test asserts going over her, not which move did it.

Knock-on deaths: a blow at the catwalk's ends or an unrailed edge could slide her onto the plates or off, and she dies (the one intended way she dies, by causal physics). The capped drag keeps slides under about 0.75 m. Her 220 kg falling off the ladder onto a player at its foot is a real crushing hit under the existing hit rules, which is fair but needs to be readable.

She survives a 20 m fall off the ladder. That's consistent with today's model (only kFallenBelowM, 12 m below her level, kills her) and plays as horror, but the owner may want it to cost her something.
Voice rule: no synthesized groan for her. It ships with a thud and the music box skip; a recorded human line, if wanted, needs a recording.

Save layout: the new stock must be appended after kMatronThrowables, as lay_machine_weights and lay_matron_throwables did, or older saves stop lining up (the native save test refuses them). Matron::Saved does not change.
The 'piece in flight' throwable slot uses one of the 32 handled_ bits and an index into throwables_. Clearing it on restore and on drop_stock must be watched.
result.wow: She comes up the ladder after you in the Turn, jerking rung by rung, face turned up at you. You're standing at the head with the oil drum. You step to the edge and LET GO. It drops eleven meters down the ladder and tears her off the rungs, and she hits the deck below with a slam. The music box on her hip skips once and goes silent. Then it starts again, slow, winding up, and she gets up wrong, stiff as a plank from the heels, angrier than before.

result.name: Sight Lines: her face is her senses
result.pitch: Up close, the Matron is a real old woman's face under a white first-aid cap. Her skin is thin, with blue veins at the temples. A burn spreads across her right cheek, her lashes are thinning, and her nose bleeds and never quite stops. None of it is decoration, because her eyes are her sight lines. When her eyes find yours over the top of a crate, that is the moment she sees you. When they are turned toward some other noise, she really is not looking at you. While she has you, she stares without blinking until a tear runs. Then she blinks: the left lid comes down late and neither lid closes all the way, the whites roll up underneath, and for that third of a second you cannot be seen. After a chase she gasps with her mouth open and hears less. Then she goes still, holds her breath, and listens harder than ever. The bruise you gave her with a dropped toolbox is still on her left cheek an hour later.
mechanics: One owner for where she looks. A new native module, MatronFace (src/sim/matron_face.hpp/.cpp), is owned by Matron and stepped in Matron::pre_step at 90 Hz. Each tick it picks one thing for her to look at, from simulation facts only, in this order: the player's eyes if she saw him last tick; the loudest sound she picked this tick, after a delay that depends on her stage (0.30 s as a pest, 0.15 s dangerous, 0.08 s fully changed); her lead (heard_x_/z_, look_x_/z_); the next point on her route (target_x_/z_); and at her post, a fixed sweep across the cage mouth. Nothing in it is random. The view stops guessing: the yaw_to_player and _head_yaw lines in matron_view.gd are deleted.

Head on a neck. The head turns and tilts (yaw and pitch, relative to her body) as a two-axis spring-damper with a limited neck: head about 4.5 kg, inertia about 0.03 kg m^2, at most 10 N m of yaw torque, ±80 degrees. Stage sets how it moves: a pest turns slowly and smoothly, dangerous she turns fast, and fully changed the head overshoots and wobbles. In the Turn the limit opens to ±170 degrees, so the head facing the wrong way is real and she can then see behind her. Each eye turns on two axes up to ±45 degrees. Eyes jump to any target more than 2 degrees off, with real eye-jump timing (about 2.2 ms per degree plus 21 ms), and turn inward on close targets, which shows at half a meter.

Sight from her eyes to his eyes. sees() now casts from the simulation's eye point: her body plus a head offset for each posture (upright, stooped, all fours, climbing, clinging, peering), turned by her yaw and head angles. It keeps today's two rays kEyesHalfM apart. It casts to the player's eyes (new set_player_eyes(), which follows his crouch) and to his chest, so a single horizontal bar like ShaftRail cannot hide both. A ray only counts inside her field of view: within ±30 degrees she sees anyone; out to ±95 degrees she sees him only if he moves faster than 1.2 m/s or is within 2 m; with lids closed she sees nothing. The same gate covers sees_far_ (the 50 m catwalk commit). It works both ways: if you can see her eyes over cover, she can see yours.

Lids, blinks and tears, which decide whether she can see. Her eyes dry out until she has to blink: at rest about every 4 s. While she holds the player in sight they dry more slowly: half as fast as a pest, 0.3 times dangerous, 0.1 times fully changed, which gives stares of 8 to 40 s. Losing him sets off 2 or 3 blinks in a row. A blink lasts 0.3 s, and on the ticks both lids are closed (about 0.12 s) she sees nothing. Staring past 1.5 times the dryness that would make her blink wells up a tear in each eye (tear_s is exported, and the view runs it down the cheek at about 1.5 cm/s). Something moving at her head faster than 3 m/s from within 1.5 m makes her blink and flinch. That check is a sphere query around her head, sorted by BodyID so it stays deterministic. Exposure changes only how a blink looks: past 0.4 the left lid lags by 60 to 90 ms; past 0.75 the lids stop at 85% closed with the eyes rolled up. How long she is blind never changes, so her look follows exposure, what she does follows rage, and there is still no radiation gameplay.

Breath, which decides how well she hears. Effort from her own movement (hunt speed squared, climbing, the Turn, the cable) builds an oxygen debt that she pays back at rest over about 12 s. Debt and stage set how fast and deep she breathes. When Peering, or Guarding after a far noise (look_s_ > 0), she holds her breath for at most 25 s × (1 − debt), and ends with a gasp. Fully changed, her breathing swells and fades with 6 to 15 s stops (the breathing pattern of the dying). Her own breathing covers quiet sounds: her hearing reach is multiplied by a factor that is 1.0 at resting breath, about 0.75 when panting, and about 1.2 while she holds her breath or between breaths. At rest nothing changes from today. Each inhale, exhale and gasp is exported, so her breath sounds play in time with her chest and mouth.

Marks from what happened to her. These are looks only, but the simulation owns them and the checkpoint saves them. Twelve body areas build up wear from quantities the simulation already has: meters on all fours (palms, knees), meters climbed (palms), cable friction work, kCableFriction × kMassKg × g × across × |speed| × dt (raw forearms), vaults and leaps, hard landings (knees, chin), and hits to the head. A hit is an ImpactLedger hit within 0.35 m of her head point; its direction in the head's frame says which cheek, the brow, scalp or nose, and its energy sets how bad the mark is. The time of the last hit is kept per face area, so a bruise turns from red to purple over minutes. A hit on the nose starts a nosebleed, and past exposure 0.7 it does not stop.

Hitting her face really does something. A hit to the head kicks the neck by the piece's momentum (the speed change is the square root of 2E/m). Her head snaps aside, her gaze is knocked off the player and she blinks: she loses sight of him for about 0.3 to 0.6 s and is never hurt badly. That gives the owner's 'keep her at bay without killing her' a real move: drop something on her from the deck above, or swing a carried load into her.

Exposure on her face, as looks only, driven by view_.exposure on the existing 600 s clock. The stages follow real radiation injury, in order: pale skin and redness, dry then wet peeling skin (a wet shine), hair falling out (each hair card has its own threshold, and clumps fall when her head's turning jerks hard), bloodshot eyes, pinpoint bleeds under the skin, bleeding gums (seen when she pants), grey-violet dead skin at the center of the burn, and milky lenses that dull the highlight in her eyes. The burn is placed by an inverse-square falloff from fixed points where she handled the source (her right palm, her right hip pocket, the right side of her face), as in real lost-source accidents, so it fades the way a real burn does.

Small movements, drawn by the view from simulation inputs and timed on simulation time so they repeat exactly. A shake of 8 to 12 Hz (stronger with exposure and with oxygen debt). Chest, shoulders, nostrils and lips move with the simulation's breath phase and depth. Tiny eye jitter, which stops during a stare. During a held breath or a stop in her breathing, every sway goes still and only the shake is left. The attendant's habit: if she sees the player hurt (arm_broken) within 3 m, she gives a one-sided reassuring smile on the unburned side that never reaches her eyes.

The head, built in this container from free (CC0) assets. Start from the MakeHuman base mesh and shape targets, reachable over git: an old woman, aged further, with uneven sides, shaped in numpy. Then headless Blender 4.2 LTS (download.blender.org is reachable) subdivides it, sculpts it procedurally (fold lines, pores, sagging), and bakes normal, ambient occlusion, curvature and thickness maps onto a head of about 10k triangles. numpy then builds the skin color from melanin and blood maps, with blue vein paths at the temples, eyelids and neck, and age spots. The colors are checked against reference portraits made with Qwen-Image (Apache-2.0) through the Hugging Face connector. Also built: a roughness map, a condition texture (burn growth thresholds, pinpoint bleeds, blister normals) and area IDs in vertex colors. The export is a GLB whose blend shapes are named after the simulation's channels (eye-left/right-closure, nose-left/right-dilatation, mouth-open, mouth-compression, mouth-corner-puller, eyebrows inner-up, neck-platysma), with separate high-detail eyes, teeth, tongue, lashes and hair cards. TRELLIS (reachable) and Hunyuan3D-2 (404 through the connector) are not used: their meshes have no separate lids or blend shapes for the simulation to drive.

Rendering on Godot's Compatibility renderer, which has no subsurface scattering, no screen-space ambient occlusion, and draws every extra light as another pass. The skin shader fakes the soft look of skin with a lookup texture keyed to curvature, a blurred normal for diffuse light, two specular lobes, and light shining through thin parts (ears and nostrils glow when lit from behind), with the condition layers on top. The eye shader has a parallax iris, a dark ring around the iris, a pupil that widens when sees_player is true and stays wide late in the day, a wet edge along the lower lid, and veins in the whites. Tear strips are revealed by tear_s, and a strand of saliva stretches between her lips when her jaw opens wide. The full head is shown within 8 m, a lighter version within 25 m, and today's primitive head beyond that. The _eye_light omni light is removed. Budget for the full head: at most 8 draw calls, at most 25k vertices, and four 1024² ASTC 6x6 maps (about 2 MB).

Lighting reveals stay honest. Light changes how she looks (highlights in her eyes, light through her ears, her pupils), but never what she sees, because lamps are not objects in the simulation. The simulation turns her face into or out of the light (the work bulb at her post), and the light does the reveal.

They see in every direction with no head or lids. pre_step calls it within kSightM 9 m, and also for sees_far_ out to kCommitSightM 50 m.
