milestones.title: M7. She learns the lifts (decision 9 C)
milestones.what: Once she has seen or heard the player start a machine with their body this run (S1's scale plate, S2's shoot bolt, a vertical machine's controls), she can start it with hers. Route::pre_step takes her support entity as a second actor. A restore forgets it. The lift you sent away comes back with her in it.
milestones.proof: Native `matron called`. After seeing the player ride the cascade mast up, she starts it at the 264 band and rides it. Before seeing it, she never does. A restore forgets it. Also `determinism`, `save`, and `matron-ride-weight` re-run.

risks: The corner fit is tight: about 0.8 m from the axis with 9 cm to each edge beam, set by the square pipe's corner. If a sweep or a crossing snags, move the four pipes 0.3 to 0.4 m into the shaft in main_world.gd and regenerate world_solids.inc. CI's diff catches it, and any zipline or stock section that sweeps against the pipes is re-run.

Force-capped hands with gravity on, on a 220 kg body at 90 Hz, may jitter sideways or snag at a flange swing. Fallbacks in order: a SliderConstraint with a velocity motor on static steel (its API was checked in the vendored Jolt), then today's gravity-off drive with the knock still read from her motion. A constraint to a dynamic hold would lock the hold's rotation to her rotation-locked capsule, so dynamic holds use the opposite force instead.

The first act breaks on purpose. A pest now climbs, and the pipe reaches 143, where the act sprints under her post. touch_matron_act and the 'climb', 'two below' and 'no way' sections must be re-staged deliberately, not patched to pass. Name this to the owner.

Fairness. A Matron who can go anywhere can make deaths feel cheap. Each guard is tested: the 4 s tell, lead worth by stage, the 20 s checkpoint rule, her link speeds below the player's lines and machines, and knocks that buy time.
Bake churn and CI time. Every world edit regenerates matron_map.inc, and the headless crossings must keep the bake under a minute. Generated diffs show up in reviews.

Silly generated links (a lamp mast, a moving machine part, a member that clips a deck edge). Guarded by the restricted region, static bodies only, swept spans, an entity deny list, headless crossings, and reviewing the connectivity report before each commit.
Her 220 kg on lifts balanced for one rider can stall or reverse one. The ride table may force counterweight retunes, each proven again, and no lift may leave the player without a way on.
ARM-to-x86 determinism is still not established (rule 10). Baking takes the graph out of that risk, but her motion still runs on Jolt's floats.
Phone cost: edge rays, far sight and replans. The host perf line comes first, then the Godot profiler on the device; static-floor edge checks move to baked lookups only if needed.

Two bodies on one member (the player and her on one ladder, or the player at a pipe's head as she dismounts). caught() needs her within 1.4 m vertically, and a shove while the player holds a ladder is noted as untested. Each case needs its own test.

Rule 11: the owner dislikes ladders, so the design adds none for her. She uses the structure and the machines, and the hatch lid is stock, not a route. Voices: effort sounds must be recorded by a person. The gasps (her face up the shaft, her hand over the edge) land only as well as her face, which the owner wants realistic and uncanny; that is a separate track.
synthesis.wow: On deck 12 you lean over the shaft rail at the north-east corner to see if she followed. Three decks down, a pale face is tipped back past where a neck should go, looking straight at you. She steps over the rail and wedges herself into the corner round the pipe. It starts to knock under her hands, a deep bong at every flange, rising. The phone pulses in your palm with each handhold, because she is on the steel beside you. When her fingers curl over the flange just under your feet, you let the oil drum go over the corner. It tears her off. She shrieks down a whole storey, slams onto the flange below and hangs there. Then her face turns up to you again, and she climbs down and walks off toward another corner.

scores.proposal: Sight Lines: her face is her senses
scores.notes: The most original of the three, and the only one where her face changes the game. Her eyes are her real sight lines. A blink is a third of a second when she cannot see you. A held breath means she is listening harder. A hit to her head knocks her gaze off you, which answers the owner's ask to keep her at bay without killing her. Its grounding checks out. Matron::sees() (matron.cpp:203-226) casts two rays 0.15 m apart, with no facing and no lids, from her body center minus 0.5 m (matron.cpp:1259/1265). The view turns her head toward player_position whether or not she sees him (matron_view.gd:737, 1005), so the drawing claims a second answer to where she looks (laws 14, 22, 26). Weaknesses: it is the largest native change of the three. A limited field of view, sight from her eyes, blinks that blind her, the breath factor on her hearing, 12 wear areas and a new Saved layout mean retuning a chase that was just finished, plus a full suite run. The 12 wear areas are mostly detail no player will see. The art path assumes Blender (not installed) and a normally imported GLB. But godot/.godot is gitignored, so CI's touch playthroughs run with no import cache. Its exposure stages begin with 'redness', and the owner's later row (00_START_HERE.md, 2026-10-19 late) says 'I don't like the red skin'. Its voice plan (find or record clips) predates the owner's 'made like the climber's fear yells' (Chatterbox) direction.

scores.proposal: The Kind Face: the Matron's face up close, built for the gasp
scores.notes: Has the best scenes. The catch is held with no camera shake and her eyes scan from your left eye to your right. Her face changes when she is at the edge of the screen and snaps back when you look at her. She goes too still. A denture plate drops. The work bulb swings at the burst instead of going dark. A heartbeat haptic stops dead in the hold. The groundwork is solid: 'catches' rises in the same tick as leave_corpse (physics_world.cpp:767-773), _tear_door sets _work_light to 0 (matron_view.gd:354), BATCH_FAR_LAYER is a precedent for a cull mask (main.gd:122), and a skin lookup shader was probed under gl_compatibility. Holes: (1) Her eyes always aim at the camera, even when the simulation does not see the player, so the drawing lies about her senses. (2) It plans to rely on normal import with ETC2/ASTC, but CI's touch playthroughs never import. (3) 'Showing her standing over the body' misses that Matron::restore() (matron.cpp:1846-1909) moves her back to her locker as Emerging in that same tick, so the view has no fact for where she stood. (4) It keeps the red stage of SKIN_BLISTERED. (5) The Freesound API returns 401 without a key, and recorded voices would wait on the owner.

scores.proposal: The Pupil Check: her real face, built from CC0 human scan topology
scores.notes: The most buildable pipeline. It uses numpy and Pillow only, with no Blender. The face loads at runtime the way audio_director.gd:703-709 loads the voice clips, which is right because CI never imports. It gets into the export through include_filter (export_presets.cfg:10 is empty today). The prototype found that blend shapes take position deltas, not absolute positions. A Skeleton3D neck spreads the Turn's 2.6 rad look-back over three bones. The test follows the CI shape of footstep_contact_test (workflow line 382). The pupil check is the most story-specific adult horror in any proposal: a first-aider confirming your death with her penlight. Weaknesses: a custom .bin format where Godot's runtime GLTFDocument may already do the job. Eyes clamped onto the camera, the same honesty problem as The Kind Face. It keeps the red skin tint. The penlight's screen whiteout is a dazzle drawn by the view with no simulation behind it, which misleads. Like The Kind Face, the death scene does not handle the restore moving her to her locker in the same tick. Her breath stays on today's synthesized cue.

synthesis.name: Eye Contact: the attendant's face is her senses
synthesis.pitch: From across a deck she is a tired old site nurse in a white cap. Up close she is a real old woman's face, pale and paper-thin, with grey veins at the temples and the lost source's work spreading from her right breast pocket up her neck: dusky, waxy, wet at the center, never red, never gore. Her eyes are not decoration. They are where she is looking, and nothing else. If they are on yours over the top of a crate, she sees you. If they have turned to the toolbox you dropped, she does not. While she has you she stares without blinking until a tear runs. Then she blinks badly, the left lid late, and that third of a second is yours to run in. When she stops breathing and goes completely still, she is listening harder than ever. If her hands close on you once she is fully changed, the view stays in your dead eyes with no shake. She leans in, clicks on her penlight, checks your left pupil and then your right, smiles at one corner and whispers for you to open your eyes for her.
mechanics: THE SPINE, one owner for where she looks (Sight Lines). A new native module, src/sim/matron_face.hpp/.cpp, is owned by Matron and stepped in Matron::pre_step at 90 Hz. Each tick it picks her gaze target from simulation facts only, in this order: the player's eyes if she saw him last tick; the loudest sound she picked, after a delay set by stage (0.30 s pest, 0.15 s dangerous, 0.08 s fully changed); her lead (heard_x_/z_, look_x_/z_); her route (target_x_/z_); at her post, a fixed sweep across the cage mouth. The head sits on a neck as a two-axis spring-damper (about ±80 degrees, ±170 in the Turn). Eyes jump with real eye-jump timing (about 2.2 ms per degree plus 21 ms) and turn inward on close targets. Within 2 m of his face the eyes scan his left eye, right eye and mouth (from The Kind Face, but owned by the simulation). Exported through MatronSnapshot and get_matron_state: head, eye_point, gaze, eyes, lids, breath phase, depth and events, and tear. The view's guesses are deleted (yaw_to_player at matron_view.gd:737/1005, and _head_yaw from _hash). Her eyes are on the camera only when the simulation says she sees you.

HER EYES ARE HER SIGHT (Sight Lines, its own milestone so the chase changes once). sees() and sees_far_ cast from the eye point to the player's eyes (a new set_player_eyes() that follows his crouch) and to his chest. They keep the two rays kEyesHalfM apart, so one ShaftRail bar cannot hide both. The field of view: within ±30 degrees she sees anyone; out to ±95 degrees only someone moving faster than 1.2 m/s or within 2 m; closed lids see nothing. 'If you can see her eyes, she can see yours.'

LIDS, TEARS AND BREATH (Sight Lines). Dryness builds until she blinks: about every 4 s at rest. Holding him in sight slows the drying (half as fast as a pest, 0.3 times dangerous, 0.1 times fully changed), so she stares for 8 to 40 s. Losing him sets off a burst of 2 or 3 blinks. About 0.12 s of every blink is blind. A long stare wells up a tear, exported as tear_s. Something fast near her head (a deterministic sphere query sorted by BodyID) makes her flinch and blink. Breath: effort builds an oxygen debt. Peering, or Guarding after a far noise, she holds her breath for up to 25 s × (1 − debt) and ends with a gasp. Fully changed, her breathing swells and stops for 6 to 15 s at a time. Panting makes her hear less (reach × 0.75); holding her breath makes her hear more (× 1.2). Exposure changes only how a blink looks (the left lid lags past 0.4; past 0.75 the lids stop at 85% with the eyes rolled up), never its timing. So there is still no radiation gameplay.

TOO STILL MEANS SOMETHING (The Kind Face and The Pupil Check, made honest). The view's frozen moments are the simulation's breath holds and breathing stops. Chest, sway, eye jitter and the matron_breath cue all stop, and only a small shake is left. An old woman who never stops moving, then stops, reads as wrong. Here it also means she is listening harder.

THE HEAD, BUILT IN THIS CONTAINER (The Pupil Check's pipeline, The Kind Face's detail). tools/matron_face/build_matron_face.py runs with python3 -I using numpy and Pillow only. It fetches MakeHuman CC0 data pinned to commit a8bc2d54 from raw.githubusercontent.com, each file checked against a SHA-256: base.obj, the old-female macro target, the aging and face targets that keep today's hooked nose and hollow cheeks, the expression units and the high-poly eye. It applies an aging preset with uneven sides, cuts the head and neck (about 9k triangles) and repacks the UVs. It writes blend-shape deltas named after the simulation's channels (blink_l/r, lids_wide_l/r, jaw_open, lips_back, smile_l/r, nostril_l/r, neck_cords, brow_inner_up) plus custom ones (jaw_unhinged, burn_sink, denture_drop). Then a numpy bake: the high mesh is the low mesh displaced, so baking is exact in UV space. It produces a normal map from fields of wrinkles (forehead lines, crow's feet, lip lines, neck rings) and pores, with curvature and thickness in vertex colors (fwidth() curvature was shown to leave grey creases). Also a pale albedo built with no photos, a condition mask (R distance from the source, G spot thresholds, B veins, A the order her hair falls out), and the skin lookup table. Code also makes her own brown lower teeth, a too-white upper denture, the tongue, lashes, about 120 alpha-scissor hair cards and the white first-aid cap. Output is a GLB plus PNGs in godot/presentation/life/matron_face/, loaded at runtime by GLTFDocument, the same way the voice clips are loaded. That needs no import cache, which CI's touch playthroughs never have. Its .import is set to keep, so the raw file ships. If GLTFDocument drops the blend shapes, the fallback is The Pupil Check's .bin. Blender and TRELLIS are not needed: TRELLIS gives a fused mesh with no lids or mouth to animate.

SHADERS ON THE COMPATIBILITY RENDERER (all three). matron_skin.gdshader's custom light() reads the skin lookup table by N·L and the baked curvature. A thickness-weighted back-scatter makes ears, nostril rims and eyelids glow when a lamp is behind her. Roughness carries wetness (lips, lid rims, the weeping burn). An object-space version of the shader covers her hands and forearms, so a real head does not sit on clay arms. matron_eye.gdshader: a cornea shell at roughness 0.02 for catchlights, a parallax iris, an old person's grey ring around the iris, a yellowed white with veins, a wet strip along the lower lid, and a pupil uniform. The amber emissive eye_glow (ffc04a at 2.2), the comb teeth, the mouth_dark blob and the _eye_light omni light are all removed.

NO RED SKIN (the owner's 2026-10-19 late row). _apply_exposure stops tinting all her skin toward SKIN_BLISTERED c4705a. Her base skin is pale and thin, greying only late. The source's work is local and one-sided: she picked it up with her right hand and carried it in her right breast pocket. It follows real radiation injury, in muted colors. Exposure 0.2 to 0.45: dusky mottling on the right side of her neck and cheek, cracked lips, a blood patch in the white of her right eye. 0.45 to 0.7: a waxy, weeping shine, pinpoint bleeds, veins showing, thinning hair at the right temple. 0.7 to 1.0: a grey-violet, sunken center (burn_sink), peeling edges, the right brow and lashes gone, a milky right lens, one pupil wider than the other. The burn covers at most 25% of her face. Hair cards drop out in the mask's order. In the Turn's wind-up a clump falls and stays on the deck (a pool of 12), so you find grey hair on a rail before you see her.

HER STAGE ON HER FACE (The Kind Face). Pest: a kind closed smile that never reaches her eyes, with no crinkle at the corners. If he is hurt (arm_broken) within 3 m, she gives a one-corner reassuring smile with her head tilted. Dangerous: the smile drops, the lids stop following her eyes so white shows above the iris, and her nostrils flare. Fully changed: the jaw hangs and the denture plate drops 3 to 5 mm from the gum. The burned-side eye drifts outward while her seeing eye stays locked on him. Breathing follows the dying pattern, from the simulation. Where you look (presentation only, changes nothing she senses): within 5 m, with her face more than 20 degrees off the screen center, her jaw sags and one side of the smile falls. Swing the view onto her and she is composed again within three frames.

KEEP HER AT BAY (Sight Lines). An ImpactLedger hit within 0.35 m of her head point kicks her neck by the piece's speed change (√(2E/m)). Her gaze is knocked off him and she blinks, so she loses him for 0.3 to 0.6 s and is never badly hurt. Drop something on her from the deck above, or swing a carried load into her, all by touch. A bruise forms on the struck side and its age is kept in Matron::Saved, turning from red to purple over minutes. Wear is trimmed to what reads on screen: palms, knees and forearms (cable friction work, from kCableFriction 0.3).

LIGHT THAT SHOWS HER (The Kind Face and The Pupil Check). At the burst the caged work bulb is knocked loose and swings on its cord instead of going dark, so her face is lit, then dark, then lit again a little closer. A dim catchlight on a render layer only her corneas carry (the cull-mask technique of BATCH_FAR_LAYER) replaces _eye_light: in the dark you see two small wet glints at head height, not glowing eyes. Under the StackLamps her eye sockets stay black until she tilts her face up. Her penlight is clipped to her right breast pocket. It lights only during Peering and the death scene, casts no shadow and never dazzles the player. Light changes how she looks, never what she sees.

THE FIRST-AIDER'S CHECK (The Kind Face's hold plus The Pupil Check's penlight). A fully changed catch restores her to her locker in the same tick (physics_world.cpp:767-773, matron.cpp:1846-1909). So the simulation stamps a catch pose (where she stood and her yaw) in count_catch, and the view draws her there from a fact instead of inventing it. The view stays in the corpse's eyes: no pull-up, no shake, world audio down 18 dB. She leans in to 0.3 to 0.4 m. Her eyes converge and scan yours. The penlight clicks on (a machine sound): left eye, then right. A one-corner smile, a late-lidded blink, and a whispered line such as 'Can you hear me, love? Open your eyes for me.' The light clicks off, then the existing pull-out runs. At most 3.2 s; a tap skips it; after the second catch in a session it shortens to 1.0 s. _haptic(&"death") moves to the cut. A heartbeat haptic runs from 70 to 120 bpm while she sees him within 4 m, keeps going through her stillness and stops completely during the check. The shove (pest, dangerous) holds her smiling face close for 5 frames.

HER VOICE (the owner's 2026-10-19 late row). A new src/voice/generate_matron_voice.py is made like generate_fall_voice.py: Chatterbox (MIT) with an older woman's reference voice from a model trained on public-domain recordings, every take checked by Whisper. It makes 4 to 6 short attendant lines ('There now.' 'Hold still for me.' 'Open your eyes for me.'), a hum, and breath, gasp and swallow clips cut from takes. They replace sound_bank.gd's synthesized _matron_breath, timed by the simulation's breath events. A loudness envelope per clip drives her lips and jaw. The licences page gets the clip note and a MakeHuman CC0 line.

PHONE COST. The full head is shown within about 10 m (visibility_range with hysteresis): at most about 14k triangles and at most 8 draw calls, against about 35 for today's head of separate blobs. A 1.2k-triangle version with a plain material runs to 30 m, then today's primitive head. Maps: a 2048 normal, the rest 1024. They are uncompressed at runtime, about 10 MB, halved on the LOW preset (settings_store.gd QUALITY_PRESETS), until a CI import step allows ASTC. No shadowed lights come from her. The face script is skipped when she is not visible. All of the view's variation goes through _hash or simulation time, so captures repeat. The target is 45 FPS sustained on the Fold 6 (law 28), and only the device proves it (law 29).
grounding: godot/project.godot:40-43: rendering_method and rendering_method.mobile are both gl_compatibility; import_etc2_astc=true; viewport 2160x1856. So there is no subsurface scattering, SSAO or SSR, and the skin light() and baked maps are required.

src/sim/matron.cpp:203-226 Matron::sees(): two rays kEyesHalfM (0.15 m) apart with no facing or lids. matron.cpp:1258-1265 casts them from her body center minus 0.5 m (kStandCentre is 1.05, so 0.55 m above her soles) to the player minus 0.3 m, within kSightM 9 m and, for sees_far_, kCommitSightM 50 m.

src/sim/matron.cpp:1174-1207: the pick() lambda and player_carry against kFullHearingM 55 m, where a breath factor would multiply her reach. matron.cpp:1295-1300: fooled twice, a far noise only turns her head (look_x_/look_z_/look_s_ = 3 s), which is the existing seed of a gaze target.

src/sim/matron.hpp:379-425: View has sees_player, stage, exposure, turn and target_x/z but no head, gaze, lids or breath. Saved holds {state, strain_s, rage, stage, exposure_s, handled}, so bruise ages would join it. matron.hpp:136-139: 220 kg capsule, radius 0.30, half-height 0.75. matron.hpp:233: kCableFriction 0.3.

matron_view.gd:519 and :587 eye_glow is emissive ffc04a at 2.2 (the 'Halloween' eyes). :570-583 a mouth_dark blob and 18 tooth blobs. :611 the scarf. :676-681 _eye_light, an OmniLight3D with range 5, energy set at :1063. milestones.title: 1. A real old woman's face, no more Halloween
milestones.what: Write tools/matron_face/build_matron_face.py: pinned MakeHuman CC0 files with SHA-256 checks, the aging preset, the head and neck cut, UV repack, blend-shape deltas, the numpy bake (normal, curvature and thickness, pale albedo, condition mask, skin lookup table), the code-made teeth, denture, lashes, cap and hair cards, and the GLB and PNG export. Add matron_face.gd (GLTFDocument runtime load, the jaw driven as a blend shape, LOD by visibility_range, today's head as the far version) plus matron_skin.gdshader and matron_eye.gdshader. It replaces matron_view.gd:568-613 under the centre pivot. Remove eye_glow, the comb teeth, mouth_dark and _eye_light. _apply_exposure loses the red tint. Eyes face forward with the head unless sees_player is true, and then look at the camera (no guessing). Add the licences line and the export include.
milestones.proof: godot --headless --path godot --script res://tests/matron_face_test.gd prints MATRON_FACE PASS lines: the GLB loads with no import cache; every named blend shape is present; the bounding box is unchanged with every weight at 1 (guarding against the absolute-position mistake); at most 14k triangles and 8 surfaces. Rerunning the tool reproduces the committed hash list byte for byte. look_matron_gallery under Xvfb with gl_compatibility writes matron_face_* at 1.3 m and new matron_face_close_* at 0.4 m in day and night light. A pixel check confirms a back-lit ear is brighter than the cheek on the same side, and no frame's mean skin hue falls in SKIN_BLISTERED's red band. touch_matron_act, touch_matron, touch_matron_climb and touch_matron_line pass unchanged. unzip -l on the CI APK lists the face files. The owner reviews the close-ups.

milestones.title: 2. Where she looks belongs to the simulation
milestones.what: Native MatronFace: the gaze target picker, the head on a spring neck, eye jumps with real timing, inward-turning eyes and the face scan, with lids and breath modeled. All of it is exported (head, eye_point, gaze, eyes, lids, breath events, tear) through MatronSnapshot and get_matron_state. sees() and hearing are deliberately untouched, so her decisions do not change. The view drives head, eyes, lids and chest from these keys and times the breath cue on the simulation's inhale events. yaw_to_player and _head_yaw are deleted.
milestones.proof: A new native group, SCRAPERX_ONLY=matron-face. On every tick she sees him, her gaze point is within 0.3 m of his eyes. After a crash she hears, her gaze reaches it within her stage's delay, give or take a tick. Her sweep at the post is the same in every run. Groups matron, matron-collision, matron-mischief and determinism pass with the same results as before. A new look_matron_eyes scenario confirms the drawn eye centers are within 0.12 m of eye_point and the drawn gaze passes within 0.1 m of the gaze point, for every posture. grep finds no head or eye code in matron_view.gd that reads player_position.

milestones.title: 3. Alive, and wrong
milestones.what: Presentation only. A small shake that grows with exposure. Chest, nostrils and lips moved by the simulation's breath. Stillness on its breath holds, with the breath cue muted. Faces by stage (the kind smile, the one-corner smile when he is hurt, lids that stop following, the dropped denture, the drifting burned-side eye, the dying breath). The edge-of-screen change. The exposure progression on her face and hands, in muted colors with no red, covering at most 25% of her face. Hair cards that fall out, and Turn clumps that stay on the deck. The swinging bulb at the burst. The cornea-only catchlight. Black eye sockets under the StackLamps.
milestones.proof: matron_face_test cases on injected data. Across an exposure sweep the right cheek gets darker and greyer at each step while the left cheek stays within 10% of its value at 0. Burn coverage stays at or under 25% of face texels. The hair-card count only falls. touch_matron_act logs at least one still moment in the pest segment, with zero matron_breath cues inside it, and pest smile weight above 0.5. A clump of hair is on the deck after the first Turn. --capture writes act_burst_bulb_0..5 with face brightness alternating bright and dark. A night gallery frame lit only by the catchlight shows two glints and face brightness under 5%.

milestones.title: 4. Her eyes are her sight
milestones.what: sees() and sees_far_ cast from eye_point to the player's eyes (set_player_eyes, following his crouch) and his chest, gated by her field of view. Closed lids blind her. Dryness holds back blinks during a stare, she blinks in a burst on losing him, tears well, and a fast object near her head makes her flinch. The breath factor multiplies her hearing reach. The chase and its tests are retuned. The snapshot layout changes, so the full native suite runs once.
milestones.proof: matron-face cases. A player standing still 4 m behind a guarding Matron is unseen for 5 s. Walking beside her at 1.5 m/s he is seen; standing still there, he is not. Crouched behind a 1.0 m crate he is unseen; standing, he is seen. Held in sight for 20 s at 5 m she blinks at most twice and a tear appears, then blinks at least twice within 2 s of losing him. On every tick both lids are at least 95% closed, sees_player is false. After a 10 s full-speed hunt, a walking noise at her resting reach goes unheard. After 30 s of Peering, a creep at 1.15 times that reach is heard. Determinism is bit-for-bit. touch_matron_act passes after retuning. The full native suite passes once.

milestones.title: 5. Keep her at bay
milestones.what: A head hit from the ImpactLedger near her head point kicks her neck, knocks her gaze off and forces a blink. The bruise forms on the struck side and its age is saved in Matron::Saved. Wear shows on her palms, knees and forearms from climbing, crawling and cable friction.
milestones.proof: An 18 kg toolbox dropped from 3 m onto her head point: her head turns faster than 3 rad/s, sees_player is false for at least 0.25 s, a bruise appears on the struck side, and she lives. A checkpoint restore brings back the bruise ages exactly, and the save group passes. In touch_matron_act, played by touch only, the climber carries a piece to the edge above her and LET GO knocks her gaze off him (sees_player false for at least 0.25 s) and leaves a mark.

milestones.title: 6. The first-aider's check, and her voice
milestones.what: count_catch stamps her catch pose. main_feel runs the check when 'catches' rises: the view stays in the corpse's eyes, no shake, the duck, her lean-in, eye scan, penlight on each eye, one-corner smile, late blink and whisper, the click off, then the pull-out. At most 3.2 s, a tap skips it, 1.0 s after the second catch. _haptic(&"death") moves to the cut. The heartbeat haptic is added and the 5-frame shove close-up is added. src/voice/generate_matron_voice.py makes her lines, hum, breath, gasp and swallow with Chatterbox, checked by Whisper. These replace the synthesized _matron_breath, with lips driven by each clip's loudness envelope.
milestones.proof: touch_matron_act asserts that one check runs at her fully changed kill. During it, head_world_position() is within 5 degrees of the camera's forward direction and nearer than 0.45 m, and the penlight lights her left target, then her right. haptic_counts[&"death"] lands at least 0.85 s after the catch frame and haptic_counts[&"heart"] is above 0 while she sees him within 4 m. The respawn still comes within 3.5 s, and a scripted tap ends the check early. touch_lethal_feedback (a death not caused by her) keeps its timing. Every generated line passes Whisper, and the fall voice and its test are untouched. --capture writes act_changed_check frames for the owner.

milestones.title: 7. Fits the phone
milestones.what: Tune the LOD distances. The LOW preset halves the maps and drops hair alpha-to-coverage. Add a look_matron_budget scenario. Optionally add a CI import step for ASTC maps. Add an evidence row in 00_START_HERE.md.
milestones.proof: look_matron_budget reads RenderingServer's rendering info with her face filling the frame: at most 8 extra draw calls and at most 16k extra primitives, with the LODs switching at the set distances. The CI APK builds and contains the face files. The evidence row says the Fold 6 frame time is not yet measured until the owner's device shows 45 FPS sustained at the check and at the burst (laws 28 and 29).

risks: Milestone 4 changes the chase. A field of view, sight from her eyes, blinks that blind her and the breath factor on her hearing will need tests and tuning redone (touch_matron_act, the matron groups) and one full native suite run for the snapshot and Saved layout. Milestone 2 deliberately ships her gaze with her decisions unchanged, so the project can stop there if the retune goes badly.

Her capsule is always upright and 2.1 m tall while her drawn head moves by posture (about 0.95 m up on all fours). The eye point and the head-hit zone come from offsets per posture, checked against the drawing by look_matron_eyes. Something landing on the empty top of the capsule counts as a hit on her back.

A mannequin instead of uncanny. The MakeHuman base is clean and generic, and the Compatibility renderer has no subsurface scattering or SSAO, so the skin can look like wax. Realism rests mostly on motion the container can build exactly (eye jumps, breath, shake, lids that follow her eyes), on uneven sides and on baked maps. The owner reviews close-ups at every milestone, and the aging and texture settings are numbers in the tool, quick to rebake.

Runtime loading has to be proven: GLTFDocument must keep the blend shapes and the skin in the Android export template, and the raw GLB must ship (importer set to keep, checked with unzip -l). The fallback is The Pupil Check's .bin. The textures are uncompressed (about 10 MB) until a CI import step allows ASTC.

The death scene depends on a new catch-pose fact from the simulation. Without it the view would have to invent her position, because a restore moves her to her locker in the same tick (laws 22 and 26). The scene also delays the retry, so it is capped at 3.2 s, skippable by tap and shortened after the second catch.

Voice. Chatterbox produces speech well, but its breaths and swallows are unproven. It also needs an older woman's reference voice whose training data is public domain, checked the way en_US-john was. The fallback is the owner recording a few takes, which would block milestone 6's audio but none of the visuals.

Taste. Radiation injury can tip into gore, and the owner rejected red skin. The burn is held to muted, documented signs, at most 25% of her face, no open tissue, and blood only in one eye and at the gum line. The edge-of-screen change could read as a bug, so it stays subtle and goes to owner review.

Her body is still primitives, and the owner said she is 'too thin'. A real head on a stick body will widen that gap. The same MakeHuman CC0 body and skin shader are the natural next design, so milestone 1 keeps the neck and collar ready to join a real body.
Phone performance cannot be measured from here. In this renderer every light near her face adds a pass, so the draw-call and triangle budgets are only proxies until the Fold 6 run (law 29).

Determinism. The new springs and oscillators add floating-point state, and ARM against x86 is still unproven. They use only dt-integrated simulation state and std:: math, and the determinism group covers them.
Merge risk. Other sessions have been active on the Matron files (one proposal saw the working tree change under it), so each milestone lands as its own commit on ScraperX-Claude after a rebase.
synthesis.wow: You lean out from behind a column at dusk. A meter and a half away she stands completely still, not breathing. A single tear runs down her cheek, past the waxy grey patch climbing her neck, because she has not blinked since she lost you. Her eyes are already on yours. It is not a camera trick: the moment you could see her eyes, she could see you. Then her lids come down, the left one late and neither all the way, the whites rolling up underneath. For that third of a second you cannot be seen, and you run.

scores.proposal: Live Steel: the tower carries her weight, and yours
scores.notes: The most physical and the most ambitious of the three. Its gait clock is right: footfall rate comes from her speed, about 2 to 3 Hz. P2 and P3 instead inherit matron_view.gd's 0.385 m hunting step, which at kHuntMps 6.8 gives about 17.7 footfalls a second. I checked its grounding and it holds. The shaft rail is a single bar 1.05 m over each deck (world_solids.inc, y 12.05 over deck 11), with posts every 8.5 m and no toe board, so low stock can walk under it. The lamp fittings sit at x +-16.4, z -150, y 13.6+22k. check_hang_grip (traversal.cpp 700-723), kLedgeGripMaxForceN 4500, matron_loudness (movement.cpp 1193) and the apply_wind gust (sin t/7.3, t/2.9) are all as it describes. The cost is three new native systems (StructureField, Physiology, Daylight), plus a change to the save layout for the hour. The bay sway it feeds into support velocity would reach every route above 176 m through track_support_jolt. Grip pump and breath loudness would rebalance hang tests and the act that pass today. Putting light into her sight is an owner-level change: it raises the law 9 question of committing the hour, and it adds a new gesture, the two-finger tap. Ideas worth grafting: breath as a sound she hears; the felt acceleration as a native number; stock under the single rail; the haptic scheduler; the long-fall whistle; tower sway above 500 m; the modal field as a later upgrade.

scores.proposal: Through the Steel (P2: steel and air paths, the Her bus, rings going dark)
scores.notes: Strong presentation design with accurate grounding: decks_between at 228, carry_m at 271, and the thrown_entity hearing loop at physics_world.cpp 648-656 are where it says. Its best parts: the Steel bus band-passed to 250-900 Hz, so a phone speaker can play it; a Her bus that is never ducked, with the 14 dB duck during her Windup; eye-shine with exposure; a HAND FEEL setting with a cap of about 6 pulses a second; a presence.gd module, so matron_view.gd and main_feel.gd stop growing. It also states the symmetric rule well: if you can hear her, she can hear you. Weaknesses: footfalls every 0.385 m while hunting at 6.8 m/s come to about 17.7 events a second, which means a haptic buzz and a near-continuous bed of kicks. The lamps she smashes are presentation state worked out from her position, with no bodies and no saved state, so they risk law 26 (presentation as a second authority) and law 20. 'Ring lamps lit once stood on' is presentation memory that a load cannot restore.

scores.proposal: Through the Steel (P3: tremor, work lamps as stock, STORY time)
scores.notes: The spine. Its grounding is the most precise: her post at (-10.3, -129.0), 143's north gap at ACT_GATE (-6.8, -132.2), the rail openings, _cracks_due at audio_director 1118 reused for the speed-of-sound delay, and the act's own beat crouched on 143. Its work lamps are real loose stock, so light moves when hit and needs no new saved state. STORY time follows the saved checkpoint height plus her saved exposure, which reflects playing time and avoids the law 9 problem. The headlamp switches on by itself (law 27). The 3 s rattled window stops the rage loop and is cleared on restore. Its proofs sit on the existing touch_matron_act. Weaknesses: the same 0.385 m hunting step, about 17.7 kicks a second, which contradicts its own risk note of 2.5 a second. It says 'Heavy' for the impact sound that is called HeavySteel. A pest's kick (0.8 x 0.25 strength, 6 m radius) reaches her three throwables at z -125, 4 m from her post (loose_stock.cpp 579-585), so it can shift touch_matron_act. Breath and fear stay in the presentation, so nothing the climber's body does reaches her.

synthesis.name: Through the Steel
synthesis.pitch: The tower is one body of steel, and she is in it with you. You feel her steps as a soft thump in the phone before you hear them, one per step at a real walking pace, from a deck above or a deck below. Each one shakes rust down from the deck seams, and the toolbox beside you hops on the plate. When she turns dangerous, light things start to walk: a gas bottle by the rail opening chatters and tips, and a lit work lamp rolls under the single shaft rail and falls, its beam sweeping each deck it passes, until the clang comes up late from far below. The sun sets as you climb. Your headlamp clicks on, and the rings you climbed stay lit beneath you. Your body is part of the simulation too: your heartbeat beats in your palm, your forearms pump on a long hang, and your breathing is a real sound she can hear. When she stops overhead and holds her breath to listen, you hold yours, for as long as your lungs allow.
mechanics: One native authority for her steps (law 22). A gait clock in Matron::walk_toward (where stride_ already grows at matron.cpp 974) fires a footfall when its phase wraps, only while the floor ray finds a floor. Cadence comes from speed: f = clamp(1.3 + 0.32*speed, 1.3, 3.4) Hz, so a shuffle at 1.0 m/s is 1.6 Hz, a search at 2.4 is 2.1 Hz, and the hunt at 6.8 caps at 3.4 Hz (CHOSEN). This replaces the presentation rule of a step every 0.385 m while hunting, which comes to about 17.7 events a second. Rung footfalls come every 0.3 m in climb() (matron.cpp 815). Landing footfalls come from her vertical speed at touchdown after a vault or leap. The force is 220 kg x g x a factor by stage: pest 1.1, dangerous 1.8, fully changed 2.4, a Turn burst 3.0. Each event carries a sequence number, kind, place, force_n, decks (decks_between from her feet to the player), carry_m (carry_m to the player's ear: the symmetric rule, if you can hear her she can hear you) and felt_mps2. felt_mps2 = F/18 t x exp(-d/8) x 0.6^decks x contact, where contact is 1 with feet or hands on the tower's steel and 0 mid-jump, on the chute or on the ground. It is a declared reduced-order model (law 25). The events sit in a ring of 16 like the ImpactLedger, exposed through MatronSnapshot, get_matron_state and a new get_footfalls.

Presence in the presentation (new life/presence.gd, so matron_view.gd and main_feel.gd stop growing). The native footfalls replace matron_view's stride/STEP_M step rule. Her fast visual scrabble can stay as audio-only texture on her own deck within 10 m. AIR path, on her deck: a pest's dragged slipper, a dangerous heel strike plus a new deck_ring clip (struck plate modes at 310 to 1,900 Hz, broad and fast-damped, never a 'ting'), and when fully changed, hands and feet slapping with a knock of bone. STEEL path, decks 1 or more: only the deck_ring 'dunk', on a new Steel bus band-passed to 250-900 Hz, because a phone speaker cannot play the boom; the haptic carries the low end. A footfall haptic fires from log(felt_mps2) above 0.05 m/s2. On her deck within 10 m the camera dips 4-15 mm and returns to exactly zero. When the player is one level below within 25 m, pooled CPUParticles3D drop rust and grit from the underside of her floor (floor_y - 0.55) over her feet.

Her breath by stage, which closes handoff item 2. Pest: one breath every 2.0 s, wet and tired, sometimes humming the music-box tune. Dangerous: every 1.2 s, ragged, with a rattle. Fully changed: every 0.8 s, clicking, with silences of 3-6 s from a deterministic hash. While she is Peering (kPeerSeconds 2.5) she draws a breath and holds it, then lets it out long. With decks between, her breath also goes to the Steel bus. During her Windup (0.9 s) within earshot, the Ambience and Effects buses duck 14 dB in 0.1 s. Her cues live on a new Her bus that is never ducked, and the Lunge's shriek brings the world back.

The tower answers. On each footfall, LooseStock::tremor runs in table order (deterministic) before physics_system_.Update. It acts on pieces of 100 kg or less, not held by her or the player, not machine parts, and not her three throwables while she is a pest, whose centers are within 6 m and 0-2.5 m above her floor. Each gets kick_up = 0.6 m/s x max(0, F/F_dangerous - 0.65) x (1 - d/6), plus 0.12 m/s sideways from a hash of (entity, footfall sequence), so pieces walk. A pest kicks nothing, so a quiet climber keeps a quiet tower and her stage can be read from the stock. At 3.4 Hz or less these are hops, not a vibrating bed. Rattled pieces are not sounds to her for 3 s: a rattled() check beside thrown_entity() in the hearing loop at physics_world.cpp 652, cleared on restore as drop_stock is. The chatter makes real ledger hits, so update_impacts plays it with no new audio path.

Stock added freely, in one batch appended after lay_matron_throwables so older saves line up. A new Kind WorkLamp: a 14 kg top-heavy tripod with an emissive head and a light child in stock_view.gd. Four go along her patrol on 154, one beside the rail opening at the catwalk's east end; two on 143; two on the 176 ring. Gas bottles stand on end by 154's rail openings and 143's 3.3 m north gap. Scaffold tube offcuts (9 kg, they roll) and bolt buckets (12 kg) go on the shaft rims of 143 and 154 and the 176, 198 and 220 rings. A crew hard hat (0.4 kg) and a site radio are the crew's signs that Brenner's fifth line waits for. The single shaft rail (1.05 m, posts every 8.5 m, no toe board) lets round and low things walk under it into the shaft.

Moments of scale. Impact cues and her far cues beyond 25 m start after distance/343 s, capped at 2 s, through the _cracks_due delayed list. The fastest tracked body falling faster than 12 m/s within 80 m carries a 3D air-rush whistle. A Shaft reverb bus takes cues whose source or listener is in the open core (|x| < 17, |z + 150| < 17). A lit work lamp that goes down the shaft keeps its light, so its beam sweeps each deck as it tumbles.

Your body, read from native facts (body_fear.gd). Dread comes from her carry_m and felt_mps2, how aware she is (hunting 1.0, searching or peering 0.8, shuffling or guarding 0.5), a stage bias, sees_player, the Turn, the fall danger, a teeter, a drop of 25 m or more under the view (get_surface_below), and a limp or broken arm. It is exactly 0 when she is dormant, dead or out of reach and nothing else is dangerous. It rises over 0.3 s and falls over 6 s to exactly zero. From it: a heart rate of 68-155 bpm (effort raises it too); a procedural lub-dub with a 200-400 Hz knock from dread 0.3; a heart double-pulse haptic from dread 0.55; the FOV narrowing by 4 x dread squared degrees; a HUD vignette that beats with the heart; a low-pass on the Ambience bus closing from 20 kHz to 1.8 kHz; trembling hands within first_person_arms' anchored_error bound. Under REDUCED MOTION the FOV, sway and dip terms are off; the vignette and haptics stay.

Honest grip. HandSnapshot and get_hand_state gain grip_share (|hang_arms lambda|/dt over 4500 N x the arm scale) and tear_share (the over-grip impulse over 350 N*s x the arm scale), the numbers check_hang_grip already computes. A catch fires a grip haptic and a view jolt scaled by its peak. While tear_share is above 0.5, a 70 ms flutter says your fingers are going. A still hang (about 0.17) shows nothing.

Dusk to night with playing time. A new STORY time of day is appended to TIME_OF_DAY_NAMES and becomes the default for new settings only. The hour follows the committed checkpoint's height (Snapshot checkpoint_position.y, saved): grade 15:00, 154 m 17:30, the 220 ring 18:30, 264 m 20:00, 400 m 22:30, 750 m 04:30, the top at 803 m 05:50, first light as you top out. Her saved exposure adds 0.5 h per 10 minutes she is out. The hour eases at most 1 game hour per real minute, never goes back within a session, and a load gives the same sky. It stays presentation-only, as sky_cycle.gd says. City glow is a warm band low on the night horizon. The headlamp is a SpotLight3D on the camera (28 degrees, 30 m, warm) that switches on with a click when the day factor drops below 0.35, with no button (law 27), and casts shadows only at HIGH and above. Grit and dust motes catch in its beam. Her eyes catch a wet highlight in the beam, and the existing _eye_light glows paler as her exposure passes 0.5: her look only. The rings lit behind you: ring_lamps.gd lights the fixed fittings of every level at or below the committed checkpoint (worked out from saved state), with the 6 nearest as pooled OmniLights and the rest emissive. Sparks: HeavySteel, Container and Machine ledger hits of 150 J or more throw a pooled burst (4) and, at night, a 0.1 s flicker light (pool of 2).

Your breath is a sound (native Physiology, src/sim/physiology.hpp/.cpp). Exertion from mechanical power (m*g*v_up climbing, a running cost by speed, the hands' isometric load) builds an oxygen debt that pays off at rest. Breath rate and depth follow the debt, as inhale and exhale events in the Snapshot. Breathing joins the max in matron_loudness at 0.03-0.15, which carries 1.6-8 m on her level and never through a deck. Held breath: crouched, feet under 0.3 m/s, her carry within 15 m, so the climber holds it (loudness 0) for up to 9 s less the debt. Then comes a release whose loudness grows with the debt: holding after a sprint ends in a gasp she can hear. Grip pump: rises with hand load times time (about 60 s of dead hang to full) and recovers on your feet. It is felt first (strain pulses quicken, forearms tremble). It lowers the grip, to as little as 0.6 x kLedgeGripMaxForceN, only behind a CHOSEN flag turned on once the hang tests pass with it. Native breath events drive audio_director's breath in place of its foot-speed proxy, so what you hear is what she hears (law 14). The physiology is not saved: a load starts with a rested body.

Haptic budget for one motor. A scheduler in main_feel.gd orders pulses by priority (footfall < heart < grip and strain < land, slip, death, break), allows at most 6 sent pulses a second, and interleaves inside the 50 ms gap, because vibrate_handheld replaces the previous vibration. It falls back to pulse length alone where amplitude is not supported. A HAND FEEL setting (off, subtle, full) sits under VIBRATION.

Later, when the feel calls for it: Live Steel. A modal StructureField replaces the felt_mps2 formula and the tremor kick, giving the same bridge fields. Each Stack deck gets 8 bays (spans between the columns at x 0/+-26 and z -124/-150/-176, with the rim free) and each ring gets 4. Stack bays have a 3.0 Hz vertical mode at 2% damping. Rings have a 2.0 Hz vertical mode and a 1.1 Hz sideways mode at 1%. Each bay is integrated exactly in discrete time at 90 Hz, and 0.3 of each bay's column reactions pass between storeys, taken from the previous tick so the loop gain stays below 1. So a fully changed Matron can stamp a deck into a bounce. Above 500 m the tower sways on apply_wind's two-swell gust signal, so stock rolls and the hook block swings. Coupling the sway into the support velocity under the player waits until the routes above 176 m prove it.
