milestones.title: M1. Her weight in the steel (about 3 days)
milestones.what: Native: the gait clock and footfall events (Floor, Rung, Landing) with force by stage and Turn, decks, carry_m and felt_mps2 with contact, in a ring of 16 with a sequence number, through MatronSnapshot, get_matron_state and get_footfalls. Presentation: presence.gd (native footfalls replace the stride/STEP_M rule; AIR and STEEL paths; the deck_ring clip; the Steel bus at 250-900 Hz; the footfall haptic; the zero-returning camera dip; grit from her floor's underside), her breath by stage held while Peering, the Her bus and the Windup duck. The haptic scheduler (6 pulses a second at most, by priority) and the HAND FEEL setting.
milestones.proof: Native SCRAPERX_ONLY=matron-footfalls (new). A still Matron emits none. A pest shuffling 10 m gives 16 +-1 footfalls at 220 x 9.81 x 1.1 N +-1%. Hunting at 6.8 m/s for 3 s gives 10 +-1, not 53. set_stage_for_test gives Dangerous 1.8x and Changed 2.4x; a Turn burst gives 3.0x. Her ladder gives Rung kinds every 0.3 m. With the player on 143 under her post: decks 1, carry_m at least 10x the straight distance, felt between 0.05 and 1.0. On her deck within 3 m felt is 1.0 or more; mid-jump it is 0. Two runs are identical. Also matron, matron-mischief, determinism and save. Touch: touch_matron_act extended. In _act_pest_unseen, 6 or more footfall haptics are counted, with every footfall cue on the Steel bus. In _act_rage_below, dangerous footfalls' felt is above the pest's. Her Peering leaves a breath gap of 2.5 s or more. Her Windup ducks Ambience by 12 dB or more. No 1 s window sends more than 6 pulses. 5 s after she is out of reach, the camera reads exactly EYE_OFFSET and FOV_BASE. The act still ends at the 220 ring with one death.

milestones.title: M2. The tower answers (about 2 days)
milestones.what: LooseStock::tremor on footfalls (100 kg or less, 6 m, nothing from a pest, never held pieces, machine parts or a pest's throwables), the 3 s rattled window kept out of her hearing and cleared on restore. The new stock batch appended last: WorkLamp (light child in stock_view.gd), gas bottles at the rail openings, tube offcuts, bolt buckets, a hard hat and a site radio on the shaft rims. The speed-of-sound delay through _cracks_due, the long-fall whistle and the Shaft reverb bus.
milestones.proof: Native SCRAPERX_ONLY=matron-rattle (new). A toolbox 1.5 m off her path hops (peak upward speed 0.15 m/s or more) when she passes Dangerous, and stays at 0.02 m/s or less when she passes as a Pest. A 160 kg crate and a 600 kg beam move 0 mm. Her rage after a Dangerous pass past chattering stock equals a control run without the stock, and the count of suppressed hits is above 0. Her three throwables stay still while she is a Pest. A tube 0.4 m from 154's rim rolls under the rail into the shaft when she hunts past fully changed, but not when the player sprints past, and its hits on the decks below are ledger hits. A WorkLamp shoved at 1 m/s topples. Two runs are identical. Also stock, magnet, stack (end-of-list offsets updated), save (older saves still load), determinism and matron-mischief. Touch: touch_matron_act ends as before. touch_shaft_drop (new): a drum shoved into the shaft at 154. Each hit's cue starts at distance/343 s, within one frame, after its native hit; Shaft-bus sends are counted; the whistle is counted while it falls.

milestones.title: M3. Your body answers (about 1.5 days)
milestones.what: body_fear.gd with dread from native facts only. The heart (clip 68-155 bpm, double-pulse haptic from dread 0.55), the FOV squeeze, the beat vignette, the Ambience low-pass and trembling hands, all honoring REDUCED MOTION. Native grip_share and tear_share in HandSnapshot and get_hand_state, driving the catch jolt, the grip haptic and the flutter above tear_share 0.5.
milestones.proof: Touch touch_fear (new, from the 154 start). With her a pest 25 m off: dread under 0.25 and no heart cues. Once she hunts to within 5 m: dread above 0.6, 3 or more heart cues, _felt(&"heart") 2 or more, vignette alpha above 0.2, Ambience cutoff under 3 kHz. Rerun with REDUCED MOTION: FOV offset 0 and the vignette still drawn. Native hang group: a still hang reads grip_share 0.15-0.2; a 1 m drop caught peaks above 1.5 and holds; a 6 m drop reaches tear_share 1 and slips, as today. touch_pause and every hold check read exactly EYE_OFFSET and FOV_BASE with her dormant. touch_lethal_feedback, touch_roll_reduced and audio_mix pass.

milestones.title: M4. Dusk to night (about 2.5 days)
milestones.what: STORY time of day (appended index; the hour follows the committed checkpoint's height plus her saved exposure, eased, monotone in a session, the same sky after a load), city glow, the automatic headlamp with its click and with shadows at HIGH and above, beam motes, her eyes' wet highlight and pale glow with exposure, ring_lamps.gd lighting the levels at or below the checkpoint (6 pooled lights), the WorkLamps' light following their bodies (into the shaft too), and pooled sparks with night flicker lights.
milestones.proof: Touch touch_story_time (new): the hour is about 15.0 at grade, 17.4 or later at 154 and 18.4 or later at the 220 ring. It moves at 1 h per real minute or less. The lamp is off at grade and on at 220, and its click is counted. A reload gives the same hour. In touch_matron_act's dangerous section a WorkLamp on 154 topples natively and its light follows the body. Capture look_matron_night: the 220 ring at dusk, her in the beam with eye-shine, the shaft from above with lit rings and a falling lamp. perf_grade and perf_top at LOW stay within the current draw-call budget with the lamp on. A night run at 220 with HIGH shadows is logged against 45 FPS; the Fold 6 numbers come from the owner's own device run (law 29).

milestones.title: M5. Your breath is a sound (about 3 days; changes play)
milestones.what: Native Physiology: oxygen debt from mechanical power; breath events; breath loudness 0.03-0.15 joining matron_loudness; the held breath when crouched and still near her, with a release that grows with the debt; grip pump felt first, with grip scaling behind a CHOSEN flag. audio_director's breath driven by native events. Not saved.
milestones.proof: Native group body (new). A 20 s sprint gives breath loudness 0.10 or more; 30 s crouched and still gives 0.04 or less. A pest passing 6 m from a crouched, panting player turns to them; at 12 m she does not; through a deck, never. A held breath lasts 9 s or less, and a release after a sprint is louder than one after rest. A 30 s dead hang pumps to about 0.5. Also climb, parkour, matron and determinism, with climb, parkour, touch_c4, touch_pipe_gallery and touch_monkey_bars passing before the pump flag is turned on. Touch: touch_matron_act still passes (its crouched beat on 143 is a deck under her, and breath never carries through a deck). touch_matron_hang (new): a hang from the 154 deck's shaft lip while she patrols above. Heart and footfall haptics are counted and one held breath is counted. The climber climbs back up after she passes.

milestones.title: M6. Live steel (about 4 days; when M1 to M2 feel thin)
milestones.what: A StructureField of modal bays (8 per Stack deck, 4 per ring; exact discretization; column transfer from the previous tick's reactions) loaded by her footfalls, the player's footfalls and landings, and ledger hits on decks. It replaces the felt_mps2 formula and the tremor kick, keeping the same bridge fields, so resonance builds under a stamping Matron. Tower sway above 500 m on the gust signal, acting on stock, with creaks. Support-velocity coupling to the player stays off until the routes prove it.
milestones.proof: Native group structure (new). With no load, every bay is still and stays still for 10 s. A dangerous Matron hunting 154's north band raises its rim peak to 3 m/s2 or more, while a player on the opposite band feels 0.3 or less. A 55 kg drum dropped 11 m onto 143 is felt on 154 at 0.1 or more within 3 ticks. Below 220 m the sway is exactly 0. matron-footfalls and matron-rattle pass at their thresholds, as do determinism and save. Touch: touch_matron_act, touch_swing and touch_c6 show no new stumbles.

risks: Footfall rate: copying the presentation's 0.385 m hunting step into the native would give about 17.7 events a second at 6.8 m/s. That means a haptic buzz past the 50 ms coalescing and a vibrating bed of kicks. The cadence clock (3.4 Hz cap) is a design requirement, and matron-footfalls proves it.

Shifting passing tests: kicks move stock that touch_matron_act, matron-mischief, stock, magnet and stack find by place. Mitigations: no kicks from a pest, her throwables excluded while she is a pest, held pieces and machine parts never kicked, new stock appended last. Run matron, matron-mischief and touch_matron_act at every milestone.

Rage feedback loop: without the 3 s rattled window, a toppled bottle 3-6 m from her (past kOwnSoundM 1.5) would feed her rage and she would enrage herself. The window must be cleared on restore, or checkpoint determinism breaks.
The CI camera hold: every new camera term (dip, FOV squeeze, sway) must be native-state-pure or reach exactly zero, and read zero whenever she is dormant, dead or out of reach.

No phone in this container: haptics and the phone-speaker mix are measured, never felt. Android amplitude support varies, vibrate_handheld replaces the previous pulse, and steady pulses drain the battery. Hence the scheduler, the cap of 6 a second, HAND FEEL, and an owner check on the device before tuning.

Phone speakers play almost nothing below 300 Hz, so the through-steel sound must carry its character in 250-1,900 Hz plate modes and bolt chatter, with the haptic carrying the low end. The existing audio_mix step's check above 300 Hz gates it.

Law 26: the decks are static, batched bodies and must not be drawn flexing. The ring, grit, dip and haptics present real native footfalls; the chatter is real Jolt motion; the kick and the later field are declared reduced-order models with native bounds and tests. Night stays presentation-only, so nothing may claim that darkness hides you from her.

Owner decision (not scheduled): light in her sight. Her sight would scale from 9 m by day to 3.5 m in the dark, the headlamp would be a beacon to 40 m, and a two-finger tap would toggle it. It is a real stealth verb, but it moves time of day into the native, needs the law 9 decision on committing the hour with the checkpoint, and changes the balance of her act.

Breath as a sound changes the chase. Its range is kept to 8 m or less on her level and never through a deck, with fast recovery, and the CHOSEN numbers are retuned in the open. Grip pump could fail long hangs (touch_c4, the pipe gallery, the monkey bars), so it stays feel-only until those pass.

Voice rule: her stage breaths, hum and held breath, and the climber's held breath, gasp and strain grunts must be recorded by people. The procedural stand-ins in sound_bank.gd play until recordings exist, with voice/ slots that replace them without code changes. The existing fall voice is TTS and already conflicts with this rule.

Performance on GL Compatibility at Fold 6 class: spot shadows only at HIGH and above, at most 6 pooled lamp lights near the camera, pooled sparks and flicker lights, WorkLamp lights unshadowed with distance fade, checked with perf_grade and perf_top. Only the owner's device run proves the numbers (law 29).

Night must stay readable: the sunset tied to the climb darkens her act. NIGHT_EXPOSURE, the lamp, the lit rings and the city glow are tuned against look captures, and look tests that need a fixed hour set it, as ui_test_chase.gd does. STORY becomes the default for new settings only, as an appended index.
Determinism: std::sin and std::exp in the gait clock, kick hash and field are as elsewhere in the sim. Sameness across ARM and x86 is still not established.
synthesis.wow: At dusk you crouch on the 143 m deck right under her post. The phone thumps softly in your hands, once, twice, and rust sifts down through your headlamp beam from the deck seams above. A lit work lamp by the rail opening on 154 chatters, tips and rolls under the single rail. It falls past you down the shaft, its beam sweeping across each deck it passes, and the clang comes up late from far below. Then the footsteps above you stop. She draws a long breath and holds it, listening, and you hold yours with nothing left but your heartbeat in your palm. You have still not caught your breath from the sprint, and you know she will hear the gasp when it comes.

result.headline: Make her unforgettable first: she follows you through the whole tower, you can knock her down without killing her, and her face and body look like a real old woman. Then the story from the yard to topping out, then the machines and older to-dos, then the phone and the store.

sections.title: 1. She roams the whole tower
sections.why: Your top ask: no 'just her deck'. Today she can hear through all 25 levels she knows, from 11 m to 396 m. In practice she stays on the 154 m deck and the 176 ring. Her only way up is one ladder, and only in her Turn. Her only way down is a line someone has already ridden. A restore always puts her back in her locker. Plan: 'She Knows the Steel'. She uses the tower's own structure (the four corner pipes in the shaft, ladders, columns, lifts, lines). You always hear how she is coming before she gets there, and nothing shows on the screen.

items.title: The corner pipe, first on the phone: she comes down the shaft after you
items.detail: A hand-built slice before the general system. Her ladder becomes two-way. One corner pipe (132 to 154 m) becomes hers: it is 0.7 m thick, too thick for your hands, so it is hers alone. Her hands carry her real 220 kg weight with gravity on. Each stage moves differently: a pest goes feet first and slow, with a breath at every flange. Dangerous, she slides down. Fully changed, she comes head first in jerks. Every handhold knocks and every flange bongs, and the phone pulses as she grips steel you are standing on. A 55 kg drum let go over the rail knocks her off. She slides a storey, slams onto the flange below, alive and angrier, and picks another way. Promise to the player: at least 4 seconds of her sound before she reaches your level, and a knock never kills her. This deliberately changes her first act (a pest can now climb), so the act's touch playthrough is re-staged around the knock, not patched to pass.

items.title: Her map, read from the steel: the whole Stack is hers (11 to 154 m)
items.detail: A bake reads the built world and writes her map as fixed tables: floors, walk lines, ladders, the four pipes (52 storey links), columns and braces, plus the lines and lifts added at runtime. CI checks the map for drift, the same way it checks the world's solids. Building it ahead of time means every phone gets the same map. The hand-made 154 deck and 176 ring keep their posts, catwalk and unrigging. A report lists every level she cannot reach so you can see it. One route search covers the tower. How far she chases a sound depends on her stage (40 s of route as a pest, 150 s dangerous, any distance fully changed), so a quiet climber leaves her behind. This also makes her hearing of the forklift and the crane testable, since they work at or below 58 m.

items.title: Where she comes back after a death, and across a quit and reload
items.detail: Today a death puts her back in her locker, and a reload finds her asleep. That clashes with her worsening all day and with her being loose in the tower. Instead she returns to her last firm footing, searching, with her rage, stage and exposure kept and her tricks forgotten. Never closer than 20 s of route to you. The checkpoint stops renewing only while she sees you or is under 20 s away. Her state joins the save as an optional block, so older saves still load.

items.title: She sees across the shaft, and chooses her way
items.detail: Her sight is no longer limited to her own level: decks block it, the open shaft does not. While searching she goes to the rail and looks up, then down. That is where you see her face three decks below. Heavy hits carry through the frame. If she can reach the end of the climb you are on first, she waits there, silent. If you stand over a ladder's head, she looks up at you and walks off toward a pipe, so you watch her decide. Ties between routes are broken without randomness, so a replay is identical.

items.title: The rings, the outside of the tower, and her weight on the lifts
items.detail: The rings from 176 to 396 m and the decks above become real levels instead of bare loops with no way up. Fully changed, she crawls the outer columns and the inside face of the diagonal bracing, and hangs and drops up to 6.5 m after a look over the edge. She clings to rides. New stock: a steel lid on the hatch in the deck at 77 m. Let it fall and weight it, and she pounds on it from below. No new ladders. A table records what each lift does with her 220 kg aboard, and no lift may leave you with no way on. This is also what opens the second cage at the 176 ring to her (blocked today: it stands 1.09 m off the ring, out of her reach) and the cage after it.

items.title: The whole tower by touch: every pose and sound of her travel
items.detail: The poses: wedged round the pipe, the feet-first and head-first descents, her hand over every edge before her head, the shaft look with her head tipped back too far, the column crawl, the slam, the wrong-limbed rise. Each kind of travel has its own sound and a rhythm that gives away her stage. A whole-tower touch playthrough fails unless each beat really happened in the simulation. Then you play it on the phone.

items.title: She learns the lifts
items.detail: Your decision 9 C. Once she has seen you start a machine with your body this run, she can start it with hers: the lift you sent away comes back with her in it. A restore makes her forget. It also covers the lift she calls when it waits near her level, and riding a line's trolley while frail.

items.title: Tune her rage numbers once she follows you up
items.detail: Her rage gain, cooling and stage thresholds are placeholders. Tune them so a steady climb meets each stage where the story wants it. Each knock and each knockdown also adds rage, so a clumsy fighter makes her worse.

sections.title: 2. Keep her at bay without killing her
sections.why: Your rule: the player is never helpless. Today the only counters are sneaking, decoy crashes, running and the rotten catwalk, and the catwalk kills her. Plan: 'Off Her Feet'. She is a 220 kg body with real balance, and anything moving that hits her hard enough puts her down. Every knockdown buys you seconds and costs you rage. Her hands always catch an edge, so the catwalk stays the one thing that kills her.

items.title: Her balance: a hard enough blow puts her down on the deck
items.detail: A blow is the measured change in her speed, counted only when something was actually moving into her. How much it takes depends on her stance (upright or on all fours) and her stage. A heave fells an upright pest; a drum only staggers a dangerous Matron; fully changed, only real mass fells her. In the half second before her Turn she has no footing, so any blow fells her at every stage. Down, she has no hands, no eyes and no Turn for 4, 2.5 or 1.2 s by stage, and the deck booms. Proof: the ingot dolly shoved into her drops her without a death, and her own hunting, vaults and cage rides never count as blows.

items.title: Throw what you carry: swipe up with a load
items.detail: Today a swipe up while carrying is a plain jump. It becomes a throw from the arms' real energy (a toolbox at about 5.8 m/s, a drum at about 3.3), along your view. The landing is a sound she hears, so a throw past her also works as a decoy. The swipe shows a THROW hint where your thumb goes. Tapping LET GO stays as it is.

items.title: Kick her, and slide under her hands
items.detail: With empty hands and her 1.1 to 2.6 m ahead, the swipe up becomes a kick: a straight trade of momentum, capped so a kick never breaks your arm. Dangerous, she braces against blows she sees coming from the front, so get behind her, go for her legs, or drop something on her. A slide under an upright Matron takes her legs, but sliding into her on all fours runs into her hands, and fully changed that is a death.

items.title: A real body on the floor: lying, crawling out, getting up
items.detail: She lies full length where there is room, or crumples to her knees where there is not, and keeps her 220 kg. Pinned under a crate she crawls out first. For 1.5 s after rising she is braced, so nobody can knock her down again and again. You can jump over her body.

items.title: Over an edge her hands always catch; the high ground
items.detail: Knocked over a rim, she always catches the edge and hauls herself back up (7, 3.5 or 1.5 s by stage). Nothing you do makes her let go. On the ladder, a toolbox let go from the ring above tears her off, and she lands at its foot, down but alive. Adds a toolbox and a drum at the 176 ring's ladder head.

items.title: What she learns, and more mass in the world
items.detail: After two blows in a run, a dangerous Matron sidesteps throws she sees. Once a rolling body has felled her, she dodges the next. Fully changed, she catches what you throw and hurls it back. She forgets all of it on a restore. New stock: a 260 kg block trolley on every stack deck and upper ring, and two free-rolling cable reels.

items.title: The music box comes off
items.detail: A hard knockdown snaps the cord, and the box skitters away, still playing as its spring runs down. A pest or a dangerous Matron goes for it before going for you, and her rage falls fast while it plays near her. Carry it off and she hunts it. Drop it down a deck and she stands at the rail over it, listening. Lose it and her rage never drops back below 0.30. Fully changed, she ignores it.

items.title: The feel, and a touch playthrough of all of it
items.detail: A pulse in the hand scaled by the blow. A short slow-down on a kick or a knockdown before her Turn (off under REDUCED MOTION). Three lines from Walt ('She's sick, Navarro. Don't hurt her, just keep her off you.'). A new playthrough, by touch, through all three stages, fails if any beat is missing. Keep the kicking brief and rare, so it reads as horror, not an action hero.

items.title: Can anything but the rotten catwalk kill her?
items.detail: Still open from the spine: can the harpoon kill her, or only knock her off the steel? Recommended: keep the catwalk as her one death, and make the harpoon knock her off. That matches 'keep her at bay, never dead'.

sections.title: 3. Her face and whole figure: a real old woman, deeply wrong
sections.why: Your ask: as real as possible, uncanny, adult-scary, not Halloween; 'too thin', no red skin. She gets the elite graphics tier. Today her head is a sphere pushed into shape with glowing amber eyes and comb teeth, on a body made of simple shapes. Plan: 'Eye Contact'. Where her eyes look is where she really looks, so if you can see her eyes, she can see you.

items.title: A real old woman's face, built here from free (CC0) human-model data
items.detail: A prototype head already renders in Godot on the phone's renderer: an aged head from MakeHuman, free to use, with an uneven half-blink, an open jaw and neck cords. Next: a pinned, repeatable build tool (no Blender needed) that makes the head and neck, facial shapes that can move (blinks, lips, jaw, smile, nostrils), baked wrinkles and pores, pale thin skin, her own brown teeth and a too-white denture, lashes, hair and a white first-aid cap. Skin and eye shaders: light glows through ears and eyelids, and the eyes are wet. The glowing eyes, comb teeth and red skin tint go. The face loads at runtime, because CI has no import step. Add a licenses line for MakeHuman.

items.title: Her whole figure to match: a real body, not too thin
items.detail: Your 2026-10-19 late row: her whole figure, not only the face. A real head on today's body of simple shapes would look cheaply wrong. Use the same MakeHuman base body, with skin on her hands and forearms, a stooped old woman's frame and weight, and clothes that move. Keep every pose she has today (shuffle, scuttle on all fours, the Turn's reversed joints).

items.title: Where she looks belongs to the simulation
items.detail: Today the drawing turns her head toward you whether or not she sees you. The simulation should choose her gaze (you, a sound she heard, her lead, her route), with a neck that eases into each turn and eye jumps at real speed. Her eyes only meet yours when she really sees you. Her chase does not change in this step.

items.title: Alive, and wrong
items.detail: A faint tremor. Breath that moves her chest, nostrils and lips. Dead still when she holds her breath to listen. As a pest, a kind smile that never reaches her eyes; dangerous, white above the iris; fully changed, a dropped denture and a drifting eye. Her exposure shows on one side only, in muted color (dusky, waxy, then grey-violet and sunken), never red and never gore, at most a quarter of her face. Hair falls out in clumps you find on the rails. At the burst the work bulb swings on its cord, so she is lit, then dark, then lit again a little closer. In the dark you see only two wet glints, not glowing eyes.

items.title: Her eyes are her sight
items.detail: She sees from her eyes, with a real field of view. Each blink blinds her for about a third of a second. She stares without blinking until a tear runs, then blinks late on the left side, and that moment is yours to run in. Holding her breath, she hears more; panting, less. This changes the chase and needs retuning, so it comes after the gaze step.

items.title: A blow to her head knocks her gaze off you
items.detail: Something dropped or swung into her head turns it and makes her blink. She loses you for half a second and a bruise forms. This fits with keeping her at bay.

items.title: The first-aider's check when she kills you
items.detail: Fully changed, her catch kills. The view stays in your dead eyes with no shake. She leans in, clicks on her penlight, checks your left pupil and then your right, smiles at one corner and whispers 'Open your eyes for me.' At most 3.2 s, a tap skips it, and it shortens after the second time. A heartbeat in your palm while she sees you close.

items.title: Fits the phone
items.detail: The full head only within about 10 m, a simpler one out to 30 m. At most about 14 thousand triangles and 8 draw calls up close. A LOW preset halves the textures. A budget scenario measures it here. Only your phone can prove 45 frames a second.

sections.title: 4. Feel the climb: immersed and engulfed
sections.why: Your ask that the player feel the climb in their body. Plan: 'Through the Steel'. The tower is one body of steel and she is in it with you: her steps come through the phone, stock walks on the plates, night falls as you climb, and your own breath is a sound she can hear.

items.title: Her weight in the steel: her footfalls and breathing by stage
items.detail: The simulation fires her footfalls at a real walking rhythm by speed and stage (at most 3.4 a second, not today's 17). Each step's force and how far it carries through the decks are computed. The phone thumps with her steps from a deck above or below, a 'dunk' of steel plate sounds through the steel, and rust sifts down from the seams over her feet. Her breath changes by stage (tired, ragged, clicking with silences), and she holds it to listen. That closes the open item on her breathing and footfalls. The world's sound drops away in the instant before her Turn. A budget for the phone's one vibration motor, plus a HAND FEEL setting.

items.title: The tower answers her: stock that walks, lamps that fall
items.detail: Under a dangerous Matron's steps, light stock hops and walks. A pest moves nothing, so her stage shows in the stock. New stock, added freely: work lamps that are real bodies with real light (one rolls under the single shaft rail and falls, its beam sweeping each deck), gas bottles by the rail openings, tube offcuts that roll, bolt buckets, and the crew's hard hat and site radio. Distant crashes arrive late at the speed of sound, a whistle follows a long fall, and the open shaft has its own echo.

items.title: Your body answers: heartbeat, narrowing view, grip
items.detail: Dread is computed from real facts (her distance through the steel, her state, a drop under you). From it: your heartbeat in your palm, a slight narrowing of the view, a vignette that beats, the world's sound closing in, and shaking hands. It all returns exactly to rest when she is gone. Your grip load becomes real numbers: a catch jolts, and a flutter warns that your fingers are going.

items.title: Dusk to night as you climb
items.detail: The hour follows your saved height and her exposure: 3 pm at the ground, 5:30 pm at her deck, full night through the middle bands, first light as you top out. A load gives the same sky. A helmet lamp clicks on by itself at dusk. The rings you climbed stay lit beneath you, with city glow on the horizon and sparks from heavy hits. This is the story's 'readable night' and it gives the foreman's 'I can see your lamp'.

items.title: Your breath is a sound she hears
items.detail: Effort builds an oxygen debt. Your breathing is a real sound out to about 8 m on her level, never through a deck. Crouched and still near her, you hold your breath for up to 9 s, and after a sprint the release is a gasp she can hear. Forearms pump on long hangs. Lower grip from tired forearms stays off until the hanging routes pass with it on. This changes play.

items.title: Live steel and tower sway
items.detail: Bays of deck that bounce for real under a stamping Matron and pass that bounce between storeys. Above 500 m the tower sways in the gusts, so stock rolls and the hook block swings, with steel creaking. Do this when the simpler version of her weight in the steel feels thin.

items.title: Smooth rides on any phone screen
items.detail: Machines are drawn without smoothing while the camera is smoothed, so rides judder. The simulation already provides an in-between position that no Godot script reads yet. Use it, then add bob and lean from motion relative to what you ride.

items.title: Does darkness hide you from her?
items.detail: Not scheduled. Her sight would shrink from 9 m by day to 3.5 m in the dark, and your lamp would be a beacon out to 40 m, with a gesture to switch it. It is a real stealth move, but it puts time of day into the simulation and changes her act. Until you choose it, night stays a look only and does not hide you.

sections.title: 5. More of her: mischief and hands
sections.why: Owner asks from 2026-10-19 that are still open, next to her reach.

items.title: She wrecks your work: shoves your placed stock off edges, resets or jams your machines
items.detail: More of it the higher her stage: she knocks the float lift's spool out of its gap and jams the door lift in the wet band. Today she only takes, throws and hoards stock and unhooks the cage rope, and only as a pest.

items.title: Her shove while you hang from a ledge or hold a ladder
items.detail: Untested. Her shove sets your speed against your grip. Build a shove that breaks the grip, and test the case where you are both on one ladder.

items.title: Check that her own throws and drops never feed her rage
items.detail: Her own sounds are left out of what she hears, but nobody has checked the clank of what she throws or drops.

items.title: Stock for her on every level
items.detail: Only 3 pieces she can throw exist, all on her deck's north side. A roaming Matron needs things to take, throw and knock about everywhere she goes.

sections.title: 6. The story spine: from the yard to topping out
sections.why: Your chosen story: a Kellerworks worker on his own site on a Saturday wakes the Matron, the only way off is up, Walt Brenner is on the radio, fun turns to horror, and it ends with topping out the tower. Built so far: Act 1's core from her deck to the 220 ring. Not started: everything above the 220 ring, plus the opening.

items.title: Real voices for the foreman, the Matron and the crew, made like the fall yells
items.detail: Your 2026-10-19 late rule. Give them their own generator, made the same way as the climber's fall yells (a voice cloned from public-domain recordings, every take checked by a speech checker). This replaces waiting on a recorded person. Walt's lines; her few attendant lines ('There now.' 'Hold still for me.'), a hum, breaths and gasps to replace her synthesized breath and shriek; a worker's startled shout. The climber's fall yells stay exactly as they are.

items.title: Act 1's yard: badge in at the gate, the crane's dropped load
items.detail: Saturday morning, a near-empty yard. He badges in at the turnstile, and the gate log is how the foreman finds out. The overtime crew's last crane lift was dropped in the way, and he clears it with the yard crane to open the way in.

items.title: The overtime crew she got: signs first, bodies higher up
items.detail: Four named workers. In the Counterweight Well: a dropped hard hat, blood on a rail, a radio still talking. Then bodies higher up. Walt's fifth line, 'Pete, come in. Pete.', waits on the hard hat. Workers and corpses already exist in the code to build on.

items.title: The rest of Walt's radio: furious, then the lifeline, then the cover-up
items.detail: After Act 1's four lines: the first hard hat; the X-ray room, where he admits the cover-up; 'I can see your lamp. Keep going.' at night; 'Set the beam. Finish it for them.' Plus his hints about her stage ('She's quiet. Keep it that way.'), which are the only telling besides reading her yourself, never a meter. The 220 ring line should also mention the canopy and the crew's last beam.

items.title: The harpoon, found around Midstack
items.detail: A line-throwing gun built on the grappling hook's real rope and bite. It gives you the high ground against her for the last stretch.

items.title: Set-pieces: the X-ray room, the scaffold she tears loose, the cloud break at dusk
items.detail: The Plate Shop's weld X-ray room, told by the place alone, where the lost source came from. A scaffold she tears loose under you at 462 to 484 m. The cloud break at dusk on the Facade Crane Stack's first ride. A forklift on a ring that lays a beam across a gap. Each one is L.

items.title: The yard crane, forklifts and hook become part of the main climb
items.detail: All three are built, but the route does not need any of them yet. The hook is still a side toy at the 220 ring, and the forklifts only reach the 11 m and 44 m decks. The slingshot stays side fun.

items.title: The ending: seat the crew's last beam, top out, fly home
items.detail: At night, as you seat the last beam with the derrick, she comes over the edge. The flag goes up and the foreman goes quiet. Then off the runway arm, the canopy opens, and you fly 800 m home to the yard as the credits roll. Built: the derrick, the summit, the beacon, the runway arm, the canopy.

items.title: Spine decisions waiting on you
items.detail: (1) The crane's first job: clear the dropped load, or lift you to the 44 m dock? (2) Does the summit searchlight stay beside the last beam? (3) After topping out, the flight home, or end at the beam? (4) At 462 to 484 m, the scaffold she tears loose or the gravity balance machine? (5) Names: Eli Navarro, Ruth Hale (the Matron) and Walt Brenner. Walt is in use; the other two are not confirmed.

items.title: How she came to carry the source, told by places
items.detail: The pellet in her right breast pocket, the lost weld-inspection source, Ruth Hale's name. None of it is told anywhere yet. Her one-sided exposure on the right fits it.

sections.title: 7. The machines and older to-dos
sections.why: Your rule 11: no new ladders on the route and no lift started by pulling something. Every machine is its own physical experience, and a spent or wrecked machine must still leave some way to fix it or go on.

items.title: Each lift its own start: the wet band's door lift and hose lift next, then the eight above them
items.detail: Done: the first three lifts (the rider's weight, a shove, an iron pig dropped into the pan), the float lift at 220 m (its own spool) and one Midstack lift. Still started by the spent hanging handle: the door lift and hose lift at Wet Isolation, three in the Plate Shop, three on the Facade Crane Stack, and two in Midstack. Each needs a different physical start.

items.title: Replace the climbs' ladders, one at a time
items.detail: Rule 11. Start above the 264 ring with the next machine.

items.title: Motor rides: the cascade mast, barrel helix, crown gondola and rack climber
items.detail: Decision 4. These are still board, press RAISE, wait. Recommended A: rework them so you power them, like the hand-hauled pitman lift (the rack climber with a hand crank).

items.title: The governors on every lift below 640 m
items.detail: These lifts arrive on the kit's brake-only governor, not their own shaped drives. Keep it as a visible brake, or re-derive the drives without it?

items.title: Platforms that dip under your steps
items.detail: Decision 5. It broke the derrick's cradle ride and was taken out. It can come back only with a latch at the lower receiver. Recommended A: leave it out for now.

items.title: Grab the machines' real controls
items.detail: For example, grab the forklift's real lift lever and the forks rise. Judged feasible: about 5 for the forklift alone, about 8 for every machine. Asked 2026-10-17, not scheduled.

items.title: Every machine fixable or gone on from, with death-and-restore proof
items.detail: A proof for every machine that dying mid-ride and restoring works, and the incline, wheel and tram exits joined to the next stage.

items.title: The backup route: plain stairs past each stage
items.detail: Rule 8: stairs and easy paths are only the backup, slower way. None is built from 0 to 221 m or above. No new ladders in it.

items.title: The swing ride is struck by a ram, not pumped by the rider
items.detail: The rider's own pumping does not build the swing up to the 242 ring.

items.title: Small machine leftovers
items.detail: The pitman lift's full-height call and brake release were never run. One of nine standing spots in the 662 m cage snags 0.8 m short (still climbable). Take a closer look at the stone wheel's stream, its pile and the skip pouring. The crane's plate clamp waits for thin plates in a rack, which can now be added as stock. Try the forklift's forks under the bottom layer of beams. A forklift landed at full speed by the crane rests 1 m further south.

sections.title: 8. Movement, world and look
sections.why: Older to-dos for the parkour and the world. Graphics depth by importance: she gets the elite tier, ordinary things do not get the same focus.

items.title: Put the wall-run and brachiation in the tower
items.detail: Pipe-to-pipe swings are in the C7 galleries. The wall-run and wall-run chains exist only on the proving ground.

items.title: Spots where moving stock opens a way up
items.detail: Stock is everywhere (317 pieces), but no spot is designed where moving it opens a route.

items.title: Band identities beyond sound; sheltered and exposed choices; consequences that carry over
items.detail: Only Wet Isolation (drawn wet) and the Plate Shop (welders) look like themselves. C7 is the only exposed alternative route. Nothing from one encounter carries into the next yet.

items.title: The look pass: grime, rust and wear; better first-person hands
items.detail: One industrial surface shader (grime under decks, rust streaks, edge wear), thick sagging ropes, lamps on the machines, lit windows, moving cloth, steam you can see from the start. The first-person hands are still crude shapes. Your art-direction decision (D10) is open.

items.title: Movement gaps
items.detail: Grip from real surface friction (wet footing broke the 220 ring's spool carry and was taken out), and from a moving support's load. Footing that rotates under a beam. A roll blocked mid-lane. A machine part hitting a rider. The slide on a slope. Carrying a wide load up a step. Ledge probes that would let you climb a worker. Spotting a cat-leap lip before the jump. The quarter turn, the turn off a wall climb, and the wall-run round a corner.

items.title: Mantle speed
items.detail: Decision 2: keep mantles fast (under half a second, recommended) or make them realistic (about twice as long).

items.title: Pressure ideas
items.detail: Pick any: gust fronts above 400 m with a streak of mist before each gust (ranked first by the research), the falling walkway, the drum run, sliding down wreckage to a lower ring, roping down a wall on the hook's line.

items.title: Time trials against an exact ghost of your best run, and shortcuts the physics allows
items.detail: The simulation is deterministic, so the ghost is exact. Probe every bypass and time it against the route, with no fake walls (your R7 ruling). A summit register serves as the site logbook.

items.title: Music that turns from fun to horror
items.detail: No music exists. Your music decision (D11) is open, and the release plan says not to ship a paid game without it.

items.title: Every machine heard from its own parts
items.detail: The forklift and the yard crane sound from their real state. The other machines still share one generic groan, creak and clunk.

sections.title: 9. Housekeeping
sections.why: Keep the one branch green and the docs telling the truth.

items.title: CI green on ScraperX-Claude
items.detail: Local and remote match at 7bb1e47. The last finished run (the act's stage screenshots aimed at her head) failed. Three newer runs are still going, including the one that takes the pad and keyboard playthroughs out of CI. Confirm one goes green, which also confirms CI on the one-run climb from the ground to 803.5 m.

items.title: One branch: delete the old side branches
items.detail: The 'stage-d-spool-start-wip' side branch is superseded and can be deleted. Three other old branches are still on GitHub (ccr-eaa1e144-8bf0c0, claude/android-game-dev-continue-m045pq, claude/ecstatic-sagan-2kvjwl). Confirm before they go.

items.title: Bring the docs up to date
items.detail: The start file still describes a 1,600 m tower with no story, an old frontier, a CI result from 10-15, 'one open ticket', and the 'climb ends at the 221 m ring' row. It also points to a plan of action that this plan now fills. The progress log's phase table and frontier are stale. Coyote time and the jump buffer are built, and two decision numbers are cited wrong. The ascent plan and move set have stale passages. The handoff doc still says 'nothing is built', lists old process rules, and calls machine starts rage events, though you settled that only sound feeds her rage. Plus ledger bookkeeping (WO-001, AS-005, AS-013 to 015).

items.title: Check every on-screen readout against the no-labels rule
items.detail: The toolbox's name is off. Still to check: 'PIPE SPOOL', the bucket fill readout, 'HOLDING 2.0 T OF 5.0 T', 'TOO HEAVY', and the release plan's proposed ride readout.

items.title: Test gaps
items.detail: One full run through the swing branch (220 ring, swing, C6, mast, pitman, helix into the Plate Shop). No proof covers the gulls. No scenario climbs the yard's containers. No rope machine has been ridden by hand since the rope fix.

items.title: This plan of action
items.detail: Every directive you gave and everything left from before, in one prioritized, color-coded list.

sections.title: 10. The phone and the store
sections.why: It ships on a phone, played by touch. Some of it only your device can prove.

items.title: First recorded run on your phone, and the feel checks
items.detail: Needs your Fold. Frame rate (the target is 45 sustained), the screen, the clouds' overdraw and whether the pine-tree shapes are gone. Haptics felt in the hand. The mix through a speaker. The incline's hop-on brake. Whether the 53 s pitman haul is too long. Whether C7's gusts read before a leap. The jump buffer, launch shot and gestures in hand.

items.title: Device hardening
items.detail: An in-game performance log, a 60-minute soak test, folding the phone mid-ride, the app killed in the background, quality tiers. Plus the same result on the phone's ARM chip: an arm64 CI run and a world hash to compare.

items.title: Updates never cost a climb
items.detail: Today a build that changes the order of bodies refuses older saves once. This has to be fixed before any public release.

items.title: Teach the moves beyond walking to the first machine
items.detail: The painted yard walkway, captions, voice slider and route hint exist. Teach the later moves without labels.

items.title: Store-ready build
items.detail: Only you can add the release key to GitHub secrets (decision 6). Then the release build under the final store identity, Play App Signing, native crash symbols and credits.

items.title: Store compliance and clearances
items.detail: Privacy policy, Data safety, an IARC 16+ rating with strong language, the listing, trailer and a closed test. Trademark searches for the title and 'Kellerworks'. Licenses for the voice model and the fall-scream clip. A MakeHuman line. Replace the sky's noise hash.

items.title: Your product calls
items.detail: Store name (the app id stays com.cory.scraperx.claude), price, rating, whether the code and the hourly test download are public, the lowest device and renderer you support, credits, and the launcher icon (a placeholder for now).

sections.title: 11. Finished recently, worth a look
sections.why: Built in the last few days. Worth seeing before the next push.

items.title: Her first act, played by touch from her deck to the 220 ring
items.detail: She wakes, makes mischief, moves up and down through her stages, shoves you at the shaft, kills you, chases you up the ladder, and you escape to 220. The playthrough fails if any beat is missing, and its screenshots now replay the same run frame for frame.

items.title: Her rage and three stages, moved by sound alone
items.detail: One hidden number fed only by sound at her ear moves her both ways through pest, dangerous and fully changed, with no floor. The music box runs fast when she is dangerous and warps when she is fully changed.

items.title: Her hands by stage, her mischief, and bumping into her is not a death
items.detail: A pest shoves you away and takes, throws or hoards your stock. Dangerous, she shoves you at the shaft's rim. Fully changed, her catch kills. Running into her body is never a death.

items.title: Walt Brenner's first four radio lines, and the story spine approved
items.detail: Set off by places and events, with a squelch and a click, shown as captions.

items.title: Lifts started their own way: the iron pig, the float lift's spool
items.detail: A 50 kg pig let go into the pan trips the third lift's brake. The float lift's spool, carried into its gap, opens the couplings. No pulled handles.

items.title: Touch only, for good; no label on every object
items.detail: The 22 pad and keyboard playthroughs are out of CI. The Action button's verb is enough, and the toolbox's name is off.

working_rules: One GitHub branch: ScraperX-Claude (IssisX/ScraperX). A side branch or clone only when truly needed. Never write to main, and no pull requests unless asked. Push at will.
Run workflows freely and on your own, including complex multi-agent ones. You have every permission: decide, act and report.

Full test runs only when warranted: locally, run only the native groups and touch scenarios a change touches. Run the full native suite only when a change reaches widely (body order, world solids, shared physics or tuning, save layout) and CI is not about to run it. Never replay CI's list locally; CI plays everything on every push.
Touch only, now and forever: no mouse, keyboard or gamepad work. The phone is the target.
No on-screen label for every object: the Action button's verb (PICK UP, LET GO) is enough in most cases.
American spelling everywhere: chat, commits, comments and docs.
Plain words: name things by what they are (the float lift at 220 m), not by internal labels.
Wow-factor first: extraordinary, immersive moments. Never shortcut to a weaker result. Prototype fast with anything available, and help develop the game, not just carry out orders.
Graphics depth by importance: the Matron gets the elite tier, and ordinary things like yard stock do not.
Spend effort on what the player sees and feels, not on invisible detail.
A causal physics world: things move when hit. The parachute is the way back from anywhere. A wrecked or spent machine must still leave a way to fix it or go on.
No new ladders on the route and no lift started by pulling something (rule 11). Nothing repetitive.
Machines make sounds; voices are people's. Character voices are made the way the climber's fall yells were, with their own generator, and the fall yells themselves are left alone.
Never edit MANIFEST.txt, SHA256SUMS.txt or 01_PRODUCT_AUTHORITY/00_GOVERNING_LAWS.md. Never change the app id (com.cory.scraperx.claude), keys or repo visibility.
Give every time in US Central.
Horror, violence and weapons are welcome; no softening or lecturing.
